items.title: Faxes, phones and Bluetooth: Microsoft outage forces businesses to find fixes
items.description: Old-school technology including telephones, faxes and Bluetooth limited the damage for some people on Friday as a worldwide outage of Microsoft’s Outlook left millions without email. The prolonged disruption, which also hit Microsoft Teams and Copilot, affected some of the world’s biggest institutions, from bankers and traders to shipping firms. While most reported their core systems were still running, trading and administrative work slowed in places in the latest reminder of how much of the world’s commerce, public services and communications run on a handful of technology providers. “The pressure is mounting to invest in contingency plans and test whether those backups actually work when needed,” said PP Foresight analyst Paolo Pescatore, adding that firms needed multiple providers for key services like communication and data storage. Microsoft, which says on its website that more than 430 million people use its 365 services, blamed server problems and said it was not aware of any malicious activity. The disruption comes weeks after attacks on the industrial systems that keep supermarket food cold and shows how a single point of failure , whether a technical fault, cyberattack or even an extreme weather event, can disrupt everyday business. In its latest update on Friday, Microsoft said it was seeing signs of stabilisation after implementing fixes more broadly to attain a persistent recovery of services. European exchange operator Euronext, which runs bourses in Paris, Brussels, Lisbon, Amsterdam, Oslo, Athens and Milan, told listed companies to pick up the phone. “We have ensured that the team has sufficient capacity to manage the situation and handle the additional workload,” a spokesperson said, adding that Euronext was verifying the identity of callers to protect confidentiality and integrity. Aviva, which reported earnings on Friday, said it had put backup plans in place, including sending out alternative phone numbers for earnings calls and using Bluetooth to transfer recordings because email was down. The British insurer tested a similar-scale outage of its most critical technology systems about two weeks ago, CEO Amanda Blanc told Reuters. Shipping group Maersk asked customers to call with anything urgent and urged them to verify any unexpected communications about the outage with their local representative. Fax machines return in Taipei In Taiwan, the outage disrupted fund management at securities firms, life insurers and investment trust companies, people familiar with the situation said. At another financial firm, trades such as purchases and sales of short-term bills, which are normally confirmed by email, had to be confirmed by fax instead, one of the people said. Foreign banks and financial institutions in Taiwan were hit especially hard, a trader said, because much of their data is emailed to overseas headquarters through Microsoft’s systems. In Britain, HSBC and Barclays activated internal incident teams to assess the impact, people within the banks told Reuters . While email systems were down, most client services were unaffected. HSBC reminded staff not to use unauthorised channels such as personal email or WhatsApp to get around the outage, one said. Two trading professionals said they observed lower trading volumes in some markets on Friday that they attributed to difficulties in executing trades. Caitlin Egen of Control Risks said that big global firms usually had contingency plans, but when key services went down abruptly it was still a “wake-up call”. “For a lot of businesses this morning, it’s probably been chaos trying to figure out how to even get in touch with people,” she said.

items.title: What we know about the global Microsoft outage
items.description: A major global Microsoft outage has caused problems, or in some cases disabled entire services, including emails and artificial intelligence products. Microsoft has said the outage was not caused by a cyber-security incident, but efforts to fix the issues have so far been largely unsuccessful. Here’s what we know about the services affected and what went wrong. What happened? Microsoft 365 Services, including Teams, Outlook and Microsoft’s artificial intelligence software Copilot, have been affected by “connectivity problems”. Customers are reporting varying levels of access – many have not been able to send or receive emails, view certain files or details on their calendar apps. Some users have been able to use Teams and are using messaging and online meeting functions without issues. How many people have been affected? More than 430 million people use Microsoft 365 apps, according to Microsoft’s website. The full scale of the outage has not been confirmed, but monitoring website Downdetector had 140,000 people from 74 countries report issues with Outlook on Thursday evening. The real figure affected is likely much higher because Downdetector relies primarily on users self-reporting. Microsoft 365 is also used by companies worldwide and is expected to have a knock-on effect to other services. Tech giants OpenAI and Anthropic have both reported problems as a result of the outage. ChatGPT-maker OpenAI said it was investigating an issue affecting its connections to Microsoft’s services, which has caused some tools to not work as expected. From city governments in the US to Australian spy agencies, disruption across the globe has been widespread. Courts from Los Angeles to Texas warned that communications might be delayed. In Canada, the public broadcaster CBC reported that a healthcare network running several hospitals in Toronto was experiencing email issues, but that patient care was not affected. The government of Japan also said its shared IT platform had been disrupted. Across the UK, GP surgeries, pharmacies, police and schools have been affected by the outage. Some GP surgeries have urged patients not to submit messages via their website while the problem remains, while several large police forces are urging members of the public to call if they want to make a report. What has Microsoft said? Microsoft has ruled out a cyber-attack and attributed the ongoing outage to “elevated load” on its infrastructure. The term refers to when servers are handling a much higher volume of stress than they usually do. In the case of the Microsoft outage, a large number of servers became “unexpectedly unavailable”, the company said, which sent added traffic to remaining servers, straining these. On Friday afternoon, Microsoft said it had seen “encouraging recovery progress” in Europe and improvement in North America. The company added it is focused on “addressing the remaining areas of disruption” and warned, “some users may still experience intermittent issues as recovery actions continue”. In an earlier statement, the tech giant had said that its attempted fixes were “not taking as expected”. Why has it taken so long to fix? Although email service Outlook appears to be resuming for some, the outage has so far lasted for more than 20 hours – in outage terms that is considered a long time. Prof James Ferryman from the University of Reading’s Department of Computer Science said the details the company has disclosed provide some clues. “What Microsoft has told us is that the part of its servers that sets up secure connections is getting swamped, and once that happens the server just stops answering,” he said. “The trouble is that this kind of failure snowballs. “One server falls over, its work gets passed to the next one, and meanwhile huge numbers of phones and laptops keep trying to get back in. “You can’t just turn it all back on at once. You have to bring it back bit by bit.” The challenge is therefore not just fixing the fault, but managing the huge surge of devices trying to reconnect once services start coming back online. Gergely Orosz, a former leading software engineer at several major tech companies including Skype and Uber, said this could be the “most disruptive” business email outage “of all time”. He said it was still difficult to know just how many people have been affected by the disruption, but added he “cannot recall” an outage over business email ever taking this long to return to normal. Australian cyber-security expert Troy Hunt told the BBC the outage could have far-reaching consequences. “Microsoft is a massive part of the internet backbone and reminds us how critical email still is. “Not only does this outage affect many people’s ability to work but also things like the ability to communicate about appointments, purchase things that need verification, create or access accounts and services,” he said.

items.title: ADC to APC: Stop shedding crocodile tears over political violence
items.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA – The African Democratic Congress (ADC) Presidential Campaign Council has accused the All Progressives Congress (APC) of sponsoring attacks on opposition parties across the country, dismissing the ruling party’s condemnation of political violence as an attempt to conceal its alleged complicity. The council said the APC could not condemn attacks on opposition gatherings while allegedly encouraging violence against political opponents, warning that the development threatened democratic freedom and the ability of parties to campaign freely ahead of the 2027 general elections. In a statement signed by its Director of Media and Publicity, Kola Ologbondiyan, the ADC-PCC was reacting to a statement by the APC Presidential Campaign Council condemning attacks on opposition parties during their political gatherings. It challenged the ruling party to take responsibility and call its members to order. “The APC cannot pretend to be a victim of the very violence it has nurtured, funded and unleashed on Nigerians since it came to power. “From Edo to Cross River, from Gombe to Lagos, the pattern is the same: APC thugs disrupt opposition gatherings, attack innocent supporters, destroy campaign materials and then rush to the press to shed crocodile tears,” it said. The council specifically linked the disruption of Thursday’s scheduled town hall meeting of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) in Lagos to what it described as the APC’s established tactics of intimidation and political sabotage. “The disruption of Thursday’s scheduled town hall meeting of the Nigeria Democratic Congress in Lagos bears the unmistakable fingerprints of the APC. “It is the same old script: orchestrate violence, intimidate the opposition, disrupt their activities and then issue public condemnations to cover up,” it alleged. Beyond the Lagos incident, the ADC-PCC accused APC governors of frustrating opposition activities through the denial of rally venues, demolition of opposition offices, physical attacks on party members and destruction of their vehicles. It also alleged that restrictions on party posters, candidates’ billboards and public political activities, alongside the imposition of prohibitive fees, were being used to suffocate opposition campaigns. The council maintained that while opposition parties were engaging Nigerians on hunger, insecurity, unemployment, corruption and governance under President Bola Tinubu, the APC had allegedly resorted to violence because it had little to offer the electorate. Questioning the ruling party’s sudden expression of concern over political violence, the ADC-PCC recalled alleged attacks on its members, including the destruction of billboards, disruption of rallies and physical assaults on supporters. “Where was the APC’s condemnation when our billboards were destroyed, our rallies disrupted and our members brutalised? “Their sudden concern is not about peace; it is about diverting attention from their own atrocities,” it said. The council urged President Tinubu to heed the counsel of elder statesman, Professor Jerry Gana, and ensure that political activities were conducted in an atmosphere of peace, tolerance and democratic freedom. It also disclosed that the ADC was compiling records of alleged attacks on its members and would submit appropriate reports to relevant international judicial and human rights institutions. Reaffirming its commitment to peaceful, issue-based campaigns, the council declared that alleged intimidation and violence would not stop its mobilisation ahead of the 2027 elections. “No amount of APC-sponsored violence will stop Nigerians from voting for competence, integrity and a new beginning in 2027,” it declared. items.title: 10 footballers with the most red cards in football history
items.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Footballers are often praised for keeping their cool when the stakes are high, but some of the game’s most recognisable names have become known for receiving repeated red cards. From tough-tackling defenders to forceful midfielders, their careers have combined success on the pitch with frequent disciplinary woes. Gerardo Bedoya stands clear at the top of the ranking, with 46 red cards during his playing career and recognised by the Guinness World Records. The former Colombia international’s fiery reputation followed him into coaching: in 2016, he was sent off just 21 minutes into his first match as an assistant coach at Santa Fe. Red-card totals can differ between databases because no single global record tracks every player’s dismissals across all competitions. According to a recent ranking by Planet Football, here are the 10 players who have been sent off the most times in football history. Alexis Ruano Delgado — 22 red cards The Spanish centre-back played for Málaga, Getafe, Valencia and Sevilla, among other clubs. He won the Copa del Rey with Valencia in 2008. Rafael Márquez — 22 red cards The Mexican defender played for Barcelona, Monaco and New York Red Bulls, among other clubs, and represented Mexico at five World Cups. Six of his red cards came during his time at Barcelona. Cyril Rool — 22 red cards The French midfielder played in Ligue 1 for clubs including Lens, Bordeaux and Nice. His career, which ran from 1993 to 2010, also included more than 150 yellow cards. Gerardo Torrado — 22 red cards Mexico’s former defensive midfielder earned 144 international caps and played at three World Cups. He spent 11 years at Cruz Azul, where he was sent off 14 times. Paolo Montero — 23 red cards The Uruguayan defender played for Atalanta and Juventus, winning Serie A titles with the Turin club. Sixteen of his 23 dismissals came in Italy’s top flight, where he holds the league record, according to the ranking. Edgar Davids — 25 red cards The Dutch midfielder won the Champions League with Ajax and also played for Juventus and Tottenham. Known for his energetic style, he continued his career with Barnet in England’s lower leagues. Felipe Melo — 26 red cards The Brazilian midfielder and defender played for clubs including Juventus, Inter, Galatasaray, Palmeiras and Fluminense. He retired in 2024, aged 41, after a career spanning more than two decades. Pablo Alfaro — 27 red cards The Spanish centre-back played for Barcelona, Atlético Madrid, Racing Santander and Sevilla. He was part of Barcelona’s 1992–93 La Liga-winning squad and later earned a UEFA Cup winner’s medal with Sevilla. Sergio Ramos — 30 red cards The World Cup winner and former Real Madrid captain is second, with 30 career dismissals. His total includes 26 red cards at Real Madrid and four across spells with Sevilla, Paris Saint-Germain and Monterrey. Gerardo Bedoya — 46 red cards The former Colombian international tops the ranking with 46 dismissals during his playing career. Known for his aggressive approach, Bedoya’s reputation followed him into coaching as he was sent off just 21 minutes into his first match as a Santa Fe assistant in 2016. items.title: Kloto: Une sensibilisation sur la charge mentale et le bien-être des hommes à Tové Ahoundjo
items.description: Kpalimé, 13 nov. (ATOP) –Une rencontre de sensibilisation et de dialogue communautaire sur la charge mentale et le bien-être des hommes et des garçons s’est tenue le jeudi 12 novembre, à Tové Ahoundjo, dans la commune de Kloto 1. Cette initiative s’inscrit dans le cadre de la célébration de la « Journée internationale de l’homme », commémorée chaque 19 novembre. Elle est organisée par le ministère en charge de la Famille avec l’appui de l’association Jeunes volontaires pour l’environnement (JVE) dans la région des Plateaux et de l’association SIBEC dans la région de la Kara. Cette sensibilisation est organisée par la GIZ à travers le projet DeZon. Placée sous le thème « Charge mentale et bien-être des hommes et des garçons », cette rencontre a réuni des hommes de différentes catégories socioprofessionnelles, notamment des leaders religieux, traditionnels et communautaires. L’objectif général de cette activité est de promouvoir la santé et le bien-être des hommes et des garçons à travers un dialogue communautaire inclusif. De façon spécifique, il s’agit de sensibiliser les hommes ainsi que les leaders religieux, traditionnels et communautaires aux enjeux liés à la charge mentale, d’encourager leur implication dans la promotion de la santé, de l’égalité de genre et du bien-être familial, et de créer un cadre d’expression leur permettant de partager librement leurs préoccupations et leurs expériences. La charge mentale désigne l’ensemble des préoccupations, responsabilités et sollicitations permanentes qu’une personne doit gérer au quotidien, souvent de manière invisible. Chez les hommes, elle peut notamment être liée à la pression de subvenir aux besoins de la famille, aux responsabilités professionnelles, aux attentes sociales, à la prise de décisions et à l’obligation de répondre aux exigences de leur entourage. Lorsque ces responsabilités s’accumulent, elles peuvent entraîner du stress, un épuisement psychologique, un repli sur soi et des difficultés relationnelles. Au Togo, ces réalités sont observées aussi bien dans les milieux ruraux qu’urbains, où certaines traditions et attentes sociales entretiennent des conceptions rigides de la virilité. D’où la nécessité de promouvoir une masculinité positive, fondée sur l’écoute, le dialogue, le partage des responsabilités, la solidarité et le respect mutuel. Cette approche concerne également les garçons, appelés à grandir dans un environnement favorable à l’expression de leurs émotions, à la responsabilité et à des relations respectueuses. Au cours des échanges animés par l’agent de développement de l’association Rassemblement des femmes unies pour le développement (RFUD) à Kpalimé, Mme Akofa Akossiwo Lolonyo, a amené les participants à identifier les différentes formes de charge mentale et à réfléchir aux comportements susceptibles d’alourdir le quotidien de leurs proches. L’accent a notamment été mis sur la nécessité pour chacun de prendre conscience de ses responsabilités et de ses attitudes. Les discussions ont également abordé les dimensions physiques, psychologiques et sociales de la santé des hommes et des garçons, ainsi que leur contribution à la cohésion familiale et communautaire. À travers un forum-débat, les participants ont été invités à briser le silence autour de leurs vulnérabilités, à exprimer leurs difficultés et à reconnaître l’importance de demander de l’aide lorsque cela est nécessaire. Les échanges ont ainsi permis de mettre en évidence la nécessité de déconstruire les stéréotypes liés à la masculinité, de favoriser une meilleure répartition des responsabilités au sein des ménages et de promouvoir des comportements responsables et bienveillants dans les familles et les communautés. ATOP/KAT/MD

items.title: NIS moves to prevent foreign interference in 2027 elections
items.description: The Nigeria Immigration Service (NIS) and other stakeholders have convened to strategise measures to prevent interference by foreign elements in the upcoming 2027 general elections. The NIS, the Department of State Services (DSS), the Border Communities Development Agency (BCDA) and other stakeholders convened at a sensitisation workshop at the NIS headquarters on Friday in Abuja. The workshop is themed: “The Role of the Nigeria Immigration Service in Election Monitoring and Management.” Speaking at the workshop, the NIS Comptroller-General, Mrs Kemi Nandap, said that the successful conduct of the upcoming elections required institutional cooperation from all security stakeholders. Nandap, represented by the Deputy Comptroller-General in charge of Visa and Residency, Mrs Franca Nwanneka, said that the deliberation was important as the general election is fast approaching. “Beyond the responsibility of conducting credible elections, there is the equally important task of providing a peaceful and secure environment in which the democratic process can thrive. “Achieving this requires collective vigilance, effective coordination and the commitment of all institutions entrusted with safeguarding our nation,” she said. According to her, the NIS occupied a strategic position in the nation’s security architecture as the agency saddled with the responsibility and mandate of border security and migration management. “We must therefore remain alert to the influx of foreigners, emerging threats, particularly irregular migration and smuggling of migrants. “We must also be on high alert to trafficking in persons and other transnational criminal activities capable of undermining national security,” she said. Nandap also reaffirmed the NIS’ stance as a non-partisan service loyal to the Constitution and the Federal Republic of Nigeria, and warned officers against using official capabilities to participate in politics. She charged officers to demonstrate the highest standards of political neutrality, discipline and respect for the rule of law. The CG charged senior officers, zonal coordinators, comptrollers, and heads of formations to ensure that every command is adequately prepared before, during and after the elections. She emphasised strengthened surveillance, intelligence gathering, effective deployment and close coordination with relevant security agencies as key areas that could facilitate credible elections. “No single agency can address the complex security challenges confronting our nation in isolation. Our collective strength lies in our ability to work together, share timely information and respond decisively to emerging threats. “I look forward to even stronger collaboration as we approach the elections because the task of securing our nation and sustaining public confidence in our institutions is a collective responsibility,” she added. Also speaking, the Director-General of the Department of State Services (DSS), Mr Adeola Ajayi, said that the security of borders and integrity of the migration system had become increasingly critical due to the upcoming elections. Ajayi, represented by Mr Patrick Ikenweiwe, Deputy Director-General of Operations and Intelligence, said that foreign elements would try to exploit such gaps. “Past experiences have shown that electoral periods attract attempts to exploit gaps in the border for movement of illicit arms, machinery, and persons intent on undermining the democratic process. “The NIS therefore stands as the first line of national defence, and its vigilance remains indispensable to a peaceful and credible exercise,” he said. He reaffirmed the DSS’ commitment to deepening collaboration with the NIS through timely intelligence sharing, joint threat assessment and coordinated operations, particularly along our land borders and at entry points. items.title: Barrick Mining expresses interest in mineral processing industries in Karachi, Gwadar
items.description: The delegation from the Barrick Mining Corporation on Friday expressed strong interest in investing in the establishment of mineral processing industries in Karachi and Gwadar. The development came as the delegation, led by Chairman John Thornton, held a meeting with Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif in Islamabad, a statement by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO) said on X. According to the PMO, the visiting delegation described the decision by the prime minister and the government to hold a minerals conference as an important step towards mineral development in Pakistan. “The delegation expressed strong interest in investing in the establishment of mineral processing industries in Karachi and Gwadar,” the statement added. It quoted the premier as saying that Pakistan was a country rich in natural resources and mineral wealth. He said that harnessing these resources to develop the province and improve the prosperity of its people was the government’s top priority. “Major projects such as Reko Diq will create new opportunities for employment, skills development and economic growth for the people of Balochistan,” PM Shehbaz said. Pakistan was committed to putting its vast mineral resources to use and creating new opportunities for global investment, he added. The prime minister further said that the Reko Diq project was an important milestone for investment in Pakistan’s mineral sector and was of key importance to the country’s economic future. “The success of the Reko Diq project will set a benchmark for future mineral investment in Pakistan,” PM Shehbaz said, adding that to develop the mineral sector, the government of Pakistan was creating a favourable environment based on “trade, investment, infrastructure and modern technology”. “The Reko Diq project is an important milestone for investment in Pakistan’s mineral sector, and that its success will also serve as a model for future projects,” he said. During the meeting, the prime minister said that Balochistan was rich in natural resources and mineral wealth and that these resources could be harnessed effectively to develop the province, improve the prosperity of its people and increase employment opportunities. “Ensuring that the people of Balochistan directly share in the benefits of mineral projects, creating employment and skills development opportunities for local young people, and developing surrounding communities are among the government’s priorities.” The prime minister also welcomed Barrick Mining Corporation’s participation in the Pakistan Minerals Investment Forum 2026, the statement said. The meeting also discussed policy, regulatory and infrastructure frameworks conducive to the mineral sector in Pakistan, the statement said. It added that the prime minister also expressed a desire to draw on Barrick’s expertise and experience to develop Pakistan’s mineral sector beyond Reko Diq. The Reko Diq mine, one of the world’s largest underdeveloped copper-gold deposits, is hoped to generate $70bn in free cash flow and $90bn in operating cash flow. Canadian mining titan Barrick Mining (formerly Gold) Corporation and the federal and Balochistan governments own the project jointly. According to government sources and industry insider s, production at the Reko Diq copper-gold project could be delayed by two years to 2030, pending improved security in Balochistan and de-escalation in the Middle East crisis. Another delegation meets PM Shehbaz Separately, Ivanhoe Mines’ founder and executive co-chairman Robert Friedland also met with the premier, with the latter asserting that Pakistan was rich in mineral resources and that the government was committed to working with global partners to harness the country’s vast reserves of copper, gold and other critical minerals. According to a statement by the PMO, designating Pakistan a “priority destination” for mineral investment reflects growing confidence among global investors in the country mineral potential and investment climate. PM Shehbaz also welcomed Ivanhoe Mines’ interest in Pakistan and its cooperation with local partners. Furthermore, per the statement, the PM said the exchange of MoUs at the Pakistan Minerals Investment Forum was a “welcome” development. “Creating a conducive environment for investment in the minerals sector is among the government’s priorities. Ivanhoe Mines will be provided full facilitation through the Special Investment Facilitation Council,” the statement read. The delegation also praised the premier’s leadership and efforts to promote regional peace and stability as well as economic reforms, according to the statement. It quoted the premier as saying that Pakistan has “vast” reserves of copper, gold and critical minerals, “which could be harnessed to boost the national economy and improve public prosperity”. The meeting was attended by Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar, federal Ministers Muhammad Aurangzeb and Ali Pervaiz Malik, Special Assistants Tariq Fatemi and Lieutenant General (Retd.) Muhammad Zafar Iqbal, and other senior officials.

items.title: Ghanaian authors take Ghana’s literary heritage to GEMS Millennium School in Sharjah
items.description: Three Ghanaian authors have engaged students at GEMS Millennium School in Sharjah, United Arab Emirates, to promote Ghanaian literature and encourage reading and creative writing. The engagement brought together Ghanaian authors Oswald Okaitei, Ruby Goka and Elizabeth-Irene Baitie and students of the school for an interactive session exploring Ghanaian writing, literature and storytelling while fostering cross-cultural learning and intellectual exchange. As part of their contribution to promoting reading and literary development, the authors donated books written by themselves and other Ghanaian authors to the school’s library. Additional copies were presented to some students to encourage reading, nurture creativity and deepen their appreciation of literature. Describing the encounter as intriguing and rewarding, Okaitei highlighted the reciprocal nature of the engagement, noting that beyond sharing their experiences and perspectives as Ghanaian writers, the authors also had the opportunity to learn from the students’ creativity, curiosity and literary interests. “It was a give-and-take experience, with quite a lot of learning curves for me,” he reflected. One of the most remarkable aspects of the encounter was the impressive literary accomplishments of some of the students. Several were already published authors, with some having written as many as six books while still in their teenage years. Their achievements offered an inspiring glimpse into the emerging generation of young writers and storytellers. The initiative provided an important platform for showcasing Ghana’s literary identity beyond its borders, reaffirming the role of books and storytelling as instruments of cultural diplomacy, education and tourism promotion. For Okaitei, the opportunity to represent Ghana on this international platform was both a profound pleasure and an honour. He acknowledged the Consulate of Ghana in Dubai and the Northern Emirates, together with BOST Energies, for creating the opportunity for the Ghanaian literary delegation to participate in this year’s Sharjah International Book Fair as part of a broader programme of literary and cultural engagements. The school engagement forms part of the wider Black Star Experience agenda, which seeks to project Ghana’s cultural identity, heritage and creative potential to international audiences. Through this initiative, Ghana’s literary heritage is being positioned as an integral component of the country’s tourism and cultural appeal. Books and storytelling offer unique pathways to discovering Ghana’s history, people, traditions, values and contemporary experiences. The engagement also demonstrates the capacity of Ghanaian literature to connect generations and cultures while creating opportunities for international collaboration in education, publishing and the creative industries. By taking Ghanaian stories, literary perspectives and publications into international learning environments, the Ghanaian delegation is extending the reach of the country’s literary heritage and strengthening its presence in the global cultural space. The Black Star Experience is therefore finding expression not only through conventional cultural showcases but also through literary diplomacy, educational engagement and international partnerships. Beyond promoting Ghana as a cultural and tourism destination, the initiative advances an equally important proposition: Ghana is a destination for literary discovery, intellectual exchange and storytelling.

items.title: 2027: Adebutu hails court ruling, says justice has prevailed
items.description: By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta The Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) governorship candidate in Ogun State for the 2027 election, Hon. Oladipupo Adebutu, has hailed the judgment of the Federal High Court, Abuja, directing the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to restore his name to the list of candidates for the forthcoming governorship election within 24 hours. Adebutu described the judgment, delivered by Justice Peter Lifu on Friday, as a victory for justice, the rule of law and democratic principles. Reacting to the ruling in a statement, the PDP chieftain declared: “Justice has prevailed! Relief is here!” He described the judgment as a significant development in the legal battle over his exclusion from INEC’s published list of candidates for the 2027 Ogun State governorship election. Adebutu said he had consistently maintained that his PDP membership, registration and emergence as the party’s governorship candidate were legitimate and in accordance with due process. “From the moment my name was omitted from INEC’s published list, I maintained that the facts surrounding my PDP membership, registration and the process that produced me as the party’s governorship candidate were clear,” he said. According to him, the party remained confident in the strength of its position and resolved to pursue the matter through the appropriate legal channels. He noted that the judgment had reaffirmed the importance of due process, stressing that political and electoral disputes should be determined on their merits rather than on speculation or premature conclusions. Adebutu expressed appreciation to the national leadership of the PDP, particularly Chief Nyesom Wike, whom he described as the party’s national leader, and its National Chairman, Hon. Abdulrahman Mohammed, for their support and confidence throughout the legal proceedings. He also thanked the Ogun State PDP leadership, party members, supporters and residents of the state for their solidarity during the period of uncertainty. “I am equally grateful to the Ogun State PDP leadership, our members, supporters and the good people of Ogun State who remained steadfast. Your patience, encouragement and confidence have been invaluable,” he stated. The governorship candidate also commended the judiciary for its role in upholding justice, emphasising that democratic institutions must remain independent and impartial, irrespective of political interests or affiliations. “Our democratic institutions must remain strong, independent and committed to upholding the law, regardless of political interests or affiliations,” he said. Welcoming the judgment, Adebutu said his focus remained on addressing the developmental challenges confronting Ogun State and engaging residents on practical solutions to improve their welfare. He maintained that his political aspiration went beyond personal ambition or electoral victory, insisting that the ultimate objective was the well-being of the people and their constitutional right to participate in choosing their leaders. “Our mission has always been bigger than an individual or a political contest. It is about the welfare of our people, the progress of our state and the right of every citizen to participate meaningfully in choosing the leadership they desire,” he said. Reaffirming his political slogan, “OGUN FOR OGUN,” Adebutu said it represented his commitment to a people-oriented administration that would prioritise the interests, welfare and development of Ogun State residents. He urged his supporters to remain calm, focused and law-abiding following the court’s decision. “To our supporters, I urge you to remain calm, focused and resolute. Let us continue to conduct ourselves with dignity, respect for the law and an unwavering commitment to democratic values,” he appealed. He added that the development would not distract him from his commitment to the state, declaring: “We have a state to build, a people to serve and a future to secure. Nothing will distract us from that responsibility.” …..Tella: Judgment victory for Ogun people Similarly, the Ogun State Chairman of the PDP, Abayomi Tella, has described the Federal High Court judgment affirming Adebutu’s candidacy for the 2027 governorship election as a victory not only for the party but also for the people of the state. Tella, who spoke in an interview following the judgment, said the ruling had further strengthened his confidence in the judiciary as the last hope of the common man. He said he had never doubted that justice would prevail, maintaining that Nigeria was governed by the rule of law, particularly in matters relating to electoral legislation and the rights of political parties and their candidates. According to him, the judgment would reassure residents who had expressed concern over the PDP’s exclusion from INEC’s published list of candidates. The party chairman reaffirmed the PDP’s determination to participate fully in the 2027 governorship election, declaring that the party remained committed to taking over the leadership of Ogun State. He insisted that the ruling transcended the interests of the PDP, describing it as a victory for democracy and the people of Ogun State. In his judgment, Justice Peter Lifu held that INEC lacked the constitutional and statutory powers to unilaterally disqualify a candidate validly nominated by a political party. The judge also ruled that the commission violated Adebutu’s right to fair hearing by excluding his name from the list of candidates without affording him an opportunity to be heard. Consequently, the court declared the removal of Adebutu’s name unlawful, unconstitutional and of no effect, directing INEC to restore his name to the list within 24 hours. Justice Lifu further held that the authority to disqualify a candidate whose name had been forwarded by a political party resided with the Federal High Court or a State High Court. The judgment followed a suit instituted by the PDP and Adebutu after INEC omitted his name from the final list of candidates published on October 10, 2026. Before determining the substantive issues in the suit, the court dismissed INEC’s preliminary objection challenging the competence of the action. Justice Lifu held that the originating summons was properly signed by a Senior Advocate of Nigeria and contained the names of other lawyers in his law firm, thereby rendering the court process competent. items.title: Décentralisation : Les communes Moyen Mono 1 et Golfe 1 scellent un accord de partenariat
items.description: Tohoun, 13 nov. (ATOP) – Les communes Moyen-Mono 1 et Golfe 1 ont signé, le jeudi 12 novembre à Tohoun, une convention-cadre de partenariat visant à renforcer la coopération entre les deux collectivités territoriales dans des domaines d’intérêt commun. Cet accord a pour objectif de promouvoir le développement local et durable à travers la mutualisation des compétences, des expériences et des ressources, ainsi que la réalisation d’actions conjointes au profit des populations des deux communes. Plusieurs domaines seront pris en compte dans le cadre de cette convention, notamment la culture et le tourisme, l’assainissement et la salubrité publique, la promotion du genre et l’inclusion sociale. Le préfet de Moyen-Mono, Col. Gnakouafré Yao Eindrè, a salué les initiateurs de ce partenariat, soulignant que cette convention constitue une étape importante dans la consolidation de la coopération décentralisée et la promotion de la solidarité entre les collectivités territoriales. Selon lui, le développement local exige une mutualisation des expériences, des compétences, des ressources et des opportunités. Le préfet a invité les signataires à traduire ce partenariat en projets réalistes, structurants et mesurables dans leurs domaines d’intervention respectifs. Le maire de Moyen-Mono 1, Assoè Yaosè, a relevé que cette convention représente une précieuse opportunité pour les deux communes, confrontées à de nombreux défis, notamment en matière de mobilisation des ressources financières. Pour sa part, le maire de Golfe 1, Gomado Koamy Gbloekpo, a indiqué que cette convention-cadre permettra aux deux collectivités de développer des initiatives adaptées aux besoins respectifs de leurs populations. ATOP/TM/JK/BV

items.title: Combien de temps Poutine peut-il encore financer sa guerre ?
items.description: Testez le Grand Continent . Les idées et les analyses qu’on ne trouve nulle part. Mais que vous verrez bientôt partout. Dans votre boîte mail à partir de 8 euros par mois Depuis février 2022, une même question revient régulièrement : combien de temps la Russie peut‑elle encore financer la guerre ? Six mois, un an ? Trois échéances d’épuisement de son fonds souverain ont circulé, de la mi‑2026 à la fin de 2027, mais aucune ne s’est jusqu’ici vérifiée. Si la question est légitime, elle induit pourtant une représentation erronée du problème. L’État russe n’est pas une entreprise à court de liquidités contrainte de déposer le bilan et peut encore soutenir les immenses dépenses que suppose l’invasion de l’Ukraine. Toutefois le coût augmente plus vite que les recettes et la rente pétrolière s’amenuise. Par conséquent, la vraie question est à présent de savoir quels sacrifices le Kremlin devra faire pour continuer à financer son effort de guerre. Dans cette économie au service de la guerre, le principe est que le prélèvement finance une dépense que le régime ne peut ni réduire ni avouer. Lus ligne à ligne, les comptes publics russes permettent cependant de mesurer ce que les communiqués ont pour mission de dissimuler. Nos précédentes analyses consacrées aux frappes ukrainiennes contre Wildberries et contre les centres de données de Yandex montraient comment Kiev s’en prenait à la puissance russe plutôt qu’à sa force. Il nous faut maintenant examiner la cible ultime de cette stratégie d’usure, à savoir les finances de l’État et les réserves accumulées en vue de la guerre de réaffirmation de la puissance russe voulue par Vladimir Poutine. Un fonds à deux poches Commençons par l'objet qui forme l’essentiel du « matelas » constitué par la Russie pour faire face au choc prévisible de l’entrée en guerre, le Fonds national de bien-être (FNB). Créé en 2008 par scission du Fonds de stabilisation, il est principalement alimenté par le surplus de recettes fiscales pétrolières et gazières perçu lorsque le prix du baril dépasse un seuil, fixé par la loi de finances. En clair, si le prix du baril est de 59 dollars, comme en 2026, et qu’il se vend 103 dollars, les recettes fiscales correspondant aux 44 dollars d’écart viennent alimenter le fonds Минфин сформировал расходы бюджета-2027 исходя из нефти по $50 за баррель » (Le ministère des Finances a établi les dépenses du budget 2027 sur la base d’un baril à 50 dollars), The Moscow Times , 22 septembre 2026, d’après Interfax .'> 1 . Qu’en est-il de l’utilisation de l’excédent dégagé ? La vocation officielle du Fonds national de bien-être est double, puisqu'il doit combler le déficit de la caisse des retraites et amortir les cycles des matières premières. Contrairement au fonds souverain norvégien, il ne dispose pas d’un portefeuille diversifié à l’étranger générant des rendements mais se compose principalement d’actifs nationaux ainsi que de quelques réserves en espèces et en métaux précieux. Or, la dédollarisation, décidée en 2021 par anticipation d’un gel des avoirs occidentaux, puis ce gel lui-même en 2022 ont réduit la part mobilisable à deux actifs, le yuan et l’or. C’est là le point décisif pour comprendre comment la Russie a financé le début de sa guerre. Ce fonds se scinde en deux poches, qui ne sont pas de même nature. Une poche liquide rassemble les avoirs en or et en devises étrangères déposés sur les comptes du fonds à la Banque centrale. Elle est mobilisable immédiatement. C'est elle seule qui permet de financer réellement quelque chose. Une autre poche, dite « illiquide » , rassemble des participations dans des entreprises russes, des prêts à des projets d'infrastructure et des actifs gelés depuis 2022. Pour la France : Insee, 27 mars 2026 (64,7 milliards d'euros d'intérêts), et Direction générale du Trésor, 2026 (2,2 % du PIB).'> 32 . Le taux moyen supporté par l'État russe avoisine 8,5 %, contre moins de 2 % pour l'État français. Ce n'est pas le niveau de la dette qui contraint Moscou, c'est son coût. Et les autorités russes elles-mêmes tiennent le seuil de 20 % du PIB comme la limite de la prudence, seuil dont elles s’approcheront à la fin de l'année The Moscow Times , d'après Reuters, 28 septembre 2026.'> 33 . La deuxième raison est que ce chiffre ne mesure qu'une partie de l'endettement de guerre. Le 25 février 2022, au lendemain de l'invasion, la loi n° 29-FZ a imposé aux banques habilitées de consentir aux fournisseurs de l'armée un financement préférentiel aux conditions fixées par le gouvernement, tout en les dispensant de rémunérer les avances que l'État dépose sur leurs comptes 34 . Ce procédé n’est pas nouveau, puisque dès 2010, le Kremlin avait financé une partie du réarmement par des prêts bancaires aux industriels, puis avait dû reprendre les créances irrécouvrables en 2016 et 2017, et de nouveau en 2019 et 2020. Juridiquement, ces dettes sont celles des entreprises. Mais économiquement, ce sont celles de l'État, qui les a déjà remboursées deux fois. Craig Kennedy, ancien vice-président de Bank of America et Merrill Lynch, chercheur au Davis Center de Harvard, en a reconstitué l'ampleur. Entre la mi-2022 et la fin de 2024, la dette des entreprises russes a augmenté de 71 %, soit environ 415 milliards de dollars et il estime que la moitié à 60 % de cette hausse, soit 207 à 249 milliards de dollars, finance des activités liées à la guerre Navigating Russia , Davis Center for Russian and Eurasian Studies, Harvard, 11 janvier 2025 (synthèse) et février 2025 (rapport complet).'> 35 . Rapportés au PIB de 2026, ces prêts représentent 8 à 10 points. Si l'on inclut cette dette hors budget, l'endettement public réel de la Russie se situerait donc entre 25 et 30 % du PIB 36 . La faiblesse de la dette publique russe tient donc moins à la solidité de l’État qu’à la manière dont il finance la guerre, en logeant une partie de son coût dans les bilans bancaires, où il ne se voit pas. Le projet de budget pour 2027, transmis à la Douma fin septembre 2026, confirme l’ancrage durable de l’économie de guerre au détriment des priorités civiles. La défense nationale y reçoit 17 100 milliards de roubles (6,9 % du PIB), soit 2,6 fois plus que la politique sociale, ramenée à 6 600 milliards (2,7 % du PIB). Avec la sécurité intérieure et le maintien de l’ordre (4 200 milliards), le bloc militaire et sécuritaire absorbe 21 300 milliards de roubles, soit 8,6 % du PIB et près de 44 % des dépenses fédérales Who Is Funding Russia’s War in the 2027 Budget ? », Carnegie Endowment , 2 octobre 2026.'> 37 . Pour chaque rouble consacré aux prestations sociales, l’État en prévoit plus de trois pour les armes et le maintien de l’ordre Business Gazeta , « Минфин сделал все, что от него зависело » (Le ministère des Finances a fait tout ce qui dépendait de lui), 2 octobre 2026.'> 38 . Cela ne signifie pas que Moscou ne pourra pas financer le déficit (5 443 milliards de roubles prévus pour 2027, puis 5 120 et 5 245 milliards en 2028 et 2029, soit environ 2 % du PIB chaque année) Правительство внесло в Госдуму проект бюджета на 2027–2029 годы » (Le gouvernement a transmis à la Douma le projet de budget pour 2027-2029), TKS.ru , 1er octobre 2026, d’après le ministère des Finances. Déficits prévus de 5 443 milliards de roubles en 2027 (2,2 % du PIB), 5 120 milliards en 2028 (1,9 %) et 5 245 milliards en 2029 (environ 1,9 %).'> 39 , mais que ce financement devient de plus en plus coûteux, et de plus en plus palpable pour la population. Nous arrivons au bout de cycles de 12 ou 24 mois au cours desquels le Kremlin a sacrifié ses propres politiques publiques et son État-providence pour alimenter son effort de guerre. Le premier millier de milliards redirigé est toujours facile à justifier et relativement indolore, le dixième l'est beaucoup moins. Le coussin est désormais mince. Au 1er octobre 2026, la partie liquide du Fonds national de bien‑être ne représentait plus que 3 800 milliards de roubles, soit moins de trois mois de dépenses de défense au rythme prévu pour 2027, et à peine plus des deux tiers du seul déficit attendu pour 2027. L’année 2027 sera sans aucun doute décisive pour les finances russes, d’autant que les dépenses de défense doivent y augmenter de plus de 30 %. Ce que les comptes disent, et ce qu’ils taisent Si le fonds souverain russe se vide, il ne le fait pas linéairement, à la manière du compte en banque d’un particulier. Depuis 2022, l’État fédéral se comporte plutôt comme un conglomérat déficitaire, qui répartit les pertes entre ses filiales afin de présenter un bilan plus flatteur que la réalité. Ses avoirs liquides se transforment en créances sur des entreprises d’État, son or sort de son périmètre et une partie de sa dette de guerre est inscrite au bilan des banques publiques plutôt qu’au sien. Aucun de ces mouvements ne constitue une faillite, et c’est précisément ce qui les rend commodes pour le régime. Chacun déplace le coût de la guerre vers un lieu où il ne se voit pas encore, mais où il s’accumule. Cette recomposition a donc une limite, que les chiffres de 2027 rendront peut‑être tangible. La réserve liquide ne couvre plus qu’une fraction du déficit annoncé, et chaque rouble supplémentaire devra venir de l’impôt, de l’inflation ou de l’épargne des ménages, c’est‑à‑dire de leviers que la population finit par subir de plein fouet. Les frappes sur les raffineries ont provoqué, à l’été 2026, des pénuries dans presque toutes les régions de Russie et ont accru le coût des compensations versées aux raffineurs. La campagne contre les entrepôts de Wildberries et d’Ozon a affaibli deux fleurons de l’économie russe et ruiné une partie de leurs vendeurs, que l’État a dû soutenir par des reports d’impôts et par l’entrée de VTB au capital de Wildberries. Les frappes contre les centres de données de Yandex, de Sberbank, puis, fin octobre, contre un centre du ministère des Finances hébergeant des registres d’État et des données fiscales, atteignent enfin l’infrastructure numérique dont dépendent les paiements, le commerce et les services publics. Prise isolément, aucune de ces attaques ne menace l’équilibre financier russe. Ensemble, elles transforment une part croissante des destructions en dépenses publiques ou en passifs implicites pour l’État. Préparé de longue date par l’accumulation de réserves et la construction de circuits de contournement, le Kremlin a longtemps pu financer la guerre sans en faire supporter la charge visible à la population. Mais depuis près de cinq ans, la guerre engloutit les ressources qui auraient dû servir à moderniser l’économie et les infrastructures russes, et les réserves qui rendaient ce sacrifice invisible sont en train de s’épuiser. Ce coût différé pourrait alors rattraper les dirigeants russes au moment où ils voudraient accentuer leur pression sur Kiev, alors même que l’offensive s’essouffle. En effet, sur les dix premiers mois de 2026, l’armée russe n’a gagné qu’environ 117 kilomètres carrés nets, selon les données de l’Institute for the Study of War, et elle a même reperdu du terrain en septembre et en octobre. Le 29 octobre 2026, Vladimir Poutine affirmait que l’Occident avait échoué à infliger à la Russie une « défaite stratégique », avant d’avertir qu’une guerre entre la Russie et l’Europe ne connaîtrait « aucun vainqueur » Putin : Russia is prepared for war with Europe », The Telegraph , 29 octobre 2026.'> 40 . Le propos se voulait une démonstration de force. Il trahit pourtant une évolution du discours. Après une invasion censée durer quelques jours, le Kremlin présente le fait ne pas avoir été vaincu comme un succès. C’est peut‑être parce que, financièrement, la Russie est déjà dans une position délicate. La crise n’est pas encore inévitable, mais elle n’aurait plus besoin d’un choc majeur pour éclater. Et elle ne resterait pas confinée aux comptes de la Fédération. En répartissant les pertes entre les banques publiques, les entreprises d’État et le fonds souverain, l’effort de dissimulation a tracé d’avance les voies de la contagion. La crise pourrait ainsi gagner l’ensemble de l’économie, puis l’ordre politique, et jusqu’à l’effort de guerre en Ukraine lui‑même. L’acte final de cette guerre reste donc à écrire. Il pourrait se jouer moins sur le front que dans les comptes, sauf si le chef de l’État russe jugeait plus sûr de modérer ses exigences et d’engager des négociations substantielles, pour « etirer ses gains » avant que la situation ne devienne inextricable. Rien ne l’annonce pour l’heure. L’article Combien de temps Poutine peut-il encore financer sa guerre ? est apparu en premier sur Le Grand Continent .

items.title: Carrick says ‘love never dies’ after Man Utd sacking
items.description: Michael Carrick wished Manchester United “nothing but success” 24 hours after he was sacked, reaffirming his enduring love for the club, who have already appointed Mauricio Pochettino as his replacement. Carrick impressed after taking over as interim boss following Ruben Amorim’s acrimonious exit in January, leading United to Champions League qualification. He was rewarded with a two-year permanent deal, but results have nose-dived in this campaign. The Red Devils are in the Premier League relegation zone after winning just one of their 10 league matches so far. The Old Trafford club named former Tottenham, Chelsea and Paris Saint-Germain boss Pochettino, currently USA head coach, as their new manager on Friday. Despite the downturn this season, Carrick remained popular with supporters in part for his role as a player in multiple triumphs under Alex Ferguson, who retired in 2013. The 45-year-old said his affection remained rock-solid. “I want nothing but success for Manchester United. This club has been such a big part of my life and that will never change,” Carrick wrote in an Instagram post. “I’ll always be proud to have played my part and I’ll always want the very best for it. “I’ll be right there with you from now on, watching from the sidelines, cheering the lads on.” The former England midfielder paid tribute to the fans, his coaching staff and United’s players. “I’ve had the immense privilege of leading Manchester United, the football club that I love,” he wrote. “There are very few who get to live that and feel it, and for that I’m incredibly grateful. With that comes huge responsibility, and to be at Manchester United, you need to understand exactly what that means. “It’s different to anywhere else. Ultimately, you need to push to be the best, but there is a culture, there are values and there are behaviours that you have to live by and respect, which have been built over a long period of time. “It’s a football club that is unique, with substance and history that cannot be ignored. This is what inspired me every single day.” Carrick described United’s fans as a “special, rare breed”. “We’ve had some great times this year and moments we’ll all remember,” he said. “The best thing about being in my position was seeing so many of you lose yourselves in the emotion of those moments, leaving the stadium desperate to come back again next time. “I just wanted to give you something back. That love never dies.” The post Carrick says ‘love never dies’ after Man Utd sacking appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Obi condemns attack on NDC supporters in Lagos, urges peaceful defence of votes
items.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has condemned the attack on the party’s supporters at a town hall meeting in Lagos on Thursday, urging them to remain peaceful while defending their democratic rights. Obi made the call in a statement posted on his X handle on Friday, a day after suspected thugs disrupted the party’s gathering in Oregun, Lagos. He said he had been informed that a group of thugs mobilised to attack participants who arrived early for the meeting, noting that he had travelled to Lagos from Abuja to attend a commendation service for Chief Sir Okey Ezibe before proceeding to join supporters at the town hall meeting. “The political violence being enabled by certain political actors against our supporters is an ill wind that blows no one any good. Anarchy consumes everyone,” he said. “We will remain law-abiding, even in the face of extreme provocation.” Obi said the town hall meeting went ahead despite the disruption and participants raised concerns about reviving the economy, the high cost of living, corruption, insecurity, support for vulnerable citizens and the integrity of elections. He said the first responsibility of any government was to secure the country and unite its people around a shared purpose. He also pledged that his administration would pursue policies to reduce living costs, improve welfare and invest in healthcare and education. On the forthcoming elections, the former Anambra governor said protecting the integrity of the process was a shared responsibility, saying the NDC would deploy agents to polling units to observe and document voting, ward collation and the final declaration of results. “I encouraged our people to eschew violence while remaining peaceful, vigilant, and resolute in defending their democratic rights,” he said. Vanguard reported that suspected political thugs armed with cutlasses, cudgels and stones invaded the Oregun rally on Thursday, attacking supporters and injuring some participants, although Obi was not at the rally when the incident occurred. The post Obi condemns attack on NDC supporters in Lagos, urges peaceful defence of votes appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: JOJ Dakar 2026 : au-delà du sport, des rencontres et des amitiés sans frontières
items.description: Des poignees de main, des eclats de rire, des pas de danse et surtout des amities qui se nouent au-dela des frontieres. a Dakar, les Jeux olympiques de la jeunesse (JOJ) 2026 ne se vivent pas uniquement sur les terrains de competition. Ils sont aussi une formidable aventure humaine, ou Senegalais, benevoles, athletes et visiteurs venus des quatre coins du monde apprennent a se connaître et a vivre ensemble. Malgre les differences de langues et de cultures, un meme esprit les rassemble : celui du partage et de la fraternite. Des langues differentes, mais une meme envie de partager Pour les jeunes athletes, les JOJ sont bien plus qu'une competition sportive. C'est aussi l'occasion de decouvrir d'autres cultures, de nouer des amities et de partager des moments qui depassent les frontieres. Marwane Abba, nageur nigerien, apprecie particulierement cette ambiance de convivialite. « L'ambiance est tres bonne, nous nous entendons parfaitement. Nous arrivons a sortir ensemble et a partager de bons moments. Bref, tout se passe tres bien. En ce qui concerne la communication, personnellement, je parle anglais, ce qui me facilite beaucoup les choses. Pour les langues que nous ne maîtrisons pas, comme le chinois, le russe et bien d'autres, nous utilisons plutot les signes. C'est aussi un langage universel qui nous permet de nous comprendre. Il n'est donc pas vraiment difficile de communiquer entre nous . » Cette facilite a aller vers l'autre se retrouve egalement chez les milliers de benevoles mobilises pour l'evenement. Parmi eux, Bilal Adama Mahamat, benevole tchadien venu de la Republique de Guinee, retient surtout la solidarite et l'entraide qui caracterisent cette experience. « Malgre la diversite, on se soutient tres bien. Meme s'il y a des volontaires qui parlent anglais, si tu es en difficulte, tu leves seulement la main, un volontaire viendra te secourir. J'ai fait des amis ici. Chacun veut rester a cote de toi pour te faire sentir que tu es chez toi . » Une hospitalite qui rappelle la celebre Teranga senegalaise. Pour Yasaint Libabe, Belge d'origine congolaise, selectionne parmi les quelque 6 000 volontaires venus du Senegal et de 90 autres pays, cette ouverture aux autres est justement l'une des grandes richesses d'un evenement international comme les JOJ. « Tous ces gens sont ouverts aux autres. Ils n'ont aucun mal a cotoyer des personnes d'origines differentes. Au contraire, ils veulent apprendre des autres, et c'est toute une richesse », temoigne-t-il. La diversite culturelle, une richesse qui rassemble Au-dela des echanges entre athletes et benevoles, les JOJ sont aussi un espace de decouverte et de rapprochement entre les peuples. Pour Carine Tecla Biaga, Camerounaise, l'esprit olympique repose justement sur cette capacite a rassembler des personnes aux parcours et aux origines differentes. « L'olympisme, ce n'est pas quelque chose qui prone la distinction des pays, des tribus, des pauvres. C'est une rencontre multiculturelle », explique-t-elle. Un sentiment partage par le Senegalais Moussa Moussine, qui souligne egalement l'esprit de solidarite observe jusque dans les gradins. « Meme dans les tribunes, nous etions la pour soutenir les athletes des autres nationalites. Ce brassage culturel et ce vivre-ensemble, c'est justement ce que nous apprecions dans les Jeux olympiques de la jeunesse. » Des rencontres, des sourires et des amities qui se construisent au fil des journees. a Dakar, les JOJ 2026 rappellent que le sport ne se limite pas aux performances et aux medailles. Il est aussi un langage universel, capable de rapprocher les peuples et de faire tomber les barrieres. Une aventure humaine dont les souvenirs et les liens tisses pourraient bien survivre au-dela de cette grande fete du sport. Cet article a ete realise dans le cadre d'un projet de coproduction aux Jeux olympiques de la jeunesse 2026 a Dakar, soutenu par la Norvege et la cooperation suisse, entre six medias de la Fondation Hirondelle : Radio Ndeke Luka Centrafrique, Studio Hirondelle RDC, Studio Hirondelle Tchad, Studio Kalangou Niger, Studio Tamani Mali et Studio Yafa Burkina Faso. L’article JOJ Dakar 2026 : au-delà du sport, des rencontres et des amitiés sans frontières est apparu en premier sur Studio Tamani - Informations, débats, magazines : toute l’actualité du Mali, en 5 langues .

items.title: À l’ONU, le Maroc recueille de nouveaux soutiens à son plan d’autonomie
items.description: La position marocaine sur la question du Sahara a bénéficié d’un soutien renouvelé de plusieurs grandes puissances et organisations régionales lors des deux séances de l’Assemblée générale des Nations unies, tenues les 10 et 11 novembre. Consacrées à l’examen du veto opposé par la Russie au projet de résolution américain relatif au mandat de la Mission des Nations unies pour l’organisation d’un référendum au Sahara occidental (Minurso), ces discussions ont également donné lieu à une série de prises de position sur les perspectives de règlement du différend. Les interventions des délégations ont notamment confirmé la place croissante de l’initiative marocaine d’autonomie dans le débat international. La majorité des pays intervenus a réaffirmé son soutien à la souveraineté du Maroc et à son intégrité territoriale, tandis que plusieurs autres ont plaidé pour que le plan d’autonomie constitue le socle des négociations destinées à mettre fin au conflit. Ces déclarations présentent un intérêt particulier en raison du cadre dans lequel elles ont été formulées. En se tenant en dehors du Conseil de sécurité, les débats ont offert à Rabat une nouvelle tribune diplomatique pour exposer son initiative aux États membres et mesurer leurs positions sur les perspectives d’un règlement politique, dans un contexte marqué par les évolutions récentes du dossier au Conseil et l’expiration du mandat de la Minurso. Les prises de parole ont fait apparaître plusieurs degrés de soutien. Les États-Unis ont notamment réaffirmé leur volonté de continuer à piloter les efforts de règlement. D’autres pays ont exprimé un appui explicite à la souveraineté marocaine et à l’intégrité territoriale du Royaume, tandis que plusieurs délégations ont surtout insisté sur la nécessité de retenir l’autonomie comme base des négociations. Des États africains, arabes, européens et asiatiques ont ainsi fait entendre des positions convergentes. Washington maintient le cap L’intervention de Mike Waltz, représentant permanent des États-Unis auprès des Nations unies, a constitué l’un des principaux signaux politiques de ces débats. Malgré le veto russe qui a empêché l’adoption du projet de résolution américain, Washington entend maintenir son engagement dans le dossier. Le diplomate a déploré le recours au droit de veto, intervenu alors que le processus politique avait retrouvé son élan après l’adoption de la résolution 2797. Il a souligné que ce texte historique avait consacré l’initiative marocaine d’autonomie comme base pour faire avancer les négociations. Mike Waltz a également assuré que les États-Unis n’avaient pas achevé leurs efforts en vue d’un règlement du conflit. Sous la direction du président Donald Trump, Washington entend poursuivre son travail avec les parties concernées et les Nations unies afin de parvenir à une solution durable. La portée de cette déclaration tient autant au fond qu'à la démarche annoncée. Le soutien américain à la proposition marocaine ne relève pas seulement d'un positionnement politique : il s'accompagne de la volonté de continuer à conduire les efforts diplomatiques et à élaborer des plans concrets pour mettre fin à un conflit vieux de près de cinq décennies. Cette intervention a également permis de replacer les déclarations des autres délégations dans une perspective plus large. Soutenu par onze membres du Conseil de sécurité, le projet de résolution américain s'inscrivait dans une orientation visant à faire de l'autonomie le fondement des négociations. Une approche que plusieurs États de différents continents ont de nouveau défendue devant l'Assemblée générale, malgré l'échec de son adoption au Conseil. L'autonomie adossée à la souveraineté marocaine En Afrique, plusieurs pays ont dépassé le cadre d'un soutien de principe à l'initiative marocaine pour réaffirmer explicitement la souveraineté du Royaume et son intégrité territoriale. La Gambie figure parmi les délégations les plus affirmatives. Elle a renouvelé son soutien au Maroc sur l'ensemble de son territoire, Sahara compris, en présentant l'autonomie sous souveraineté marocaine comme la seule base réaliste, crédible et durable pour les négociations. La Guinée-Bissau a, elle aussi, réitéré son appui à l'intégrité territoriale et à la souveraineté du Royaume, tout en plaidant pour une solution définitive dans le cadre de l'initiative marocaine. Des positions similaires ont été exprimées par Madagascar, qui a renouvelé son soutien à la souveraineté du Maroc et à son intégrité territoriale, ainsi que par Djibouti. Ce dernier a réaffirmé son appui constant à l'initiative d'autonomie dans le cadre de la souveraineté marocaine, qu'il considère comme la seule solution politique susceptible de garantir un règlement juste, durable et mutuellement acceptable. La Guinée a, pour sa part, estimé que la proposition marocaine constituait la seule base sérieuse, crédible et réaliste pour parvenir à un règlement politique respectueux de la souveraineté du Royaume et de son intégrité territoriale. La convergence de ces déclarations réside dans le lien direct qu'elles établissent entre le règlement politique du différend et la souveraineté marocaine. Au-delà des appels classiques à la reprise du dialogue, ces pays défendent ainsi un cadre de référence précis : une solution fondée sur l'autonomie dans le cadre de la souveraineté du Maroc. Une orientation qui confère au soutien exprimé sur le continent africain une portée politique particulière. L'initiative marocaine comme socle des négociations D'autres États africains ont privilégié une approche centrée sur la pertinence de l'initiative marocaine, qu'ils présentent comme le cadre le plus réaliste, crédible et applicable pour parvenir à un règlement. Leurs déclarations ne comportent toutefois pas toutes le même degré d'affirmation sur la question de la souveraineté. La Sierra Leone a ainsi soutenu la proposition marocaine, qu'elle considère comme le cadre le plus crédible, réaliste et applicable, tout en rappelant que tout accord devrait recueillir le libre consentement des populations du Sahara. La Côte d'Ivoire a, de son côté, qualifié l'initiative d'offre sérieuse et crédible, permettant aux habitants de la région de prendre part à la gestion de leurs affaires politiques, économiques et sociales. Elle a également salué les projets de développement menés à Laâyoune et à Dakhla. Cette orientation a été reprise par les Comores, qui se sont appuyées sur la résolution 2797 pour réaffirmer que l'autonomie marocaine devait constituer la base des négociations. Le Togo a, pour sa part, décrit l'initiative comme l'option la plus crédible, réaliste et pragmatique, appelant les parties à négocier de bonne foi et sans conditions préalables. Le Liberia a également apporté son soutien à la proposition marocaine, qu'il considère comme la base la plus réaliste, crédible et applicable pour parvenir à un règlement négocié. Le pays a tenu à préciser que son abstention lors du vote sur le projet de résolution russe ne modifiait en rien son soutien à cette démarche. La position du Sénégal s'inscrit dans une logique similaire. Dakar a mis en avant la capacité du plan d'autonomie à favoriser une solution pacifique, durable et tournée vers le développement, tout en soulignant sa compatibilité avec le principe de l'autodétermination. Le pays a également appelé à poursuivre le dialogue sous l'égide des Nations unies. La Guinée équatoriale a, quant à elle, présenté l'initiative marocaine comme une avancée concrète dans le processus politique. Elle a réaffirmé son soutien aux efforts de l'envoyé personnel du secrétaire général des Nations unies, ainsi que son attachement au respect du cessez-le-feu par le Maroc. Un soutien qui dépasse le cadre africain Au-delà du continent africain, les déclarations recueillies à l'Assemblée générale ont également fait ressortir une convergence de positions dans les espaces arabe, européen et asiatique. Sur le plan arabe, les pays du Conseil de coopération du Golfe (CCG) ont renouvelé leur soutien à l'initiative d'autonomie sous souveraineté marocaine. Cette position a été exprimée par Bahreïn au nom des États membres du Conseil, avec l'adhésion des Émirats arabes unis et du Qatar. En Europe, la France a affirmé que le présent et l'avenir du Sahara s'inscrivaient dans le cadre de la souveraineté marocaine. Le Royaume-Uni a, de son côté, renouvelé son soutien à l'initiative marocaine, qu'il considère comme la base la plus crédible, applicable et pragmatique pour parvenir à un règlement durable. Le Portugal a également appuyé la proposition, tandis que la délégation de l'Union européenne a réaffirmé son soutien à des négociations fondées sur l'initiative marocaine et inscrites dans le cadre de la résolution 2797. Le soutien s'est également manifesté en Asie. Le Japon a réaffirmé son appui à la résolution 2797, tout en rappelant la déclaration conjointe maroco-japonaise de mai 2026, dans laquelle Tokyo avait exprimé son soutien à l'autonomie sous souveraineté marocaine. L'Estonie a, pour sa part, plaidé pour des négociations fondées sur la proposition marocaine, dans une position qui rejoint l'orientation défendue par plusieurs pays européens au cours de la séance. Au terme de ces deux journées de débats, le Maroc a ainsi disposé d'une tribune lui permettant de mesurer l'étendue du soutien international à son initiative et de consolider les positions exprimées par les États sur cette question au sein d'une enceinte réunissant 193 membres. La portée de cette séquence diplomatique ne tient cependant pas au seul nombre de pays ayant manifesté leur soutien. Elle réside également dans la nature de leurs déclarations : certains établissent explicitement le règlement du différend dans le cadre de la souveraineté marocaine, d'autres consacrent l'autonomie comme base des négociations, tandis que plusieurs réaffirment la volonté des États-Unis, des pays européens et des États arabes de poursuivre leur engagement en faveur d'une solution politique articulée autour de cette initiative. The post À l’ONU, le Maroc recueille de nouveaux soutiens à son plan d’autonomie appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Muniz answers Murphy in three minutes as Fulham hold Newcastle
items.description: Newcastle spent most of Saturday afternoon looking for an opening at Craven Cottage. When Jacob Murphy finally curled the ball past Bernd Leno in the 80th minute, the visitors had a lead that lasted only 179 seconds. Rodrigo Muniz equalised for Fulham in the 83rd, leaving the sides with a 1-1 draw on 7 November 2026. Iwobi and Calvin Bassey both started for Fulham. The match went into the break goalless, a result that has to be kept separate from the full-time draw at betting sites in Cameroon , since the two selections cover different periods. The chances that went begging Fulham were lively early on. Oscar Bobb forced Lukáš Horníček into a save, and Gonzalo García glanced the following corner over. Newcastle soon found a route of their own. Harvey Barnes met an attack from Yoane Wissa and Will Osula, but Leno stopped his close-range finish with a foot. Barnes escaped again and tried to place the ball beyond the goalkeeper. This time Leno got his head to it. Newcastle thought they had scored from the resulting corner when Dan Burn turned in Murphy’s delivery. The goal was ruled out for a foul by Wissa on Timothy Castagne. The official score remained 0-0. It was hardly a first half without attacking chances. Fulham’s Alex Iwobi supplied a cross for Josh King, whose volley brought a sharp save from Horníček. Iwobi picked out King again near the interval, only for the header to go wide. Calvin Bassey also started for the home side, giving the match a second Nigerian international in Fulham’s lineup. The missed opportunities explain why Murphy’s eventual strike looked so decisive. Both goalkeepers had already made stops that could have changed the score considerably earlier. One careless pass, then the reply Newcastle’s goal began with Fulham losing possession in midfield. Murphy collected the loose pass, drove in from the right and bent a left-footed finish beyond Leno. After all the earlier saves, it took one mistake in possession to break the stalemate. Fulham did not leave much time for the away end to celebrate. A high regain put the ball into Shea Charles’s path; he moved it to substitute César Palacios. The attempted cross was blocked, but Muniz reacted to the loose ball and flicked it through a crowd near goal. Muniz had come off the bench earlier in the half. The Premier League said this was his first league goal in 28 matches. His finish came before Newcastle could settle into defending the advantage. Three scorelines, one match The last ten minutes made the score change twice, even though neither side took all three points. A selection covering Cameroon football also depends on the named period, not on which side led for part of the match. The confirmed sequence was short: Match point Confirmed score What changed Half-time 0-0 Neither side had scored 80th minute Fulham 0-1 Newcastle Murphy put the visitors ahead 83rd minute Fulham 1-1 Newcastle Muniz equalised Full-time 1-1 The teams shared the points The draw at half-time and the draw at full-time are different market selections. An in-play price quoted straight after Murphy’s goal would also reflect a different score from one displayed after Muniz’s response. The period on an accepted ticket remains relevant to settlement; full-time markets normally include stoppage time, not extra time, unless the rules specify otherwise. Iwobi’s part before the goals Iwobi was not credited with either goal, but Fulham’s report shows he helped create chances when there was still no score. His cross led to King’s volley, and he later combined with Palacios as the hosts looked for a way into the box. Those moves matter when judging the balance of the game. If attention goes straight to Murphy and Muniz, the work before the 80th minute disappears. Leno’s saves against Barnes and Horníček’s interventions at the other end show that neither goalkeeper had enjoyed an uneventful afternoon. Bassey played from the start as part of the home defence. His presence alongside Iwobi gave Nigerian readers two familiar names to follow, though neither player was credited with a goal. The first-half cross and the late scramble tell different stories: one ended in a goalkeeper save, the other in a finish from close range. Fulham had needed both kinds of attacking pressure just to take a point. The draw was nearly lost again There was still time for a winner. Lewis Hall had a chance from inside the area but Leno kept out the attempt. At the other end, Ryan Sessegnon struck a fierce volley in added time that Horníček turned away. The draw took Fulham’s unbeaten league sequence to four games. Newcastle, meanwhile, had to settle for a point after a better display than in their recent defeats. The Premier League described the match as the clubs’ first draw at Craven Cottage in this competition. For Fulham, the late equaliser is the headline. But without Leno’s interventions before and after it, the home side might not have taken even that point. Newcastle’s frustration is the reverse: Murphy finally found the finish they wanted, and within three minutes Muniz had taken the win away.
