items.title: IHC suspends local government elections in Islamabad
items.description: ISLAMABAD: The Islamabad High Court (IHC) on Friday suspended the upcoming local government elections in the federal capital, putting the Election Commission of Pakistan’s (ECP) latest election schedule on hold until the next hearing. Last week, a writ petition was filed by Chaudhry Amjad Ali, who had challenged the ECP’s short order and the subsequent election schedule , both dated Oct 21, 2026, for holding local government elections in the Islamabad Capital Territory (ICT). He argued that the polls, scheduled for Dec 20, could not be held until the legal status of the existing constituency delimitation was conclusively determined. A single-member bench comprising Justice Umair Majeed Malik granted the interim relief while hearing the writ petition on Friday. “Operation of the impugned order dated Oct 21, 2026, and the impugned election schedule dated Oct 21, 2026, as revised by the Election Commission, shall remain suspended until the next date of hearing,” the court order read. The court also issued notices to the respondents, directing them to submit their reports and para-wise comments before the next hearing, scheduled for Nov 26, 2026. Advocate Barrister Qazi Adil Aziz appeared for the petitioner, along with Malik Talha and Muhammad Yaseen Iqbal. They argued that under Articles 140-A(2), 218(3) and 219(d) of the Constitution, the ECP was “duty-bound to hold local government elections honestly, justly, fairly and in accordance with the law”. The counsel contended that the election programme had become legally compromised due to legislative changes between the original Islamabad Capital Territory Local Government Act, 2015 (LG Act 2015), and the subsequent Islamabad Capital Territory Local Government Ordinance, 2026 (LG Ordinance 2026). According to the petition, the LG Act 2015 provided for one Metropolitan Corporation and 125 Union Councils, each divided into nine wards. The delimitation process for this structure began in December 2024, and an election programme was issued on Dec 26, 2025, but was subsequently withdrawn. Meanwhile, the LG Ordinance 2026 altered the capital’s local government structure by introducing three Town Corporations, changing the process for constituting and delimiting Union Councils, removing the nine-ward structure and providing for delimitation on the basis of census blocks. Consequently, the number of Union Councils increased from 125 to 130. The counsel submitted that the ECP subsequently issued revised delimitation timelines on Aug 25, 2026, and completed the process with the publication of the final list of 130 Union Councils on Oct 14, 2026. However, after a single 120-day extension, the LG Ordinance 2026 ceased to have effect under Article 89 of the Constitution, resulting in the revival of the original LG Act 2015. At this point, the counsel argued, the ECP suddenly issued the impugned order and election schedule to conduct polls under the original LG Act 2015. The petitioner’s counsel contended that the impugned order did not address the delimitation of the 125 Union Councils, their nine wards or the Metropolitan Corporation under the revived law. They argued that the delimitation carried out under the amended law could not serve as the basis for elections under the revived LG Act 2015. They therefore maintained that fresh delimitation and preparation of electoral rolls in accordance with the LG Act 2015 and the Elections Act, 2017, were necessary before the elections could lawfully be held. The counsel further argued that holding elections without completing the required delimitation would violate Article 218(3) of the Constitution and the electoral framework under the LG Act 2015 and the Elections Act, besides resulting in unnecessary expenditure of public funds. After hearing the initial arguments, the court observed that the points raised required consideration and suspended the operation of the ECP’s order and election schedule until the next hearing, scheduled for Nov 26. Later in the day, in compliance with the IHC order, the ECP suspended the local election programme in Islamabad till the date of the next hearing, as per a notification issued by the ECP Secretariat. On Thursday, Chief Election Commissioner CEC Sikandar Sultan Raja accused the federal government of trying to sabotage the local government elections in Islamabad. The local government elections in Islamabad have faced numerous delays and postponements since the term of the last local government expired in February 2021. The ECP has issued multiple schedules, only to cancel them later for various reasons, including legislative changes and court orders. The delimitation of constituencies and union councils was carried out six times, while the election schedule was issued four times. The ECP had decided that, since the local government law enacted in 2015 was still in force, elections would be held under the Act. This meant polls would be held in 50 constituencies, after which the mayor and deputy mayors would be elected. After the completion of various stages of the electoral process, it had decided that p olling would be held on Dec 20 . The ECP had reserved four days, from December 21 to 24, for the consolidation of results.

items.title: Kane takes Ballon d’Or as England’s wait finally ends
items.description: Twenty-five years after Michael Owen won it, the men’s Ballon d’Or belongs to an Englishman again. Harry Kane picked up the 2026 award at the London Palladium on 26 October, with 73 goals behind his claim. Real Madrid’s Kylian Mbappé finished second. Kane also left the ceremony with the Gerd Müller Trophy for the leading men’s goalscorer. Comparing a Ballon d’Or forecast through 1xbet South Sudan with a top-scorer selection involves two different results: one comes from a jury, the other from a goal count. Kane collected both honours in London, but they remain separate contests. The numbers behind the London announcement The goals came in two shirts. England Football’s account of the season separates his Bayern appearances from his international ones: Team Appearances Goals Bayern Munich, all competitions 51 61 England, all matches 14 12 Combined 65 73 The league supplied 36 goals in 31 appearances. Kane finished top of the Bundesliga scorers again, for the third year running. He added ten in the DFB-Pokal and one in the Supercup; his European haul was 14 as Bayern went as far as the Champions League semi-finals. Competition names also matter to sports betting in South Sudan , since Kane’s 61 club goals and 36 Bundesliga goals answer different questions. The Champions League figure is part of his club total, rather than an extra contribution to add on top. For England, six goals came in seven World Cup finals appearances. The national side finished third, its best placing since the 1966 victory. The remaining international goals in his season record came in qualifying and friendlies. Five came in five World Cup qualifiers, with another in two international friendly appearances, giving him 12 goals in 14 England outings overall. Bayern’s three domestic trophies give the goals some context, too. They kept the league title and lifted the DFB-Pokal, after winning the Franz Beckenbauer Supercup. The Ballon d’Or case included a team collecting silverware while Kane supplied the finishing. Owen’s wait ends, and Bayern’s too Kane becomes the fifth English player to receive the Ballon d’Or. The four names before him cover very different chapters of the award: 1956: Stanley Matthews took the first award. 1966: Bobby Charlton added it to his World Cup year. 1978 and 1979: Kevin Keegan won twice with Hamburg. 2001: Michael Owen brought it to Liverpool. Owen’s victory had remained the last English success for a quarter of a century. Kane’s award adds another name to that short list rather than another win for a previous recipient. Bayern had been waiting even longer. Karl-Heinz Rummenigge was their last winner, back in 1981. The Munich line now runs from Gerd Müller and Franz Beckenbauer through Rummenigge to Kane. There was recognition for another current Bayern player near the top of the voting, with Michael Olise finishing ninth. Kane’s own award nevertheless ends a 45-year gap for the club, stretching well beyond the careers of its present squad. A vote that included the World Cup The judging did not stop when the club season ended. Under the 2026 rules, performances counted from 3 August 2025 through 19 July 2026. The World Cup was inside that window. The rules provide for an international jury of specialist journalists, with one representative from each of the top 100 countries in the relevant men’s FIFA rankings. Each juror ranks ten players from a 30-man shortlist. A juror’s first pick gets 15 points. Second is worth 12, with smaller totals for the remaining eight places. Individual performances take priority under the published criteria. Titles count as well, and the rules ask the jury to consider class and fair play. Adding up the ballots produces the winner. That process explains why a scoring chart and an awards result can put different players first. In the Champions League scoring race, Kane finished with 14 and Mbappé with 15. The Ballon d’Or ballot put them in the reverse order. An award-winner selection and a Champions League top-scorer selection would therefore concern different winning names for this season. Two honours on the same evening The Gerd Müller Trophy was Kane’s second, after he shared it with Mbappé in 2024. His European Golden Shoe had already been secured through his Bundesliga scoring: 36 league goals carried 72 points in that award’s calculation. The Golden Shoe was also his second, having previously taken it in 2023/24. Bayern’s May announcement placed Erling Haaland second on 54 points and Mbappé third on 50. Those were league-scoring points, a different measure from the journalists’ ballots used for the Ballon d’Or. The London setting had a historical purpose. The ceremony marked the Ballon d’Or’s 70th anniversary and paid tribute to Matthews, its first winner. France Football’s award has been co-organised with UEFA since 2024. England coach Thomas Tuchel congratulated his captain, saying he was delighted that Kane’s performances had received formal recognition. At Bayern, the response also looked towards the trophy’s return to Munich. Kane told the audience: “It’s an honour to play for this club and I’m glad to be bringing this trophy back to Munich.” The post Kane takes Ballon d’Or as England’s wait finally ends appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Microsoft’s latest email outage turned into a full blown global cloud crisis
items.description: Microsoft is slowly recovering from its day-long outage after much of the company’s systems were hit by a cascading software issue. The problems, which started Thursday, were initially flagged as affecting the company’s services in the U.S. and the Americas, but quickly spread around the world, as engineers struggled to recover downed servers. What began as an Outlook email and Teams video conferencing outage soon developed into a full blown meltdown, affecting the company’s cloud services for both consumer and business email, files, and documents. The outage also knocked out the company’s Copilot AI tools, Defender security screening software, and prevented system administrators from accessing their internal Intune dashboards and features. Some users reportedly experienced issues with accessing their cloud-based Windows computers. Microsoft hasn’t yet said what caused the issues, only saying the outage involved “a large number of servers being unexpectedly unavailable.” The company said it continues to investigate the cause. The outage affected a broad range of industries, including TechCrunch’s own email. We’ve reached out to Microsoft for comment about the incident. Image Credits: Fabrice COFFRINI / AFP / Getty Images As of Friday morning on the U.S. east coast, Microsoft’s Outlook email service had begun to recover and some emails have been trickling in. The recovery comes after engineers initially could not find the cause of the issue that was causing servers in Microsoft’s data centers to fail. Doug Madory, the director of internet analysis at Kentik, a company that monitors internet traffic worldwide, said in a post on Bluesky that traffic was returning to Microsoft’s services after about 18 hours of downtime. Microsoft said in its latest status update on Friday that there was “no evidence of malicious activity associated with this incident.” That may be some solace for the millions who went without their email and online services yesterday, but the company is likely to face questions about its inability to swiftly recover from an outage of its own making. A Microsoft spokesperson did not respond to our questions asking if the company has the technical means to detect malicious activity, such as logs, or if Microsoft has a way to check what happened. The last major incident affecting Microsoft services was in September , when a days-long outage hit Microsoft’s cloud services. During that outage, Microsoft blamed a “core authentication configuration” issue that prevented users from accessing the service.

items.title: Yiaga Africa: Youth participation in 2027 elections declines by 20%
items.description: Yiaga Africa, an NGO, says the number of young people under 35 expected to participate in the forthcoming general elections has declined by a further 20 per cent, in spite of the enactment of the Not Too Young to Run law. The Executive Director, Yiaga Africa, Dr Samson Itodo, made this known at the Ready To Run Bootcamp for young candidates of political parties under the age of 35 years in Lagos on Friday. The News Agency of Nigeria reports that the programme, which is funded by the European Union, has the theme: “Ready to Run Bootcamp: From Aspiration to Representation”. Itodo, represented by its Programme Coordinator, Mr Ibrahim Faruk, said that following the passage of the law in 2019 by President Muhammadu Buhari, young people under 35 constituted 38 per cent of candidates in the 2019 general elections The executive director said that the percentage further dropped to about 28 per cent in 2023. Itodo attributed the decline to the high costs for nomination forms, campaigning, along with party structures and primary control among others. The executive director added that this leaned toward established interests, which had pushed young people to the margins and made securing political tickets difficult. He said: “The first thing Yiaga is doing is what we are doing here today, you know, there is the narrative that says young people are not ready to run. “Yiaga Africa is also changing that narrative to say young people are ready to run, and we are doing that through the Ready to Run boot camps to ensure that young people are ready to run. “​We have also done a lot of electoral reform advocacy; a lot of the changes to the Electoral Act have been as a result of advocacy. ​”While there have been attempts to reduce the high cost of nominations, also ensure that parties are more democratic and inclusive in a way that supports young people. “​Some of these advocacy efforts have been fruitful, some of them have taught us lessons. “We will continue to advocate for an electoral process that accommodates more young people, is more inclusive, less expensive and as democratic as possible,” he said. ​Itodo urged INEC and stakeholders to emphasise on ensuring a credible, secure, and logistically sound electoral process that the outcomes would reflect the will of the people. He also urged young Nigerians to collect their Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs), participate fully and peacefully as voters, candidates, or agents, and refuse to sit out the democratic process. In his remarks, the Founder, African Governance Institute for Development, Mr Seyi Adisa admitted that running for office was more difficult for young people, as elections required not only financial resources but also “social capital”. According to him, while older individuals generally have more experience and social capital, young people can win elections. “It is more difficult, but achievable with the right strategies, networks, coalitions, and alliances,”he said. Adisa said although some established political parties had strong structures, many were open to young candidates if they brought value, capacity, and strong backing from their party and peers. “​Age is not the sole criterion; candidates must bring substantive contributions, be strong party members, and have community support rather than relying solely on youth or personal funds. ​”While laws like the “Not Too Young to Run” lowered the age barrier, progress has not been as fast as hoped. The political environment remains dynamic, and young candidates still face cultural, financial, and systemic barriers. “​The key challenge isn’t just that young people are running, but whether they are prepared to win, ” he said. A facilitator, Dr Samuel Oguche, said while aspiration was encouraged, candidates must “play by the rules” for democracy to thrive, the rule of law must reign, which means obedience to the law rather than acting as violators of it. Oguche said candidates must know the terrain of elections was regulated by law, governed by instruments such as the Constitution, the Electoral Act, INEC regulations, and guidelines, and internal rules of political parties and judicial authorities. Oguche, a Senior Executive Fellow from the National Institute for Legislative and Democratic Studies, said compliance was required from the pre-election stage through the election and post-election stages. Speaking to newsmen, Mr Oladipupo Ogunseye, the ADC candidate, House of Representatives, Mushin II, in Lagos State, said youth participation faced significant entry barriers. Ogunseye, who said he started politics at the age of 18, said that contesting for political office required substantial financial, mental, and emotional resources as well as experience and relationship-building. According to him, because of these demands, many young people do not actively participate in contesting for office, though many are involved in political party membership and youth group activities. The candidate said he did not necessarily brand himself solely as a “young person running, ” as it could sometimes feel like a disadvantage with the electorate. To bridge the gap between perception and reality, he noted that the entry barrier must be lowered so more young people could participate as candidates and aspirants. He said: “Increased participation will prove that young people can succeed in office, establishing a positive sample size to encourage further youth representation.” NAN reports that the programme brought together young aspiring candidates for an engaging learning experience designed to strengthen their capacity, build their confidence, and prepare them for effective political participation ahead of the 2027 elections. Through the Ready To Run initiative, Yiaga Africa is equipping young aspiring political candidates aged 35 and below with the knowledge, skills, and tools to navigate the journey towards elective office. The boot camp featured practical sessions on campaign strategy. Political participation and the dynamics of the electoral environment. items.title: « Si vous êtes successful, nous, on est successful », Simon Tiémtoré aux clients et partenaires de Vista Bank
items.description: Le président de Vista Group Holding, Simon Tiémtoré, a échangé avec les clients et partenaires de Vista Bank Burkina, ce jeudi 12 novembre 2026, au siège de Vista Bank et Assurances à Ouagadougou. À cette occasion, il a réaffirmé l’engagement du groupe à renforcer ses capacités de financement, notamment à travers la fusion entre Vista Bank Burkina et la Société Générale Burkina Faso (SGBF), attendue au début du premier trimestre 2027. Il a également annoncé une nouvelle dynamique commerciale pour améliorer la qualité des services et répondre plus rapidement aux attentes des clients. La rencontre a réuni des opérateurs économiques, des clients et des partenaires des différentes entités du groupe, notamment Vista Bank Burkina, la SGBF, Vista Assurances Burkina et ACEP. Pour Simon Tiémtoré, cette initiative devait permettre de remercier les acteurs économiques pour leur confiance, mais aussi de recueillir directement leurs préoccupations. « Il est important pour moi d'être présent avec vous, non seulement pour vous remercier, parce qu'on ne le fait pas très souvent. On ne s'assoit pas pour pouvoir en fait se regarder, se dire merci. Vous dire merci pour la confiance que vous portez à Vista Bank depuis que nous l'avons créée il y a cinq ans » , a-t-il déclaré. Le président de Vista Group Holding a également souhaité que les clients puissent prendre la parole afin de partager leurs attentes et leurs difficultés. Il a notamment reconnu que les délais de traitement de certains dossiers constituaient une préoccupation pour plusieurs partenaires de la banque. « Nous allons impulser une nouvelle dynamique commerciale, où nous serons beaucoup plus réactifs, pour répondre un peu plus à vos attentes dans les délais. Parce que c'est important de comprendre l'importance de la célérité dans la réponse, dans le traitement de vos dossiers, parce que vous aussi, vous avez des engagements avec des partenaires, soit localement ou à l'international » , a-t-il assuré. Une fusion pour renforcer les capacités de financement L'un des principaux sujets abordés au cours de cette rencontre concerne le rapprochement entre Vista Bank Burkina et la Société Générale Burkina Faso, membre du groupe Vista. Cette opération doit aboutir à la création d'une seule banque qui conservera l'enseigne Vista Bank. Pour Simon Tiémtoré, cette fusion doit permettre de renforcer le bilan de la future entité, ses ressources et ses fonds propres, afin d'accroître sa capacité à accompagner les entreprises et les particuliers. Il estime que le regroupement des deux établissements permettra également de diversifier les financements et d'élargir les possibilités d'accompagnement des clients. « Vous avez une équipe renforcée, une équipe qui est dynamique, une banque forte qui sera mise en place à l'issue de la fusion et qui aura beaucoup plus de ressources » , a-t-il indiqué. Le président de Vista Group Holding a toutefois tenu à rassurer les clients sur la continuité de leurs opérations durant cette transition. Tirant les enseignements des difficultés rencontrées lors d'une précédente migration informatique, il a assuré que les dispositions nécessaires étaient prises pour éviter des perturbations dans le traitement des comptes et des engagements. « Dans le cas de la fusion, il n'y aura pas de souci, et il n'y aura aucune friction en termes de traitement de vos comptes, aucun traitement de vos engagements » , a-t-il affirmé. Il a précisé qu'une équipe de la holding bancaire travaille sur ce processus depuis deux ans. Les différentes étapes légales et réglementaires devront être franchies avant l'harmonisation des enseignes et du réseau. Le groupe vise une concrétisation de la fusion au début du premier trimestre 2027. Le financement des projets publics et privés au cœur des ambitions-©Faso7 Au-delà de la fusion, Simon Tiémtoré a insisté sur la volonté de Vista Bank de contribuer davantage au financement de l'économie burkinabè. Il a notamment encouragé les opérateurs économiques à solliciter la banque pour leurs projets, particulièrement dans les secteurs de l'énergie, du bâtiment et des travaux publics, de la cimenterie, de l'import-export et du transport. « Nous avons de l'appétit pour l'État, nous avons de l'appétit pour les projets de l'État. Donc n'hésitez pas à nous solliciter si vous avez des projets de l'État » , a-t-il lancé. Le président de Vista Group Holding a également invité les banques locales à renforcer leur collaboration pour mobiliser les ressources nécessaires au financement des projets structurants. Il estime que les capacités financières existent et qu'une meilleure coopération entre les établissements bancaires peut contribuer à soutenir les ambitions économiques du pays. « Nous avons la ferme conviction que les ressources sont là, les ressources sont disponibles pour le Burkina Faso pour appuyer le développement de l'économie burkinabè. C'est à nous, banques locales, de pouvoir nous fédérer, travailler ensemble pour pouvoir soutenir le développement économique du Burkina Faso » , a-t-il déclaré. Il a cité plusieurs opérations auxquelles le groupe a pris part, notamment le financement du programme de modernisation du transport public à travers la Société de transport en commun de Ouagadougou (SOTRACO) et l'opération Diaspora Bond de l'État burkinabè. Cette dernière a permis de mobiliser 151,5 milliards de F CFA en 30 jours, pour un objectif initial de 125 milliards de F CFA. Simon Tiémtoré a annoncé la préparation d'une deuxième tranche de cette opération en 2027. Selon lui, la demande exprimée par la diaspora burkinabè témoigne de son intérêt à participer au financement du développement national. « Nous allons en faire une deuxième. C'était la première tranche. Nous allons faire une deuxième tranche l'année prochaine et nous travaillerons ardemment avec les autorités. La diaspora en demande. Elle veut participer. Aujourd'hui, elle veut jouer son rôle dans le cadre du développement économique du Burkina Faso » , a-t-il annoncé. Une ouverture vers les marchés internationaux-©Faso7 Le renforcement des capacités de financement passe également, selon le président de Vista Group Holding, par le développement de ses activités à l'international. Il a notamment évoqué la création d'une succursale de Vista Bank en France, présentée comme un outil destiné à faciliter les opérations financières transfrontalières et à mobiliser des ressources sur les marchés de capitaux. Cette implantation doit notamment permettre au groupe d'améliorer l'accompagnement des entreprises burkinabè engagées dans des opérations d'importation et d'exportation. Simon Tiémtoré a évoqué la possibilité d'effectuer des transactions dans plusieurs devises, notamment le dollar, l'euro, le yuan chinois, le dirham marocain, le rand sud-africain, le dollar singapourien et bien d’autres devises. Il a ainsi invité les opérateurs économiques à tirer davantage profit de cette plateforme pour leurs activités commerciales avec la Chine, la Turquie, l'Europe et d'autres marchés. Le groupe entend également accompagner les entreprises burkinabè qui souhaitent étendre leurs activités dans les autres pays où il est présent, notamment en Sierra Leone, en Gambie, au Tchad, en Guinée équatoriale, Cameroun, Niger. La relation client et les services digitaux comme priorités Simon Tiémtoré a par ailleurs annoncé un renforcement des services destinés à la clientèle, notamment à travers Vista Online. Cette plateforme numérique permet aux clients d'effectuer certaines opérations à distance, notamment la consultation des soldes et des transactions. L'objectif, selon lui, est de réduire les déplacements en agence et de faire gagner du temps aux utilisateurs. Il a également assuré que le groupe entendait améliorer la disponibilité de ses équipes et la réactivité dans le traitement des demandes. S'adressant directement aux opérateurs économiques, il a résumé la relation qu'il souhaite établir avec eux en ces termes : « Votre problème, c'est de trouver les marchés. Notre problème, c'est de mobiliser les ressources et de vous accompagner au niveau financier le plus rapidement possible » Il a enfin invité les clients et partenaires à faire remonter leurs observations afin de permettre à la banque d'améliorer ses prestations. « Si vous êtes successful, nous, on est successful » , a-t-il conclu, insistant sur le lien entre la réussite des entreprises accompagnées et celle de l'établissement bancaire. Cette rencontre intervient alors que Vista Bank Burkina prépare une nouvelle étape de son développement avec le rapprochement de la SGBF. À terme, le groupe ambitionne de renforcer son positionnement sur le marché bancaire national et d'accroître sa contribution au financement des activités économiques au Burkina Faso. Josué TIENDREBEOGO Faso7 L’article « Si vous êtes successful, nous, on est successful », Simon Tiémtoré aux clients et partenaires de Vista Bank est apparu en premier sur Faso7 .

items.description: Le smartphone a bouleversé notre mode de vie ainsi que notre façon de s’informer. Beaucoup en sont devenus accrocs, particulièrement les jeunes. items.title: How a sex scandal at Nvidia is putting pressure on the White House
items.description: How close is Donald Trump to Jensen Huang? The answer is very. The Nvidia boss was one of the few business leaders with direct access to the US president. He had met Trump repeatedly, travelled with him to Britain and, in May, joined him on Air Force One for his trip to China. Jensen Huang wasn’t just another tech billionaire seeking the president’s ear. He had become an important voice in one of the biggest arguments inside the administration: how much of America’s most advanced technology should be allowed to reach China. Nvidia makes the chips that power the AI revolution. Washington has restricted exports of its most advanced processors to China since 2022, believing they could help Beijing develop its military and technological capabilities. But enforcing those restrictions is difficult. Chips can be bought legally by customers in countries such as Singapore and Malaysia and then diverted to China. Chinese companies can also rent access to computing power through data centres outside the country. Jensen Huang has long argued that the restrictions are counterproductive. They shut Nvidia out of a huge market and encourage Chinese companies to develop their own alternatives. Trump appeared sympathetic to this view, allowing Nvidia to resume sales of certain chips to China last year in return for a share of the revenue, although its most advanced Blackwell chips remain off limits. But that relationship now looks rather more complicated. The allegations surrounding Jensen Huang’s reported affair with Alice Huang, of no relation but a former executive at Singapore-based company Megaspeed, have raised the possibility that a foreign intelligence operation was targeting not just a powerful businessman, but someone with unusually close access to the American president. US intelligence reportedly suspects Alice Huang of having links to Chinese intelligence. Beijing has rejected the allegations. Nvidia’s board says it has no reason to believe company secrets or national security were compromised. But the affair has opened up a much bigger question: what did the administration in Washington know, and what did it do about it? That question leads directly to Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick. His department was responsible for controlling exports of sensitive American technology. It was also being pressed to act on concerns about Megaspeed, an Nvidia customer suspected of helping divert advanced chips to China. On Thursday, Megaspeed chief executive, Tan Yong Pong, also known as James Tan, said the company “takes its compliance obligations under US export control laws extremely seriously” and is “committed to working constructively and transparently with the US government”. He said the company had co-operated with US Commerce Department inspections. A highly classified memo was shared with Lutnick about the concerns surrounding Alice Huang and Megaspeed. He resisted taking action against the company, a decision that is now under scrutiny. Other senior officials wanted a tougher response. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent was among those who reportedly questioned why Megaspeed had not been placed on the Commerce Department’s blacklist. There were also questions about why an investigation into the Singapore-based company was stopped after Nvidia intervened. The New York Times reported that Nvidia’s general counsel contacted Commerce Department investigators probing suspected chip smuggling by Megaspeed, invoking a senior Trump appointee. The department allegedly then froze its investigation and handed the case to the Justice Department. This apparently highlighted a significant disagreement about the direction of Trump’s China policy. Huang wanted access to the Chinese market. Other officials were supposedly worried about the national security consequences. Lutnick was caught in the middle. Now the political pressure is building. Members of Congress from both parties want answers. Democrats have launched an investigation into how the Commerce Department vetted Chinese companies approved to buy AI chips. Republicans are also questioning the administration’s approach. And Jensen Huang’s departure has not eased the pressure. Republican representative John Moolenaar, who chairs the House Select Committee on China, said it was in the national interest for Nvidia and other American AI firms to succeed, but that companies “should never jeopardise our nation’s security” by giving Chinese firms access to their most advanced chips. Senator Elizabeth Warren, the top Democrat on the Senate Banking Committee, said Huang’s resignation did not absolve him of responsibility, and urged Lutnick to explain why export control loopholes remain open. Meanwhile Jensen Huang’s team told Republican lawmakers on Wednesday that he plans to cooperate with their request to testify behind closed doors. The White House has not responded to the BBC’s request for comment. It has, however, told the New York Post that Trump has complete confidence in Lutnick, describing him as “the most transformative commerce secretary in modern history”. That is a fairly emphatic show of support, particularly amid reports that officials are weighing whether Lutnick should be forced out. There are some obvious questions. If Lutnick had indeed been warned about the risks, why did his department fail to act? And if other senior officials were indeed pressing for action, why did it take so long? The BBC has contacted the Commerce Department for comment. But there is an even bigger question for Trump. The president cultivated a close relationship with Huang. He was directly involved in decisions about chip sales to China. And, according to reporting in the New York Times, he was briefed on the intelligence concerns. This is becoming difficult to dismiss as the misjudgement of one businessman or one government department. Jensen Huang’s personal life may have triggered the crisis, but the questions now reach into the White House itself. How much influence did he have? What did the president know? And who was ultimately responsible for protecting America’s most sensitive technology?

items.title: At least nine detained protesting at blast-hit Turkey steel plant
items.description: Turkey's security forces on Friday detained at least nine people protesting a ban on bringing mobile phones into a steel plant that was hit by a deadly explosion this week, a workers' collective said. Workers arriving for their morning shift at the HABAS steel factory were told to leave their mobile phones at a security checkpoint, prompting them to gather at the facility's entrance in protest, according to a spokesman for the Aegean Workers' Collective.

items.title: SOBTO II à Tenkodogo: des essais de production concluants avant la mise en service de l’usine
items.description: La deuxième usine de transformation de tomates de la Société burkinabè de tomates (SOBTO), implantée à Tenkodogo, se rapproche de sa mise en service. Les essais de production réalisés ce mercredi 11 novembre 2026 se sont révélés concluants. Des résultats qui confirment le bon fonctionnement des installations de cette unité industrielle réalisée par l’APEC, avant son inauguration prochaine. Les essais se sont déroulés en présence du Directeur général de l’APEC, Karim Traoré, venu superviser les opérations. Ils ont permis de vérifier le fonctionnement des équipements et l’ensemble du processus industriel, depuis la réception de la matière première jusqu’au conditionnement du produit fini. « Les résultats sont très très satisfaisants », a déclaré le Directeur général de la SOBTO de Tenkodogo, Souleymane Sodré, satisfait du déroulement des opérations. Le Directeur général de l’APEC, Karim Traoré, a également exprimé « un sentiment de fierté de voir justement que l’équipement fonctionne bien ». Il s’est réjoui de voir les contributions des souscripteurs à l’Actionnariat populaire se traduire par des réalisations industrielles concrètes. L’usine de Tenkodogo devrait employer plus de 100 personnes et offrir de nouveaux débouchés aux producteurs de tomates, notamment dans la région du Nakambé. Avec cette deuxième unité, après celle de Bobo-Dioulasso, la disponibilité du concentré de tomate de la marque A’diaa devrait également se renforcer sur le marché national. Karim Traoré a annoncé une réorganisation du circuit de distribution, afin de faciliter l’accès des consommateurs au produit. Concernant l’approvisionnement en matière première, le Directeur général de l’APEC a indiqué que des équipes iraient à la rencontre des producteurs et des coopératives pour leur présenter les conditions de livraison des tomates à l’usine. À l’approche de l’inauguration, Karim Traoré a remercié les souscripteurs pour leur engagement et les a invités à maintenir leur confiance dans l’Actionnariat populaire. Il a également annoncé la présentation prochaine d’un bilan d’étape sur l’utilisation des ressources mobilisées et les perspectives du programme. items.title: Mahama charges new NLC members to ensure fair and timely resolution of disputes
items.description: President John Dramani Mahama has called on the newly inaugurated National Labour Commission (NLC) to make fairness and timely resolution of disputes the foundation of its work, warning that public confidence in the institution depends on how it handles workers’ grievances. He said the Commission must ensure that workers who seek redress are treated fairly and that their complaints are not subjected to unnecessary delays. The President made the remarks on Friday, November 13, when he swore in the seven members of the new Commission, emphasising the importance of its role in sustaining industrial peace and protecting workers’ livelihoods. He noted that employees who bring complaints before the institution must be confident that their cases will receive a fair hearing and be dealt with promptly. “A worker with a grievance wants to know that somebody will hear it and deal with it fairly and expeditiously. And the National Labour Commission has a responsibility to apply rules to the letter,” President Mahama said. He urged the members to discharge their responsibilities in accordance with the rules governing labour relations, noting that consistency in decision-making was necessary to strengthen the Commission’s credibility. President Mahama also congratulated the appointees and acknowledged the work of the outgoing Commission, expressing gratitude to its members for their service to the country. The new seven-member body is headed by retired Court of Appeal Justice Isaac Delali Duose. The Ghana Employers Association is represented by Joseph Kingsley Amuah and Isaac Sackey, while Prince William Ankrah and Abdul-Samad Ali Gomdah represent Organised Labour. The other members are Rosemond Freeman-Tettey and Antwi-Boasiako Sekyere, both presidential nominees. Responding on behalf of the Commission, Justice Duose thanked the President for entrusting the members with the responsibility. He pledged that the Commission would discharge its responsibilities with transparency and impartiality, assuring that every matter brought before it would be treated in accordance with those principles.

items.title: J’ai lu… « Géoféminisme, Si tu veux la paix, prépare l’égalité » de Chloé Ridel
items.description: À l’occasion de la parution de Géoféminisme : Si tu veux la paix, prépare l’égalité (Stock), Pascal Boniface reçoit Chloé Ridel, députée européenne et cofondatrice de l’Institut Rousseau, pour un échange consacré à sa lecture féministe des relations internationales et des conflits contemporains. En réponse à la formule qu’elle associe au réalisme « Qui veut la paix prépare la guerre », elle défend une autre approche des relations internationales : l’égalité entre les femmes et les hommes comme un levier de paix et de sécurité. Elle dénonce une pensée masculiniste qui imprègnerait les théories et les pratiques géopolitiques, valorisant la force et la domination au détriment de la coopération, donnant les exemples des politiques de Vladimir Poutine et Donald Trump. Chloé Ridel dénonce également la sous-représentation des femmes dans les fonctions de pouvoir y compris au sein de l’Union européenne. Une réflexion sur les liens entre domination masculine, rapports de force internationaux et sécurité collective, qui invite à repenser les conditions d’une paix durable. L’article J'ai lu… « Géoféminisme, Si tu veux la paix, prépare l'égalité » de Chloé Ridel est apparu en premier sur IRIS .

items.title: Ebola: Nigeria records zero secondary infections as 62 contacts exit monitoring
items.description: … Index patient recovers, discharged in Switzerland By Chioma Obinna Nigeria has recorded zero secondary transmission of the deadly Bundibugyo Virus Disease, a form of Ebola, following the successful completion of the 21-day monitoring period for all 62 contacts linked to the imported case confirmed in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) on October 20, 2026. The Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) yesterday announced that the last contact had been discharged from monitoring, with none of the 62 individuals developing the disease. In another development, the index patient, who was medically evacuated to Switzerland on October 26 for further treatment, has recovered, subsequently tested negative for the virus and been discharged from hospital. However, the NCDC warned that the successful completion of contact monitoring does not amount to a formal declaration that the outbreak is over, insisting that Nigeria must sustain heightened surveillance amid continued Ebola transmission in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC). Director-General of NCDC, Dr Jide Idris, who announced the development, described the outcome as encouraging, crediting early detection, prompt investigation and cooperation between health authorities and affected communities. “The 21-day monitoring period for contacts linked to the index case has been completed, with the last contact discharged today. We are glad to announce that none of the contacts became ill with the disease, meaning no transmission from the index case,” Idris said. He disclosed that 13 of the 62 contacts reported fever or other non-specific symptoms during the monitoring period. All 13 were tested for Bundibugyo Virus Disease and returned negative results. Similarly, seven alerts reported in Adamawa, Rivers, Borno, Lagos and Ekiti states within the last three weeks were investigated, with laboratory tests confirming that none was positive for the virus. The NCDC boss explained that the imported case was detected following an alert raised by healthcare workers through the agency’s event-based surveillance system, enabling the government to activate an emergency response and commence investigations. Under the leadership of the Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Professor Muhammad Ali Pate, the National Emergency Operations Centre was activated, while an Incident Management System was established to coordinate the response. According to Idris, the response focused on providing clinical care, identifying and monitoring exposed persons, preventing further transmission, protecting healthcare workers and strengthening disease surveillance. He said contact tracing covered healthcare facilities, households and other relevant settings, while infection prevention and control measures were reinforced in health facilities within the FCT and across the country. The agency also supported healthcare worker training and supplied personal protective equipment and other response materials to the affected facility and relevant points of entry. Providing an update on the index patient, Idris said laboratory tests conducted upon her arrival in Switzerland on October 26 confirmed that she was still positive for the virus. However, following further treatment and care, she recovered, tested negative and was successfully discharged. Despite the positive outcome, Idris said Nigeria’s National Emergency Operations Centre remained activated, with the Incident Management System operating at Level 3, the highest response level for Ebola disease. He said surveillance would remain heightened nationwide, while the country continued monitoring developments in countries and regions affected by the disease. The NCDC also warned that the approaching December festive season, characterised by increased movement of people, religious gatherings, concerts, festivals, sporting activities and political campaigns, required sustained public health vigilance. Idris urged Nigerians and international visitors to seek medical attention promptly if they became unwell, particularly those with recent travel history or possible exposure to infectious diseases. “Do not assume that every fever is malaria, particularly if you have recently travelled or may have been exposed to an infectious disease,” he cautioned. He advised people seeking medical care to disclose their travel history and possible exposure to healthcare workers, stressing that such information was essential for early detection and appropriate management. He also warned against unprotected contact with the blood and other body fluids of anyone suspected of having Ebola or another infectious disease. The NCDC urged organisers of religious gatherings, political rallies, concerts, festivals and sporting events to provide appropriate sanitation, safe drinking water and medical assistance, while ensuring prompt reporting of suspected infectious illnesses. Healthcare workers in public and private facilities were equally advised to maintain a high index of suspicion, observe infection prevention precautions and report suspected cases without delay. The agency further reminded inbound international travellers of the requirement to complete the Nigeria Health Declaration Form before arrival and provide accurate information about their health and travel history. “There is no reason for panic. What is required is continued vigilance, early reporting and cooperation with public health authorities,” Idris said. He commended President Bola Tinubu, the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare, the FCT health authorities, Port Health Services and national and international partners for supporting the response. He particularly acknowledged the private hospital in the FCT where the index patient initially received care, noting that its healthcare workers’ vigilance triggered the alert that led to the diagnosis. Idris said the experience had demonstrated the critical role of private healthcare facilities in disease detection and response, adding that collaboration between public and private health sectors remained essential to strengthening Nigeria’s health security. He also appreciated the 62 contacts and their families for complying with monitoring and quarantine requirements, describing their cooperation as central to the successful containment of potential transmission. items.title: From shoreline waste to useful products: How solar-powered recycling is helping communities rethink plastic waste in Ghana
items.description: An environmental non-governmental organisation, Plastic Punch, has partnered with Marco Bernardo, founder of Sun Factory, to demonstrate how solar energy can be used to convert plastic waste into useful products and create economic opportunities. The initiative was part of a two-week Sun Factory Residency, held from October 26 to November 7, which combined practical demonstrations, environmental education and community engagement. The programme began at the Plastic Punch office, where the team assembled a solar concentrator, a key component of the recycling system. The technology was subsequently used to demonstrate how discarded plastics could be repurposed using solar energy. At Street Academy, students participated in a live demonstration and discussions on plastic pollution, recycling, and sustainable waste management. The team later moved to Ada Foah, where it joined PROTEGO monitoring activities along the shoreline before engaging pupils of Tojeh Basic School in similar educational activities. Reflecting on his time in Ghana, Bernardo said the school engagements were particularly encouraging, citing the participation and enthusiasm of the communities. He also highlighted the economic potential of solar-powered recycling, explaining that the technology could reduce production costs by eliminating the need to purchase raw materials and pay for conventional energy. “In this case, you don’t pay for the material, you don’t pay for energy, and you can sell it. So, for me, it’s important that people see that recycling is more about creating jobs,” he said. Project Coordinator at Plastic Punch, Spencer Awortwi, said the residency had equipped the organisation with a practical tool for demonstrating the value of responsible plastic waste management. He noted that although the organisation did not consider recycling a complete solution to plastic pollution, using solar energy to transform plastic waste into attractive products could help change public attitudes towards waste disposal. As part of the residency, Bernardo and Plastic Punch Executive Director, Richmond Quarcoo, also visited the organisation’s developing Agumatsa Eco-Lodge near Wli Falls. There, the team demonstrated how recovered plastics could be transformed into products such as key holders. Plastic Punch members also received hands-on training in operating the technology to ensure the knowledge gained would remain within the organisation. The team further explored the use of locally available materials, including bamboo, to develop sustainable structures, with an early dome prototype. Speaking on the successful two-week residency, Quarcoo commended Marco Bernardo for his commitment to knowledge sharing and capacity building among Plastic Punch team members. “What I want to say about the Sun Factory is that, as an NGO, we are very excited to have Marco come to Ghana for a residency. It is important for the communities we serve, especially because most of them do not have access to electricity,” Quarcoo said. “…However, some of these communities are producing waste. And even those that do not use or create waste are facing problems with transboundary pollutants,” he added. He further emphasised that the Sun Factory Project is meant to show communities that they can create their own solutions to the challenges around them. “We want to be able to demonstrate this to them so that they can be inspired to create more to solve the challenges around them that we have,” Quarcoo noted. Meanwhile, the Agumatsa Eco-Lodge is being developed as an off-grid community facility between the Agumatsa River and Njeraki Stream. It is envisioned as a centre for practical skills training, technology, environmental education, and community-led innovation.

items.title: 2027: Obanikoro confident of Tinubu, Hamzat’s victory
items.description: Sen. Musiliu Obanikoro, a chieftain of the All Progressives Congress (APC), has expressed confidence that President Bola Tinubu and the party’s governorship candidate in Lagos State, Dr Obafemi Hamzat, will emerge victorious in the 2027 general elections. Obanikoro, Director-General, PBAT-KOH Campaign Council, Lagos State, gave the expressed this while speaking during the Lagos SWAGA 2.0 Summit and launch in Lagos, on Friday. He said the party was well positioned to win Lagos, adding that the achievements of the Tinubu administration at the federal level and those of the Lagos State Government had endeared the APC to the electorate. “We are confident of victory. President Tinubu has shown leadership, and Hamzat has the experience and capacity to sustain the progress of Lagos. “Lagos residents know what good governance looks like, and they will not gamble with their future “I commend the grassroots mobilisation and initiative of SWAGA 2.0 for mobilising supporters to this event venue. “With this great turnout, massive victory is assured for Tinubu and APC gubernatorial candidate, Dr Obafemi Hamzat, ” he said. Obanikoro tasked party members to intensify grassroots mobilisation and ensure the party delivered 3.5 million votes for Tinubu and Hamzat in the state He said the target was achievable if members remained united, disciplined and committed to the party’s campaign structure. “Our target is 3.5 million votes. It is not just a number, it is a statement that Lagos stands firmly behind Tinubu and Hamzat,” he said. He urged party leaders at ward and local government levels to take the campaign to every polling unit and engage voters on the party’s achievements. Obanikoro said the opposition lacked the structure and credibility to challenge the APC in Lagos, describing the party as the only party with a clear vision for the state and the country. He called on supporters to shun violence and conduct issue-based campaigns, stressing that the APC would win through performance, not intimidation. “We must campaign with our records. We must not engage in violence. Our victory will come from the people because they have seen what we have done,” he said. He assured supporters that the party leadership would provide the necessary support to ensure a hitch-free campaign and victory at the polls. The post 2027: Obanikoro confident of Tinubu, Hamzat’s victory appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: 95,000 PVCs uncollected in Plateau – INEC
items.description: The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), says more 95,000 Permanent Voters Cards (PVCs) have not been collected in Plateau. Prof. Samuel Egwu, the Resident Electoral Commissioner (REC) in the state, disclosed this during a press conference on Friday in Jos. The REC explained that the uncollected PVCs were largely for those who registered before the 2023 general elections. Egwu, who said that the commission was worried over the large number of unclaimed PVCs in the state, urged voters to take advantage of the ongoing distribution exercise to collect their PVCs. “More than 95,000 PVCs from 2023 were still with our Electoral Officers across the state. “We call on who those who registered before the last general elections to come and collect their PVCs to enable them participate in the 2027 general elections,”he advised. The REC said that PVCs from the first phase of the Continuous Voter Registration (CVR) exercise conducted between August and December 2025, were made available for collection at INEC offices across the 17 Local Government Areas (LGAs) of the state. He said particularly that the PVCs of Shendam, Langtang North, Jos South and Kanam, were now available for collection. “More than 19,000 PVCs for those who applied for transfers and corrections are also available for collection. “All PVCs for the second phase of CVR conducted between January and April, are available and have been taken to the 17 LGAs for collection. “PVCs for the third phase of CVR are not ready, but will be made available before the end of November for collection,”he said. Egwu also disclosed that all non-sensitive materials for the 2027 general elections were available at the INEC office in Jos and would soon be distributed to the 17 LGAs. He further said that training of electoral officers who were not trained in 2023 had commenced. The REC reiterated INEC’s readiness to conduct a credible election in 2027. The post 95,000 PVCs uncollected in Plateau – INEC appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Simandou Mining Summit : « Nous voulons mobiliser des investisseurs pour concrétiser le programme Simandou 2040 » (Aminata Bangoura)
items.description: La première édition du Simandou Mining Summit, organisée à Conakry du 11 au 14 novembre 2026, se poursuit avec la participation de décideurs et d’investisseurs issus de divers domaines, autour des programmes et des opportunités liés à Simandou 2040. Ce programme comprend 122 mégaprojets et 36 réformes répartis dans 14 secteurs prioritaires. Au programme de ce sommet figurent notamment la participation de plus de 2 000 personnes et l’organisation de plus de 3 000 rencontres d’affaires. L’objectif de ce sommet est de réunir les décideurs publics, les investisseurs, les institutions financières et les dirigeants d’entreprise afin de leur présenter les projets de la Guinée et d’examiner les possibilités de contribution à leur financement. Durant quatre jours, cet événement sera marqué par des discours des hautes autorités du pays, des panels, des rencontres d’affaires ainsi que des visites de terrain. Dans une interview accordée à la presse à l’occasion de la cérémonie d’ouverture, Aminata Bangoura, cheffe de cabinet du ministère des Mines et de la Géologie et porte-parole du Simandou Mining Summit, a souligné que la Guinée a, une fois de plus, démontré son sens de l’hospitalité. Elle est également revenue sur la particularité de ce sommet. « Chaque pays a ses priorités. Le Simandou Mining Summit est la plateforme officielle du gouvernement pour présenter le programme Simandou 2040. Notre objectif est de trouver des investisseurs qui puissent nous aider à mettre en œuvre ce programme. C’est ce qui distingue ce sommet des autres événements organisés en Guinée. Pour son organisation, nous nous sommes aussi inspirés de grands rendez-vous miniers internationaux ». Poursuivant son intervention, la porte-parole du sommet est revenue sur les raisons qui ont motivé le choix de l’île de Kassa pour accueillir la cérémonie d’ouverture. « Les premières exportations de bauxite sont parties de l’île de Kassa. Le choix de l’île s’est donc imposé à nous. C’était aussi l’occasion de faire découvrir les attraits touristiques de la Guinée et de montrer les merveilles de notre pays à nos invités étrangers. Du 11 au 14 novembre, le monde s’invite en Guinée et la Guinée reçoit le monde. C’est l’occasion de faire découvrir aux visiteurs nos sites touristiques, notre hospitalité et notre richesse culturelle », a-t-elle conclu. Mamadou Yaya Barry L’article Simandou Mining Summit : « Nous voulons mobiliser des investisseurs pour concrétiser le programme Simandou 2040 » (Aminata Bangoura) est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: 2027: How to secure victory for Tinubu, APC — Banire
items.description: A former legal adviser to the All Progressives Congress (APC), Dr Muiz Banire, has urged members of the South-West Agenda for Asiwaju (SWAGA) 2.0,a support group,to campaign aggressively with the achievements of President Bola Tinubu to secure victory for him. Banire,a former commissioner of transportation in Lagos,made the call during the SWAGA 2.0 Summit and official launch in Ikeja, on Friday. He said political rallies alone were not sufficient to secure electoral victory. The chieftain said there was need for sustained grassroots mobilisation and direct engagement with voters. According to him, campaigns should not be characterised by abuses, confrontation or unnecessary political arguments but should focus on educating the electorate about government policies, programmes and achievements. “Rallies are not what win elections. What wins elections is going from door to door, engaging the people and explaining to them what the government has achieved. “Campaigns should not be about abusing opponents or engaging in fights. They should be about educating the electorate and convincing voters with facts about the performance of the present administration,” he said. Banire urged SWAGA leadership to establish functional campaign teams across all wards, local government areas and local council development areas in the South-West to strengthen grassroots mobilisation. He advised the organisation to compile and coordinate information on registered All Progressives Congress (APC) voters in the various communities to facilitate effective voter engagement and mobilisation. “SWAGA must ensure that it has representatives in every ward and local government area. You must know your people, understand the voting strength in each locality and develop a strategy for reaching them. “Wherever members or campaign agents encounter challenges in the course of their assignments, they should report such issues to their respective leaders for prompt attention and necessary solutions,” he said. The former commissioner emphasised the importance of appointing competent and literate campaign agents who could communicate effectively with residents and provide accurate information about government policies and achievements. He added that campaign and party agents must be able to read, write and understand the issues they are expected to communicate to the electorate. Banire expressed confidence that the South-West would deliver at least 70 per cent of its votes to President Tinubu in the 2027 presidential election if party members remained committed to effective grassroots mobilisation. Banire mentioned some of the infrastructure projects and economic reforms undertaken by the Tinubu administration, including the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway and the Badagry-Sokoto Coastal Road, describing them as significant interventions capable of promoting economic growth and national development. He said the removal of fuel subsidy, although accompanied by economic difficulties for Nigerians, was part of broader efforts to redirect government resources towards national development, debt obligations and economic restructuring. “The subsidy removal has brought some hardship, but the resources saved are being channelled into developing the economy, addressing the nation’s debt burden and restructuring the economy. “We must continue to enlighten Nigerians on the reasons behind the reforms and the benefits expected from them. There is light at the end of the tunnel, and the people should not lose hope,” he said. He urged SWAGA members to remain committed, organised and consistent in communicating the administration’s achievements. The chieftain said that credible information and direct interaction with voters would be critical to securing electoral support in 2027. items.title: Nigerian university in mourning after four students die at post-exam party
items.description: Four Nigerian students have died after attending a party in the south-eastern town of Nsukka to celebrate the end of their final exams. The cause of death has not been confirmed, but police spokesman Daniel Ndukwe said the two men and two women had reportedly fallen ill after consuming alcoholic drinks at the party. The University of Nigeria, Nsukka has declared three days of mourning, during which academic and social activities will be suspended. The tragedy comes amid a wider crackdown on fake and adulterated alcoholic drinks in Nigeria, where the food and drug regulator has been raiding suspected producers of unsafe food and beverages. The university’s Vice-Chancellor, Professor Simon Ortuanya, said the university had received a distress call at 22:00 on Wednesday, and sent security personnel to a house party at Praise Lodge, outside the campus in Nsukka’s Hilltop area. “The preliminary investigation and interim report point to alleged alcohol abuse or drug paraphernalia and things like that. But we are not conclusive on those matters,” he said. He described the deaths as “tragic and painful”. “As a community, we mourn, not just alone; we mourn with the families, the parents that have suffered these years to train the men and women in their studies,” he said. Ortuanya also announced a ban on signing-out celebrations, which are commonly held by final-year students to mark the completion of their studies. The celebrations often involve parties, dancing, photographs and friends signing one another’s shirts. He urged students to use graduation as a time to reflect on their university experience and prepare for life beyond campus. The university said it was working with security agencies to establish what had caused the deaths. The police have also launched an investigation. They said alcoholic drinks had been recovered from the scene and the bodies taken to a mortuary for autopsies. The investigation comes amid wider concerns about unsafe alcoholic drinks in Nigeria. In September, dozens of people fell ill after consuming locally made alcoholic drinks and herbal mixtures in communities across Ondo State, south-west Nigeria. More than 11 people died in the Araromi-Obu area, while more than 50 others were hospitalised. Investigations found that some of the drinks had been contaminated with methanol, a highly toxic form of alcohol that can cause blindness and death. Nigeria’s food and drug regulator, Nafdac, reported more than 150 cases, including 48 confirmed deaths. More than 80 people were hospitalised, and five lost their sight. The regulator has been carrying out raids across the country, targeting facilities suspected of producing fake or adulterated alcoholic drinks, food and beverages. Nigeria has long struggled with the sale of unsafe and adulterated products, which campaigners warn pose a serious threat to public health.

items.title: COP has a guest-list problem
items.description: “The entire conversation around climate change was, ‘Pakistan…it’s Pakistan now, but the world next,’ 23-year-old Maryam Jamali recalls. “But no one from those communities was present at COP.” Co-founder of Madat Balochistan, a women and indigenous-led grassroots organisation dedicated to rehabilitating communities affected by climate change, Jamali became a climate activist during the catastrophic floods of 2022. As her family and community members faced its devastation, Jamali used phone calls to coordinate relief efforts in Sindh and Balochistan. It soon became apparent to her, however, that her work was akin to putting a bandaid on a gunshot wound. The communities at the forefront of climate disasters could not just be passive recipients of reactive relief work, she realized. They should have the leverage to determine what prevention, recovery and rehabilitation means for them before catastrophe strikes their homes and fields. A view of a crossing flooded after rains in Lasbela district. Moved by her experience, Jamali decided to apply for participation in the 27th edition of United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) COP, scheduled to be held in Sharm el-Sheikh, Egypt in November that year. It proved to be a challenge and she soon realized, she wasn’t experientially equipped enough to navigate the bureaucratic process and international networks that could support her accreditation and funding. She didn’t give up. She applied for COP28, and then, again, for COP29. On this attempt, she managed to secure a conference badge with the help of a friend through a sponsoring organisation. COP29 took place in Baku, Azerbaijan and Jamali soon ran into a funding issue. She turned to online fundraising for support, but of the USD 2500 required at the time for the trip, Jamali was only able to raise USD 2000 (approximately PKR 555,600 in 2024). Jamali is not the only one who ran into this wall. Aitzaz Roonjha is an 18-year-old climate activist from Lasbela, Balochistan. He began work in 2022 by joining WANG (Welfare Association for New Generation), a youth-led organisation, which worked on flood relief and recovery in Balochistan. Madat Balochistan holds al camp to raise awareness about climate change in affected communites. Last year, Roonjha applied and was selected to attend COP30, but he couldn’t make it because the selection did not include financial assistance. He reached out to many organisations and international groups he had worked with previously but couldn’t secure enough funding to cover travel, accommodation, and visa costs. And travel costs are not the only problem. Attending international climate conferences, Jamali says, often hinges on personal connections and organisational affiliations. “It’s a very, very secretive process,” she says. She noted that activists from major cities and more privileged, urban backgrounds managed to gain greater access to these international forums than people who are practically on the frontlines of climate catastrophes. “These climate forums are inaccessible to working class people or actual climate affectees who are experiencing climate change on the ground,” she says. Volunteers from WANG engaged in relief work Roonjha says WANG provided a foundation for his work through which he gained hands-on experience, began pursuing further opportunities, and earned recognition. “Even with my experience in climate work and the backing of an organization, I still couldn’t make it to the COP,” he says. “Aspiring to attend COP and actually being able to attend COP are two very different things.” The money and the badge Many young climate activists work in an individual capacity in their communities since structural funding is hard to come by, so they have to rely on more recognized climate organizations to access major forums like COP. Durlabh Ashok, founding director of Climate Forward Pakistan (CFP), a leading youth-led climate organisation that sends delegations to COP every year, says the organisation offers limited financial assistance to its delegates. It supports delegates through subsidised accommodation, accreditation assistance, and speaking opportunities, while delegates are normally supposed to pay for their own travel, meal, and other expenses. “We don’t want to operate as a grant-driven organisation because that inevitably gives us inherent clout over funding decisions,” Ashok says. However, the model leaves delegates responsible for taking the financial obligations of the participation. Applicants may be ascertained on the basis of their climate related work and the familiarity with the UNFCCC procedure, but they must also showcase that they can fund their participation either on their own or through sponsorship. Climate activists from underrepresented communities often deal with additional impediments of participation. A person with years of grassroots experience supporting climate-hit communities which are on the frontlines of climate disasters find it difficult to access the networks of these organisations compared to their counterparts operating from more urban settings. This year, for example, of the cohort selected by CFP, only one activist from Balochistan made the cut. While admitting the challenge, Ashok says that CFP seeks to keep the COP route accessible by providing necessary documentation to delegates in order to approach potential sponsors while assisting them with logistical arrangements, including visas and accreditation. There is no restriction on paper, just between the lines There is no explicit requirement under UNFCCC rules for climate activists to come from an urban or privileged background. For NGO observers, participation generally takes place through organisations that have been conferred observer status, which then nominate delegates within their allocated quotas. Travel, meal and accommodation are not particular requirements for securing observer status, but they still can determine whether a nominated delegate can turn their formal selection into actual participation. An aerial view shows a flooded residential area in Balochistan province. The UNFCCC has also noted concerns regarding geographical diversity and representation in observer participation. The UNFCCC has admitted the financial obstacles confronted by observer organisations from marginalized communities and developing countries and has planned to explore ways to facilitate broader participation. Currently, there is no specific funds generally available to observer organisations as compared to the Trust Fund for Participation that provides financial assistance only to the representatives of developing country Parties. Even those who eventually make it to the COP as representatives of observer status do not have the same negotiating impactful role as country negotiators. Observer organisations can participate in supplementary events, deliberations, campaignings, networkings, while official negotiations come within the domain of Country Parties. You’ve made it! Now what? But, suppose, a young climate activist somehow jumps through all the hoops: they arrange the funds, navigate the system, get accreditation, and manage to reach the conference, what happens then? Irfan Azad succeeded in making it to the climate conference in 2025. His climate works started during the 2022 floods. He collected donations, coordinated relief efforts and ran volunteer medical camps. After a survey of over 1,000 homes, he started to focus on and set up Salahuddin Academy in his village, Goth Salahauddin Pandrani in Jaffarabad District, for 100 children. He began to wonder and question why communities are continuously vulnerable to similar disasters such as major floods in 2008, 2010, 2012 and then 2022 even after taking big pledges every year in global climate summits. He was selected to attend COP30 through Climate Forward Pakistan (CFP), however, he was required to submit $2,200 (approximately PKR 620,448 at the time) for the trip. Jamali, who had managed to collect a sizable amount in her previous fundraising efforts, was happy to add to Azad’s pool. Azad with other members of his cohort at COP30 held in Brazil. “I arrived in Brazil with meagre cash, no ATM card and limited preparation in order to navigate an unfamiliar language and a foreign country,” he says. Azad initially had access to the Green Zone — a space managed by UNFCC which is open to the general public— while receiving entry to the Blue Zone — where the formal negotiations take place under the management of the host country — only during the final days of the conference. Azad spent much of his time talking with global indigenous communities in the Green Zone and hearing about their experiences regarding climate change, while climate negotiations went on among world leaders, disconnected from the affectees right outside their door. To Azad, it became obvious that even being in the room did not guarantee a seat at the table. COP31 is currently underway in Antalya, Türkiye.

items.title: Premier League : Mauricio Pochettino prend les commandes de Manchester United
items.description: Manchester United a annoncé vendredi la nomination de l'Argentin Mauricio Pochettino au poste d'entraîneur principal, en remplacement de Michael Carrick, limogé la veille après un début de saison difficile en Premier League. Le club mancunien a précisé, dans un communiqué, avoir conclu un accord avec la Fédération américaine de football (US Soccer) pour permettre au technicien argentin et à son équipe de quitter leurs fonctions à la tête de la sélection des États-Unis, une fois leurs engagements achevés. Actuellement sélectionneur des États-Unis, Pochettino (54 ans) dirigera ses deux dernières rencontres avec la sélection américaine face à Haïti, samedi et mardi, dans le cadre de la Ligue des nations de la Concacaf, avant de rejoindre Manchester la semaine prochaine, rapportent des médias britanniques. Il devrait faire ses débuts sur le banc des Red Devils le 22 novembre, lors du déplacement à Liverpool en championnat. Cette nomination intervient alors que Manchester United occupe la 18e place de la Premier League, avec une seule victoire en dix rencontres. Le club avait annoncé jeudi le départ de Michael Carrick, invoquant la nécessité d'un changement après un début de saison décevant. Nommé initialement en janvier 2026, Carrick avait permis à Manchester United de terminer troisième du championnat précédent, avant d'être confirmé dans ses fonctions jusqu'en 2028. Pochettino retrouve ainsi la Premier League, où il a notamment conduit Tottenham en finale de la Ligue des champions en 2019. Il a également remporté le championnat de France et la Coupe de France avec le Paris Saint-Germain.
