items.title: NDC attack: NYCN warns Lagos youths against political thuggery
items.description: The National Youth Council of Nigeria (NYCN), Lagos State Chapter, has warned youths against allowing themselves to be recruited or manipulated into political thuggery. The youth organisation gave the warning following the attack on supporters of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) during a town hall meeting in Lagos. The council’s Chairman,Ibrahim Adigun, spoke with the interview with the News Agency of Nigeria on Friday in Lagos. Adigun said no amount of financial inducement or promise of political patronage was worth the life, freedom or future of any young person. He urged Lagos youths to recognise their importance as stakeholders in the democratic process and channel their energies towards peaceful political participation, civic responsibility and nation-building. “No amount of financial inducement or promise of political patronage is worth a life, a criminal record or a future destroyed. “As young people, we must recognise that we are stakeholders in the democratic process and we should channel our energy towards peaceful participation, civic responsibility and nation-building. “For emphasis, the NYCN Lagos State Chapter maintains its unequivocal opposition to political thuggery, electoral violence and every form of intimidation,” he said. Adigun said the council would continue to advocate peaceful political participation, responsible youth engagement and an electoral environment where every citizen could freely express their political choices without fear. He described the attack on NDC supporters as a serious threat to democratic participation, peaceful political engagement and the safety of citizens. According to him, political differences, no matter how deeply held, must never be settled through violence, intimidation or destruction of property. He expressed sympathy with those injured or otherwise affected by the incident, particularly young people, and wished them a speedy and full recovery. The NYCN chairman urged the relevant authorities to identify and bring those responsible for the attack to justice. He also appealed to political parties, candidates and their supporters to embrace civility and tolerance as political activities ahead of the 2027 general elections gathered momentum. “Campaigns should be driven by ideas, policies, track records and credible alternatives capable of addressing the concerns of Nigerians, particularly young people,” he said. Adigun called on security agencies, particularly the Lagos State Police Command, to strengthen security arrangements around political gatherings and other public events. He urged the agencies to remain professional, impartial and proactive in identifying potential threats, preventing attacks and protecting lives and property, irrespective of political affiliations. The chairman also reiterated the council’s commitment to opposing political thuggery, electoral violence and all forms of intimidation. The attack reportedly occurred at about 11:00 a.m. on Thursday when suspected political thugs, armed with cutlasses, cudgels, stones and other dangerous weapons, invaded Classique Event Place, Oregun, where NDC supporters had gathered for a town hall meeting. The meeting was organised ahead of the expected arrival of the party’s presidential candidate, Mr Peter Obi, and his running mate, Sen. Rabiu Kwankwaso, to engage party supporters and stakeholders ahead of the 2027 general elections. Accounts of some eyewitnesses indicated that the attackers stormed the venue as participants were preparing for the meeting, triggering pandemonium and forcing supporters and journalists to flee for safety. items.title: Ondo APC assures of unity, readiness for 2027 elections
items.description: The Ondo State chapter of the All Progressives Congress (APC) says it is united and committed to securing victory for President Bola Tinubu and other candidates in the 2027 general elections. The APC State Chairman, Mr Babatunde Kolawole, said this on Friday in Akure at a news conference organised by the party. Kolawole also dismissed concerns over alleged internal divisions, saying reconciliation efforts were yielding positive results with no exclusion of any member. He dismissed claims of rivalry among party leaders, insisting that members belonged to the same political family and should not regard one another as opponents. According to him, there is no basis for rivalry, particularly as there won’t be governorship election in Ondo in 2027 while President Tinubu has emerged as the party’s sole presidential candidate. “Therefore, there is no rivalry. There is no cause for alarm. I can assure you we are on top of it and everything will be okay,” he said. The chairman appreciated Tinubu and the APC National Chairman for their support, while commending the Senate Leader, Sen. Michael Opeyemi Bamidele, and other party members for their contributions to the success of the presidential campaign. Also, Mr Victor Olabimtan, Director-General, State APC Presidential Campaign Council, said the reconciliation committee constituted after the party congress had reached out to party organs, interest groups and individuals across the country. Olabimtan said the committee had visited Abuja to engage some party leaders, while others were contacted in Lagos and different parts of the country. “We had Mr Wale Akinterinwa and Princess Oladunni Odu at the recent presidential campaign rally in the state as evidence of progress in the reconciliation process. “Nobody is left out. All we need to do is to ensure that we put more effort into strengthening the existing unity that we are all enjoying in the party today. “So, there is no cause for alarm. As we make progress, you will also see that our efforts, the efforts of the governor, the party and its leaders are indeed yielding fruits to ensure that everybody is brought on board,” he said. Similarly, state Commissioner for Women Affairs, Dr Seun Osamaye, pledged the support of women across the state for Tinubu’s re-election, saying collective mobilisation was essential to achieving the party’s one million votes target. items.title: Poursuites pour faits de terrorisme: De Paul-Henri Damiba à François Compaoré et France 24, le Burkina dévoile la liste officielle des suspects et des entités visés
items.description: Dans une déclaration liminaire accompagnée d'un récapitulatif officiel des poursuites, le Procureur Général près la Cour d'appel de Ouagadougou, M. SAWADOGO Désiré Pinguédewindé, a dressé le bilan des dossiers en cours d'instruction devant le Pôle judiciaire spécialisé dans la répression des actes de terrorisme. Révélant les identités des prévenus et des entités morales poursuivis parmi lesquels figurent l'ancien président Paul-Henri Sandaogo Damiba, Paul François Compaoré, l'activiste Yacouba Aladj Bama ainsi que le média France 24, le ministère public a réaffirmé sa résolution à conduire ces procédures à terme. S'appuyant formellement sur la Résolution 1373 du Conseil de sécurité de l'ONU et l'article 8 de la Convention de l'OUA de 1999, la justice républicaine réclame la coopération internationale pour l'exécution des mandats d'arrêt et des procédures d'extradition. Le Parquet général près la Cour d'appel de Ouagadougou a rendu publique la liste des personnes contre lesquelles une instruction est actuellement ouverte pour des faits de terrorisme. Le récapitulatif officiel recense des profils variés comprenant d'anciens dirigeants, des civils, des activistes et des médias : DAMIBA Paul Henry Sandaogo : poursuivi pour complicité d'association de malfaiteurs terroristes, complicité de détention d'armes et complicité de financement du terrorisme (Code pénal et loi n°016-2016/AN). COMPAORE Paul François : poursuivi pour complicité d'association de malfaiteurs terroristes et financement du terrorisme (Code pénal et loi n°46-2024/ALT). DIALLO Ousmane Moumouni Raouni et Maturin Serges : poursuivis pour complicité d'association terroriste, détention d'armes et financement. ZERBO Laoko Mohamed et SAWADOGO Abdoul Karim : poursuivis pour complicité d'association de malfaiteurs terroristes. BAMA Yacouba Aladj : poursuivi pour apologie du terrorisme sous l'article 361-19 du Code pénal. SOME Maixent et OUEDRAOGO Aminata alias Aminata Rachow : poursuivis pour complicité d'association et apologie du terrorisme. France24 : visée en tant que personne morale pour complicité d'association de malfaiteurs terroristes et complicité d'apologie du terrorisme. Les juges du Pôle spécialisé appliquent une grille de lecture juridique particulièrement stricte. Les faits reprochés s'appuient sur les articles 131-4, 131-5, 131-8, 316-1, 361-2, 361-3, 361-19, 361-23, 362-1 et 362-2 du Code pénal. S'y ajoutent les dispositions des lois financières sur la lutte contre le blanchiment et le financement du terrorisme (loi n°016-2016/AN du 3 mai 2016 et loi n°46-2024/ALT du 30 décembre 2024). Pour assurer le rapatriement des personnes résidant à l'étranger, le Procureur Général fonde son action sur les engagements internationaux des États tiers. Dans sa déclaration officielle, M. SAWADOGO Désiré Pinguédewindé (Officier de l'Ordre de l'Étalon) rappelle que la Résolution 1373 du 28 septembre 2001 du Conseil de sécurité de l'ONU fait obligation à tous les États de criminaliser le financement du terrorisme, de geler les avoirs financiers et de refuser l'asile aux suspects. De surcroît, le ministère public invoque l'article 8 de la Convention de l'Union Africaine (OUA) de 1999 sur la prévention et la lutte contre le terrorisme, lequel stipule que « les parties s'engagent à extrader toute personne poursuivie, inculpée ou condamnée pour des actes de terrorisme commis dans un autre État partie et dont l'extradition est sollicitée par cet État » . Le Parquet général conclut en exprimant le ferme espoir que les mandats d'arrêt et demandes d'extradition connaîtront des suites utiles dans le respect des droits fondamentaux des prévenus. L’article Poursuites pour faits de terrorisme: De Paul-Henri Damiba à François Compaoré et France 24, le Burkina dévoile la liste officielle des suspects et des entités visés est apparu en premier sur NetAfrique.net .

items.title: IMF praises economy, says macroeconomic stability is now becoming entrenched
items.description: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) has praised the Ghanaian economy, saying the growth rate has exceeded expectations. According to the Director of Communications, Julie Kozack, Ghana’s macroeconomic stability is now becoming entrenched, with the indicators pointing in the right direction. ” Ghana’s macroeconomic stability is now becoming entrenched, and our engagement with the authorities is now shifting from crisis response, which was really the focus of the previous programme, to supporting a consolidation of reforms and the building of longer-term resilience in the country”. “We’ve also seen that Ghana’s economy has improved significantly. We’ve seen growth exceed expectations. Growth was 6.0 percent last year, and we project it at 5.7 percent this year. Ghana’s external position has strengthened. Its debt has fallen. Its debt-to-GDP ratio is now around 50 percent, and inflation is now in the single digits”, she added. She continued that the fiscal position in Ghana is now strong, and the primary surplus is on track to meet the year-end targets. She also expressed happiness that Ghana has a very strong ownership of the reform programme that has been critical to ensuring it has been implemented. “It has been a homegrown programme which we have supported”. “We’ve also seen a willingness by the authorities to undertake some very difficult policy decisions. The programme, the previous programme, was implemented in very difficult circumstances, but the authorities took the difficult decisions at that time, and those are now bearing fruit, as I said, in terms of stability and the strength of the economy”, Dr. Kozack said. Social Dialogue She also praised the government for its social dialogue, saying it held lots of engagement with key stakeholders on reforms, feedback and broader priorities for the country. “And that has all helped to build support for the difficult reforms that the country had to take. And so that’s, I think, another key lesson is the importance of broader societal engagement, which was also done in Ghana”. She concluded that there is light at the end of the tunnel.

items.title: Benue APC Campaign Council rejects Akume-led coalition for Tinubu’s re-election
items.description: ..alleges plot against Alia’s re-election By Peter Duru, Makurdi Benue State All Progressives Congress, APC, Tinubu/Alia Campaign Council, has opposed the emergence of the Senator George Akume-led Strategic Alliance for Tinubu/Shettima Re-election 2027, alleging that the group is being used as a platform to undermine Governor Hyacinth Alia’s political fortunes ahead of the 2027 governorship election. The party expressed concern over the involvement of some prominent APC chieftains, including Secretary to the Government of the Federation, Senator George Akume, and Minister of Water Resources and Sanitation, Professor Joseph Utsev, in the alliance, which it claimed also accommodates opposition figures and governorship candidates. The Director-General of the Tinubu/Alia 2027 Campaign Council in Benue State, Citizen Richard Asema, stated the party’s position during a press briefing insisting that the alliance was unnecessary and could create divisions within the APC while threatening its electoral prospects in the state. Asema said, “The Benue State Chapter of All Progressives Congress (APC) views with serious concern the purported formation of the ‘Strategic Alliance For Tinubu/Shettima Re-election 2027’ by some political individuals and groups and the subsequent announcement of a Campaign Council for the re-election of our dear President, Bola Ahmed Tinubu. “The Party observes that this ‘Strategic Alliance’ is populated by some members of the APC, some of whom are holding senior positions in the Federal Government of Nigeria, including Senator George Akume, Secretary to Government of the Federation (SGF) and Prof Joseph Utsev, Hon. Minister of Water Resources and Sanitation. “A critical look at the membership of this so-called Campaign Council reveals that governorship candidates of other political parties, especially the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) and Labour Party (LP), as well as officers of some other minority parties, are members of the Group and its ‘Campaign Council’. “The APC in Benue State under the leadership of Rev Fr Hyacinth Alia and the Chairmanship of Benjamin Omale, wishes to strongly reject this purported Strategic Alliance and its Campaign Council. “This Council, to say the least, is contemptuous and injurious to the fortunes of APC and its electioneering machinery in the state as being coordinated by His Excellency, Rev Fr Dr Hyacinth Alia. “From all credible intelligence available to the party, this Strategic Alliance has a hidden agenda, which is to sabotage the election of Rev Fr Hyacinth Alia in the 2027 elections, while masquerading as supporters of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu. “The APC in Benue State recently constituted a comprehensive Campaign Council with over 900 loyal and credible party leaders as members. In fact, most members of the so-called Strategic Alliance were appointed into the Council, which was publicly inaugurated on Thursday, 5th November at the IBB Square, Makurdi. “Soon after the Council membership was announced, these same persons hastily declared that they won’t participate in the activities of the Council. “It is regrettable that some APC members have fallen prey to this political gimmick by allowing themselves to be used for this act of political mischief. “We wish to state unequivocally that Benue State is fundamentally and evidentially a strong base of the APC. The party is well grounded, popular and loved by the people of Benue State. By God’s grace, APC will win the 2027 elections decisively with a higher margin of votes than it did in 2023. He noted that in the 2023 elections, the party not only won the governorship seat but also delivered President Bola Tinubu and secured two of the three senatorial seats stressing that today, it controls 27 of 32 State Assembly seats, 10 of 11 House of Representatives seats, 23 Local Government Chairmanship positions and all 276 elected councillorship seats across the state. The Director-General insisted that Governor Alia’s achievements in infrastructure, industrial development, job creation and education, including the employment of 9,700 teachers, had further boosted his popularity. “His prompt payment of salaries and pensions, alongside the clearance of outstanding arrears, has also strengthened public confidence in his administration. “APC doesn’t need any alliance to win the 2027 elections and hereby warns against any attempt to confuse the teeming members of the party and the good people of Benue State, who are already poised to vote for the party at the forthcoming elections. “From the foregoing, we advise APC members in the Strategic Alliance to disengage forthwith, retrace their steps and regroup with the mainstream leadership of the Party under Governor Hyacinth Alia.” The Campaign Council vowed to deliver victory for President Tinubu and Governor Alia in the forthcoming polls. The post Benue APC Campaign Council rejects Akume-led coalition for Tinubu’s re-election appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Maroquinerie : Les produits du Niger et du Mali à l’honneur
items.description: Le Niger et le Mali, pays invités spéciaux, du SIAO 2026 ont aussi exposé leurs créations en maroquinerie. Les deux pays invités spéciaux du SIAO, à savoir le Niger et le Mali, ont honoré leur présence à travers plusieurs activités dont les expositions- vente de leurs produits de maroquinerie. A entendre Lawali Abdou du Village artisanal de Wadata à Niamey, la maroquinerie au Niger repose sur un riche savoir-faire artisanal des peuples tamasheq (Touareg), haoussa et woodabe. Il a ajouté que les principaux produits de maroquinerie sont des poufs et coussins en cuir : Grands classiques de l'artisanat nigérien, souvent ornés de motifs floraux ou régionaux, produits historiquement et actuellement dans les centres artisanaux. Selon Lawali Abdou du Village artisanal de Wadata, la maroquinerie nigérienne repose sur un riche savoir-faire artisanal En plus de cela, il y a des chaussures, des portefeuilles, ceintures et autres. La maroquinerie au Mali a aussi un savoir-faire artisanal ancestral transmis de génération en génération, particulièrement centré à Bamako autour de la Maison des artisans. La gamme de créations exposé sont composé de Sacs à main, portefeuilles, ceintures, chaussures, pochettes, cartables et porte-documents. Les matières utilisées sont des cuirs locaux (vache, mouton, chèvre) mais aussi, traditionnellement, de peaux de reptiles (serpent, varan, crocodile, caïman). Le cuir est parfois associé au bogolan. Evariste YODA

items.title: Kozah : Un colloque scientifique à l’UK aborde la problématique de l’eau dans la région
items.description: Kara, 13 nov. (ATOP) – Un colloque scientifique axé sur la problématique de l’eau dans la région de la Kara s’est ouvert le jeudi 12 novembre à l’Université de Kara (UK). Ce colloque régional, à l’actif de l’UK, est placé sous le thème « La problématique de l’eau dans la région de la Kara : quelle approche de gestion pour une stabilité durable de l’eau potable ? ». Il intervient dans un contexte marqué par des difficultés récurrentes d’accès à l’eau potable dans la ville de Kara et ses environs, particulièrement durant les mois de janvier et février. Durant trois jours, des enseignants-chercheurs, des professionnels du secteur de l’eau, des responsables institutionnels et des partenaires vont échanger autour des défis liés à la disponibilité, à l’accessibilité et à la gestion durable de l’eau potable. Ils vont élaborer un plan stratégique régional de gestion des ressources en eau, assorti de recommandations scientifiques, techniques et opérationnelles. L’objectif est de formuler des recommandations stratégiques susceptibles de contribuer à l’amélioration de l’approvisionnement afin de faire face à la croissance démographique, l’extension urbaine, la pression sur les ressources hydriques et aux effets de la variabilité climatique. Six thématiques seront abordées. Trois portent sur le diagnostic des ressources en eau ; les solutions alternatives et innovantes d’approvisionnement et la qualité de l’eau et les risques sanitaires. La performance des infrastructures d’adduction ; la gouvernance des services de l’eau, les dynamiques sociales liées aux usages et à l’accès à cette ressource, sont d’autres thématiques à aborder. Le directeur national de la recherche scientifique et technique, Dr. Kossi Sénamé Dodzi, a relevé le rôle de la recherche scientifique dans la résolution des défis hydriques. Il a réaffirmé l’engagement du gouvernement à soutenir les initiatives de recherche-action susceptibles d’éclairer les politiques publiques et de favoriser une gestion durable de l’eau. Pour le président du comité d’organisation, Prof. Alpha Issaka Sambo Falay, doyen de la Faculté des sciences et techniques de l’UK, ce colloque traduit la volonté de l’institution universitaire d’apporter sa contribution à une meilleure gouvernance de cette denrée importante Le directeur de la planification, des études et des travaux à la Société de patrimoine eau et assainissement (SP-EAU), Djibril Soulemana Hamissou, a rappelé les actions engagées par l’Etat pour améliorer la desserte en eau potable dans la région. Il a cité le projet d’alimentation en eau potable à partir de la rivière Sara dans l’Assoli qui a été lancé en septembre dernier, ainsi que d’autres projets en cours d’identification. Le professeur Assogba Guezere, directeur de la recherche et de l’inondation, a souligné la nécessité d’une approche pluridisciplinaire pour répondre aux enjeux liés à l’eau. « Le plan stratégique attendu servira d’outil d’aide à la décision aux autorités et orientera les interventions en faveur d’un approvisionnement régulier et durable en eau potable », a-t-il précisé. Le gouverneur de la région de la Kara, général de brigade, Adjitowou Komlan a assisté à la cérémonie d’ouverture. ATOP/AE/TAL/BA

items.title: Terrorisme et financement : François Compaoré, petit frère de l’ancien président Blaise Compaoré formellement poursuivi par le Burkina Faso
items.description: Déjà au centre de plusieurs procédures judiciaires, Paul François Compaoré, frère cadet de l'ancien président Blaise Compaoré, figure officiellement parmi les personnalités poursuivies dans le cadre des dossiers de terrorisme instruits à Ouagadougou. Selon le document récapitulatif du Parquet général près la Cour d'appel de Ouagadougou, l'instruction en cours retient contre lui des faits de complicité d’association de malfaiteurs terroristes et de financement du terrorisme. La justice burkinabè invoque à son encontre non seulement le Code pénal, mais également les dispositions de la nouvelle loi n°46-2024/ALT adoptée fin 2024 pour réprimer le blanchiment, le financement du terrorisme et la prolifération des armes de destruction massive. Les affaires judiciaires entourant les anciennes figures politiques burkinabè s'enrichissent d'un nouveau chapitre répressif. Le Parquet du Procureur Général près la Cour d'appel de Ouagadougou a inscrit Paul François Compaoré sur la liste des personnes physiques soumises à une instruction pénale active pour des faits à connotation terroriste. Le frère cadet de l'ancien chef d'État Blaise Compaoré se voit appliquer les procédures réservées aux atteintes graves à la sécurité de l'État et à la sûreté publique. Les poursuites engagées contre François Compaoré s’articulent autour de deux infractions majeures : La complicité d'association de malfaiteurs terroristes ; Le financement du terrorisme. Sur le plan du droit, le ministère public fait application des réformes légales les plus récentes. Outre les articles 131-4, 131-5, 131-8, 316-1, 361-2, 361-3, 361-23, 362-1 et 362-2 du Code pénal, les juges s'appuient sur les articles 1, 2, 10, 188, 189, 190, 191, 196, 200, 203 et suivants de la loi n°46-2024/ALT du 30 décembre 2024. Ce texte législatif régit spécifiquement la lutte contre le blanchiment des capitaux, le financement du terrorisme et la prolifération des armes de destruction massive au Burkina Faso. items.title: Forget building another ChatGPT; Ghana must focus on AI solutions for healthcare, agric – GradePoint AI CEO
items.description: Founder and Chief Executive Officer of GradePoint AI, Dr Gillian Hammah, has cautioned the government against investing heavily in attempts to develop its own large artificial intelligence models, arguing that the country should instead adapt existing technologies to solve local problems. She believes Ghana’s limited financial resources make competing with global AI developers an expensive undertaking that could divert attention from more pressing national needs. Speaking at the Step Up Executive Breakfast Series, Dr Hammah said Ghana does not need to build another ChatGPT but should concentrate on developing smaller, specialised AI models tailored to the country’s needs. “We don’t need to build our own ChatGPT,” she said, arguing that the country should leverage existing large language models and customise them for specific local applications. She explained that such models, known as Small Language Models (SLMs), can be adapted using specialised datasets to address challenges in particular sectors. Using healthcare as an example, she said the Ministry of Health could develop an AI model trained on Ghana’s health data while benefiting from the capabilities and training of existing larger models. “The Ministry of Health, for example, is deciding that they’re going to build a model that has our health data, but it has all the benefits and the training from the bigger models. That’s what we need,” she explained. Dr Hammah argued that this approach would allow Ghana to benefit from advances in AI without committing the enormous financial resources required to develop entirely new large language models. She said the country should instead direct its attention towards practical applications in healthcare, agriculture and food production. “For us to try and be another ChatGPT, we’re wasting our time. Let us try and start solving the problems that are relevant to us today,” she stressed. She further argued that developing the biggest AI model should not be Ghana’s priority when the technology could be deployed to address everyday challenges affecting citizens. “And building the biggest model is not it. Solving our problems day to day, health, food, agriculture, that’s where we need to start,” she said. Dr Hammah also identified poor data management as a major obstacle to Ghana’s AI ambitions, calling for a nationwide exercise to digitise and harmonise government records. She believes reliable and accessible data would provide the foundation for developing specialised AI applications that respond to the country’s needs. The discussion formed part of the Step Up Executive Breakfast Series held under the theme, “The AI-Powered Project Leader: How to Lead, Deliver & Stay Relevant in the Age of AI.”

items.title: Nvidia fallout throws spotlight on Southeast Asia’s AI boom
items.description: Southeast Asia’s chip and data centre industries expect greater scrutiny after news of former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s affair with a suspected Chinese spy put the spotlight on Singapore and Malaysia, executives and analysts said. US lawmakers from both parties are pushing for tougher restrictions on China’s access to advanced artificial intelligence chips after the Huang scandal increased scrutiny of Nvidia’s role in US national security. Washington restricts exports to China of Nvidia’s most advanced AI chips to protect US dominance of the sector, but lawmakers want to close a loophole that allows Chinese firms to rent computing power from overseas data centres and access the systems equipped with the chips remotely. Tougher regulations could include new export rules and licensing requirements to Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Singapore, the Wall Street Journal reported . The alleged spy, Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang , was an executive at a cloud computing firm in Singapore called Megaspeed that has subsidiaries in Thailand, Indonesia, Malaysia, Australia and the US. Megaspeed has been under investigation by Singapore authorities since February last year for potential false declarations in relation to the purchase of servers and other related offences. “After this case, every operator in the chain will be expected to know its end user. Southeast Asian operators will still get Nvidia chips, but proof of where every chip sits and who it serves is now part of the product,” said Ke Yan, head of research at Singapore-based investment research firm Shenton Research. ‘Post-DeepSeek moment’ Southeast Asia’s data centre industry is thriving. Since 2021, Malaysia has approved 385.7 billion ringgit ($94.67 billion) of data centre-related investments in the country, according to the trade ministry, while Thailand has 42 data centres, representing 3,400 MW of IT load and about 750bn baht ($22.58bn) in investment as of February. Indonesia’s data centre market was valued at $2.81bn in 2025. Gary Goh, CEO of Malaysia-based data centre consultancy Sprint DC, likened the current situation to a “ post-DeepSeek moment ”. “Once the new rules are out, there will be a lot more restrictions for countries like Malaysia. There could be a short- to medium-term market shock to the Malaysian data centre market,” said Goh. The AI boom has boosted the region, with Singapore in August raising its economic growth forecast to 4.5 per cent to 5.5pc this ​year, from 2.0pc-4.0pc, citing the AI cycle. In Malaysia, rising data centre development projects pushed the construction sector up 6pc in the third quarter of 2026. Singapore’s and Malaysia’s trade ministries did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Malaysia on Thursday said it was weighing a law that will allow the government to monitor data centre operations, including their use of high-performance chips, saying it needed to ensure that any chips subject to US restrictions were imported into Malaysia for domestic use, rather than for re-export. An investor and CEO of an Asian neocloud company, who declined to be named, spent Friday morning in calls with lawyers in the US. “Everyone is still figuring out… Maybe every time you export something, there will be additional process to go through. We are worried about more scrutiny which will make it longer for chips to come through,” the CEO said. In February 2025, Singapore said that while 22pc of Nvidia’s chip sales were booked to entities with operations in Singapore only 1pc physically came to Singapore. Singapore has also just charged a fifth person in an AI server fraud case. Jarick Seet, head of small-mid caps at Maybank, said the region could weather tighter rules. “Singapore itself will be more stringent, I think it’s a natural thing that happens. Singapore will tighten rules and the US will tighten rules, but I don’t think this will harm Singapore’s and Malaysia’s prospect of buying chips.” A senior executive at a chip maker in Singapore, who declined to be named, even sees a silver lining. “With Jensen out , then the Chinese will have a harder time getting chips from the US. Maybe it is not a bad thing for the non-US people who will have more access to chips.” If the US slows building data centres following Democratic victories in key data-centre states such as Texas and Georgia in midterm elections, “those companies are going to look elsewhere and likely come to countries that can offer them land and deals and power,” the executive said. “Even if we lose a chunk of the China business, I think we will get other companies coming looking for compute.”

items.title: Can Ghana talk its way back to reading?
items.description: On a Sunday afternoon at Theia Coffee House in Airport Residential, members of the Just Read Book Club troop in with books of their own, read for an hour, and only then introduce themselves. The club is one of a growing number in Accra: Bibliophiles and Vibes , started by four young Ghanaian women, meets monthly on Twitter Spaces and every quarter in person; Noname Book Club has had an Accra chapter since 2025; Between the Covers held its first meeting at the Goethe-Institut in February; and in April, the founders of Accra Culture & Co started a club at a neighbourhood eatery in Achimota because, as they put it, “we wanted something where we actually live”. These clubs are an answer to a lament now familiar across social media: adults confessing – usually in good humour – that they cannot read as much as they once did, and mourning the days when they devoured novels, before screens and adult distractions fractured their attention. Considering that by October 2025, 26.3 million Ghanaians, about three in every four, were online, the screens are hard to escape. This chorus is one sign of a wider erosion, which the country’s educational and cultural leadership now acknowledges, above all among the young. At the Ghana Literacy Fair in June, Professor George K. T. Oduro pledged on behalf of the Ministry of Education to turn reading into a national movement. A month later, the Minister for Tourism, Culture and Creative Arts called for fresh energy to spark a reading habit among the youth, echoing the Ghana Library Authority, which serves 35 million people through just 139 public libraries, in describing the nation’s appetite for books as waning. With the decline widely acknowledged and new gatherings multiplying in answer, one of the most instructive has been running in Accra since March 2025 under the name Unplugged & Reconciled. Its growth has been measured and steady, building a close community before scale. The first edition, held at Full Option Lounge in East Legon on 6 March 2025, drew 35 people to hear the celebrated playwright Chief Moomen and the novelist Lawrence Darmani, whose Grief Child won the Commonwealth Writers’ Prize for best first book from Africa in 1992. The second, in February 2026, was devoted to West African and diaspora writing, supported by Compassion International Ghana and Creatives Project Ghana, doubling its previous attendance. The StorySlam in September drew 60. Bambu Heritage Productions, Chief Moomen’s theatre company, has since joined as a partner. But attendance says little about whether anyone reads more as a result; the platform’s clearest effects lie elsewhere. It dissolves the distance between emerging minds and established craft, placing young adults across the table from writers and creatives credited with decades of work; at the pilot, Darmani urged the young writers present to treat their writing as a gift to humanity. It alsp transforms passive listeners into active creators, most vividly at its recent StorySLAM, where attendees stepped onto the stage to share stories of their own. Above all, it has successfully created a living literary community among people who seldom share an evening, with four in five pilot participants reporting meaningful new connections. While the organisers nod to the literary salons of early modern and nineteenth-century France and Italy, they have stripped away the salon’s defining trait: its exclusivity, leaving it with a truer lineage closer to home. At independence, Efua Sutherland founded the Ghana Society of Writers, launching Okyeame in 1960, the landmark journal that featured early works by Kofi Awoonor, Ayi Kwei Armah, and Ama Ata Aidoo. Sutherland’s own theatre drew deeply from anansesem , the Akan tradition of Ananse storytelling in which the boundary between teller and listener dissolves. By convention, the musical interludes, mmoguo , are contributed by those listening, who sing, interject and comment as the story proceeds. Unplugged & Reconciled attempts to reclaim this indigenous convention for contemporary Ghanaian literary life by turning listeners into participants. It also responds to a growing global desire for shared, unmediated spaces beyond the reach of constant digital distraction. The Silent Book Club , begun by two friends in a San Francisco wine bar in 2012, now has more than 2,000 chapters in 62 countries. The Offline Club , founded in Amsterdam, takes guests’ phones at the door and has opened in London, Paris, Barcelona and Dubai; its London organiser says every event sells out at once. In Britain, where only one in three children aged eight to eighteen said in 2025 that they enjoyed reading in their free time, the government declared 2026 a National Year of Reading. Closer to home, alongside the book clubs now multiplying across Accra, Ghana’s literary ecosystem already pulses through established channels: including but not limited to independent bookshops, public libraries, the Pa Gya! literary festival and a vibrant spoken-word scene that has flourished since 2010. Unplugged & Reconciled opens a distinct pathway aimed at the audience those institutions find hardest to reach: the lapsed reader or, simply, the person who knows how to read, yet has drifted away from the habit. The soirée acts as a bridge back into the fold, such that every reader it restores becomes a fresh participant for Accra’s book clubs, festivals and libraries across the country. The harder test lies beyond East Legon, however. Even within Accra, as the Achimota club’s founders note, literary events “cluster in the same handful of neighbourhoods.” The readers Ghana is losing fastest are younger and further from the capital still; nearly half of Grade 4 pupils fall short of minimum proficiency in English on the National Standardised Test. Similarly, the Ministry of Education’s sector plan places the largest gaps in foundational learning in the northern regions. The groundwork has already been laid. Over the past twenty months, Unplugged & Reconciled has moved past the experimental stage, successfully coaxing lapsed readers back to the page, bridging the generational divide between emerging talents and literary elders, and securing some level of institutional and theatrical backing. Across Accra, independent book clubs are proving that the youth are more than willing to read, provided the invitation is made. If the Ministry’s ambition is to ignite a national reading movement, the cultural spark is already burning in the capital’s lounges and salons.

items.title: Les crises humanitaires du 21e siècle : la situation en République démocratique du Congo
items.description: La République démocratique du Congo (RDC) traverse actuellement une crise sanitaire majeure : la pire épidémie d’Ebola jamais enregistrée de l’histoire du pays. Le 17 mai 2026, l’Organisation mondiale de la santé (OMS) a d’ailleurs qualifié cette épidémie d’Urgence de santé publique de portée internationale (USPPI). La contamination du virus augmente rapidement, à l’heure actuelle, il a franchi le cap des 11 000 cas confirmés et connus, causant plus de 5 300 morts. En l’absence de traitement ou de vaccin efficace contre la souche Bundibugyo qui en est à l’origine, la propagation de la maladie s’intensifie fortement. Pour riposter contre ce fléau, L’Organisation non gouvernementale (ONG) ALIMA (The Alliance for International Medical Action) a mis en place des Chambres d'Urgence Biosécurisée pour Épidémies (CUBE). Ces dispositifs permettent alors de protéger au mieux le corps médical, d’offrir au patient la possibilité d’être accompagné par leur proche et de leur donner les meilleurs soins possible. Cette crise sanitaire intervient également dans un contexte où l’insécurité liée aux groupes armés est constante, interrogeant alors sur la capacité d’action des ONG à fournir une aide humanitaire appropriée dans un environnement sous haute tension. Comment décririez-vous la situation sanitaire du pays aujourd’hui, au-delà de la seule urgence Ebola ? Pourquoi ces crises reviennent-elles sans cesse ? Quels sont, selon vous, les principaux obstacles structurels à l’accès aux soins ? En quoi l’insécurité globale complique-t-elle la riposte contre l’épidémie ? Qu’est-ce qui est différent aujourd’hui avec la souche Bundibugyo, contre laquelle il n’existe encore ni vaccin ni traitement homologué, et dans un contexte de coupe budgétaire ? Le point avec Moumouni Kinda, directeur des opérations chez ALIMA (The Alliance for International Medical Action). L’article Les crises humanitaires du 21e siècle : la situation en République démocratique du Congo est apparu en premier sur IRIS .

items.title: Burkina Faso : Le dossier judiciaire de l’ancien président Paul-Henri Damiba en pleine instruction selon le procureur
items.description: Le dossier judiciaire concernant l'ancien président de la Transition, le Lieutenant-Colonel Paul-Henri Sandaogo Damiba, franchit une étape formelle majeure devant la justice républicaine. Selon les informations communiquées par le Parquet général près la Cour d'appel de Ouagadougou, l'instruction suit son cours sous le contrôle du Pôle judiciaire spécialisé. L'ancien chef d'État fait face à de lourdes accusations pénales, notamment des faits présumés de complicité d'association de malfaiteurs terroristes, de détention d'armes à feu et de munitions à des fins terroristes, ainsi que de complicité de financement du terrorisme. Une procédure qui s’appuie sur les dispositions du Code pénal et sur la loi relative à la lutte contre le blanchiment des capitaux. La justice burkinabè poursuit l'examen des dossiers liés à la sécurité nationale et à la déstabilisation de l'État. L'instruction du dossier judiciaire impliquant l'ancien président Paul-Henri Sandaogo Damiba est activement menée par le Parquet général près la Cour d'appel de Ouagadougou. Inscrit formellement au rôle des personnes contre lesquelles des poursuites sont engagées pour des faits présumés de terrorisme, l’ancien dirigeant militaire se trouve au cœur d'une procédure criminelle approfondie. Le bordereau récapitulatif des poursuites émis par le ministère public détaille avec précision les griefs imputés au prévenu. Le Lieutenant-Colonel Damiba Paul Henry Sandaogo est poursuivi sous trois chefs d'inculpation principaux: La complicité d'association de malfaiteurs terroristes ; La complicité de détention illégale d'arme à feu et de munitions à des fins terroristes ; La complicité de financement du terrorisme. Pour fonder ces poursuites, les juges s'appuient sur un cadre légal rigoureux combinant le droit pénal général et les textes financiers spécialisés. Les faits reprochés sont prévus et punis par les articles 131-4, 131-5, 131-8, 316-1, 361-2, 361-3, 362-1 et 362-2 du Code pénal burkinabè. La procédure invoque également les articles 4, 7, 8, 119, 120, 122 et 123 de la loi n°016-2016/AN du 3 mai 2016 relative à la lutte contre le blanchiment des capitaux et le financement du terrorisme au Burkina Faso. L’article Burkina Faso : Le dossier judiciaire de l'ancien président Paul-Henri Damiba en pleine instruction selon le procureur est apparu en premier sur NetAfrique.net .

items.title: With my record in Oyo, I’ll win 2027 — Makinde
items.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Oyo State Governor Seyi Makinde says his record in the state gives him confidence ahead of the 2027 election, pointing to increases in the state’s minimum wage, regular salary payments, investment in agriculture and infrastructure, and support for moving local produce to international markets as achievements he believes will help win voters’ support and edge him above other candidates. In an interview with Arise Television on Friday, the Allied Peoples Movement (APM) presidential candidate contrasted his administration’s approach with the Federal Government’s economic policies, arguing that national reforms should be judged by their impact on people’s daily lives. He also said economic growth and higher reserves meant little if Nigerians remained hungry and families could not afford basic needs. “Taking little reforms here and there will not work. If you are saying that things are happening at the macro level but it will filter down to micro, I see these as just excuses and shifting blames. Explaining, so we have very high reserves. What’s the impact on the ordinary people on the street? Are Nigerians hungry? Are more families able to, you know, afford certain things?” Makinde said. He cited increases in the minimum wage in Oyo State during his time as governor, saying it had risen from N18,000 to N30,000 and later to between N70,000 and N80,000. “How about the salary? Since I came in, I met a minimum wage at 18,000 naira, and we moved it to 30,000, all within seven plus years. When this administration started in 2023, I mean things basically went haywire, and we moved again minimum wage to 70-75, 80,000 naira,” he said. Makinde added that the state had not delayed salary payments during his tenure, including throughout the Buhari administration. “We have never held salaries for one month out of the seven plus years that I’ve spent here in Oyo State, all through the President Buhari period in office, we paid salaries. Oyo State never owed salaries under my watch,” he said. The governor said his administration had sought to expand Oyo’s economy by using the state’s agricultural advantage and investing in infrastructure. He said the Oyo State Agribusiness Development Agency was established to support the sector. “Here in Oyo State, we said, ‘Look, we will expand our economy using agriculture because obviously we have a comparative advantage in agriculture.’ When we came in, we set up Oyo State Agribusiness Development Agency, and also we said we will use development of our infrastructure to also drive our economy,” he said. Makinde linked infrastructure investment to the cost of living, saying transportation costs affect the movement of goods and services and contribute to prices. “When you are talking about structural cost of living. Transportation is a major part of it. To move goods and services from one area to the other, they all contribute to the structural cost of living, and it’s quite major,” he said. He also criticised the lack of public information about the pricing of petroleum products, asking how much crude oil was being allocated for domestic refining. Makinde said Nigerians could pay less for fuel without damaging the economy, and promised to publish the pricing template if elected. “And I’ve asked a question. Okay, this is Nigeria is an oil-producing country. Are we getting the benefit from petroleum products? They should bring for Nigerians to see the pricing template that we are using from crude oil production,” he said. “I know the pricing template; the pricing templates, they have refused to publicly bring it out. How much crude are being allocated on a daily basis for domestic refining? They know it and I know it that that Nigerians can pay less for petroleum products here without taking and value away and without distorting or dislocating our economy.” Makinde also said he would disclose the pricing template from the first day of his administration and maintained that petrol could cost less than it does currently. “I will disclose from day one, transparently, what is the pricing template for petroleum product in Nigeria. The price of petroleum product can be lower than what it is today,” he said. According to Makinde, Oyo had also invested in its airport to help move agricultural produce to international markets, adding that redistribution of federal allocations alone would not resolve the country’s economic problems. “Apart from agriculture, agribusiness, we saw that as a place with where we have comparative advantage. We put a lot of investment in our airport here, so that we can have the chance to get our produce out to elsewhere in the world,” he said. “If you are not productive, it is not sharing of federal allocation that will take us out of this. We have a lot more mouth to feed now than even then, and the industries have disappeared.” The post With my record in Oyo, I’ll win 2027 — Makinde appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Lacs/FIHA 2026 : La 5ème édition lancée sous le signe du partage des mémoires
items.description: Aného, 13 nov. (ATOP) – Les festivités de la 5ᵉ édition du Festival international d’histoire d’Aného (FIHA) ont été lancé le jeudi 12 novembre sous le signe du partage des mémoires. Porté par la Fondation Aquereburu & Partners et la commune des Lacs 1, avec le soutien de partenaires institutionnels, techniques, culturels et économiques, le FIHA poursuit sa vocation, celle de faire de l’histoire et du patrimoine des leviers de rapprochement entre les peuples. Après avoir mis en avant la diversité lors de sa précédente édition, le festival met cette année l’accent sur le partage des mémoires, des savoirs, des cultures et des opportunités. Pendant quatre jours, traditions locales, expressions artistiques venues d’ailleurs et initiatives de coopération se conjuguent pour faire de cette ancienne capitale du Togo un espace de dialogue et de découverte. Cette édition met à l’honneur non pas un pays, mais une région : l’Union européenne. Un choix qui renvoie à l’histoire d’Aného, dont le passé est étroitement lié aux présences allemande et française. À travers cette démarche, les organisateurs entendent revisiter les liens historiques entre l’Afrique et l’Europe, tout en ouvrant de nouvelles perspectives de coopération. L’Allemagne, la France, le Luxembourg, l’Autriche et l’Espagne prennent ainsi part à cette célébration, aux côtés du Maroc et du Brésil. La ville de Blitta est également associée à cette édition, dans une volonté d’élargir le festival aux autres territoires togolais. Un carnaval, les projections de films, les danses folkloriques des groupes de Blitta, les prestations d’une école de samba brésilienne et les concerts donnent à la ville une animation particulière. Une fanfare germano-togolaise de l’Institut Goethe et des caravaniers venus de Bonn, en Allemagne, participent également à cette rencontre festive. L’un des moments marquants de cette édition sera le dévoilement d’une fresque dédiée à Gervais Koffi Djondo, fils d’Aného, ancien ministre et figure majeure de l’entrepreneuriat togolais et africain. A travers cet hommage, la municipalité entend mettre en lumière un parcours remarquable et transmettre aux jeunes générations l’exemple d’un engagement au service du développement du continent. Le maire Aquerebourou Les officiels En prélude au lancement, un Forum sur le développement économique local (FoDEL), a été organisé la veille en partenariat avec la Coopération allemande à travers la GIZ. Il a permis à une quarantaine d’acteurs, d’échanger sur les moyens de renforcer l’attractivité des territoires et de stimuler les investissements privés. Cette rencontre a été également marquée par la signature d’une convention de partenariat pour le développement économique local entre les communes de Lacs 1, Blitta 1 et Dankpen 1. Pour le maire de la commune des Lacs 1, Me Alexis Coffi Aquereburu, le thème « partage » traduit une conviction profonde : « aucun peuple, aucune ville et aucune nation ne peut construire durablement son avenir dans l’isolement ». Le partage constitue, selon lui, une richesse qui se développe lorsqu’elle est transmise et mise au service du plus grand nombre. Désormais organisé tous les deux ans, le FIHA alternera avec le Festival international Bella Bellow, conçu autour de la musique, de l’humour et de la formation des jeunes talents. Le nouveau festival ambitionne notamment de créer des espaces de formation et de transmission à travers des master class, des ateliers, des rencontres professionnelles et des scènes ouvertes aux jeunes créateurs. Il reposera sur une complémentarité entre trois villes : Atakpamé, ville d’origine de Bella Bellow, accueillera l’ouverture ; Aného sera le cadre de l’apothéose, tandis qu’une troisième ville sera associée à chaque édition pour contribuer à la diffusion du patrimoine musical. ATOP/BA/AAK

items.title: Ghana needs national data cleanup to unlock AI potential –Founder of GradePoint AI
items.description: Founder and Chief Executive Officer of GradePoint AI, Dr Gillian Hammah, has called for a nationwide data-cleaning exercise, urging the government to prioritise the digitisation and standardisation of public records to enable Ghana to fully harness artificial intelligence (AI). She says the country’s ability to benefit from AI will remain limited if critical government information continues to be stored in paper files and fragmented databases across public institutions. Speaking at the Step Up Executive Breakfast Series, Dr Hammah proposed a presidentially endorsed initiative requiring every government ministry to organise, digitise and harmonise its records within three to six months. She believes such an intervention would provide the foundation for developing AI solutions capable of addressing Ghana’s developmental challenges. “I would advocate for a national data cleanup that is endorsed by the President to say, every ministry in the next three months or six months, we are going to go through, we’re going to assign people, and we’re going to start putting our data in order,” she said. Dr Hammah explained that many public institutions still rely heavily on paper-based documentation, making it difficult for AI systems to access and process the information needed to develop solutions. “Everything is paper. AI can’t do anything with paper,” she stressed. She said the exercise must go beyond digitisation to ensure that information held by different government agencies is accurate and consistent. Using personal records as an example, she questioned whether details such as names and dates of birth held by the National Identification Authority would correspond with records in other government institutions. According to her, inconsistencies across public databases could undermine the reliability of information used to train and develop AI systems. Dr Hammah also called for Ghana to make relevant datasets available to international AI developers, arguing that the benefits of such information should extend beyond the country’s borders. She cited sickle cell disease as an example, explaining that sharing relevant health information could help foreign-developed AI systems better understand conditions affecting Black populations, including Ghanaians living abroad. “Yes, Ghana should have its own models, that we should be able to build solutions that are for Ghanaians, but we also need to be willing to share our data and actually share it with the foreign models,” she said. She maintained that Ghana’s AI ambitions should combine responsible data-sharing arrangements with the development of locally relevant solutions. “The only way to do that is to start with cleaning up our data,” she added. The Step Up Executive Breakfast Series, organised by Step Up Business School, was held under the theme, “The AI-Powered Project Leader: How to Lead, Deliver & Stay Relevant in the Age of AI.”

items.title: COP31 : enjeux et engagement des pays du Maghreb face au dérèglement climatique
items.description: Lors de la 31e Conference des Parties a la Convention-cadre des Nations unies sur les changements climatiques (COP31), organisee du 9 au 20 novembre en Turquie, a Antalya, la Tunisie, l'Algerie et le Maroc ont mis en avant les enjeux, les defis, les engagements, voire les contraintes qui se posent pour chacun de ces pays dans la lutte et l'adaptation au changement climatique. Outre les pays du Maghreb, l'evenement a mis en exergue les divergences entre les delegations participantes en matiere de decarbonation et de cooperation internationale sans echange de credits, une situation qui risque de peser lourd sur l'acces des pays en developpement au financement pour reussir leur transition ecologique. Financement et transformation des engagements en investissement au cœur des enjeux climatiques pour la Tunisie La Tunisie a besoin de financements a la hauteur de son ambition pour la reduction des emissions de gaz a effet de serre. Le pays a mis en place une feuille de route (CDN 3.0) engageant ses politiques publiques sur la voie de la decarbonation avec pour objectif de reduire ses emissions de 46,4 % d'ici 2030 et de 62 % pour 2035, avant d'atteindre la neutralite carbone a l'horizon 2050. La priorite pour le pays est de plaider pour ses besoins de financement climatique et de promouvoir ses engagements ecologiques en investissements concrets. L'ambition du pays engage la transformation structurelle progressive de ses secteurs economiques majeurs, a savoir l'energie, l'agriculture, l'industrie, les transports et la transformation et la valorisation des dechets. Il s'agit aussi d'accelerer le deploiement de solutions de production d'energie renouvelable et d'ameliorer l'efficacite energetique, entre autres imperatifs imposes par la CDN 3.0. La situation de la Tunisie a ete resumee par Seif Derouiche, conseiller en politique et finance climatique au sein de l'Agence federale allemande de cooperation internationale pour le developpement durable (GIZ) pour le projet du Programme d'appui a l'action environnementale de l'UE en Tunisie (PAGECTE). Il a declare : « Le financement climatique doit evoluer vers des approches capables de combiner les ressources publiques, les financements internationaux et les capitaux prives. Il s'agit notamment de developper des projets suffisamment structures et bancables pour attirer les investisseurs, tout en garantissant leur contribution aux objectifs nationaux de developpement et de decarbonation ». Contribuer aux efforts mondiaux de reduction des emissions en repondant aux aspirations de developpement et d'emploi, une « equation delicate » pour l'Algerie Dans une allocution du president algerien, Abdelmadjid Tebboune, lue par son Premier ministre Sifi Ghrieb devant les participants a la COP31, il a souligne que le changement climatique en Algerie n'etait pas vecu comme « une simple prevision lointaine, mais comme une realite etablie frappant de plein fouet sa securite hydrique et alimentaire ». Dans un contexte de dereglement climatique, le pays fait face a trois phenomenes graves : la desertification, les frequentes vagues de secheresse et la menace des feux de foret dont la gravite s'etend, a indique le chef de l'etat, d'ou la necessite de placer ces questions au centre des « politiques publiques, dans un cadre institutionnel et de planification qui ne cesse de se renforcer ». Le gouvernement algerien prevoit une reduction « inconditionnelle » des emissions de 14 % a l'horizon 2035, « entierement finance sur nos ressources nationales, avec notre disposition a porter ce taux a 31 % des lors qu'un soutien international serait assure », soulevant ainsi la necessite de financements internationaux a l'instar de la Tunisie. Selon le president algerien, son pays fait face a une « equation delicate » devant concilier les aspirations de developpement et d'emploi avec la contribution aux efforts internationaux de reduction des emissions. Dans ce cadre, Abdelmadjid Tebboune a fait part des projets gouvernementaux pour la production d'energie renouvelable, celle de l'hydrogene, tout en developpant l'efficacite energetique et le transport collectif. Il a cependant souligne que les objectifs de transition energetique doivent se faire sans responsabilite commune, mais differenciee, tout en respectant les processus de developpement propres a chaque pays et en tenant compte de leurs imperatifs de souverainete et des engagements en matiere de financement et transfert technologique. Le Maroc plaide pour une mobilisation plus importante de la communaute internationale sur le dossier climatique Le chef de la diplomatie marocaine Nasser Bourita a defendu une approche internationale basee sur la justice energetique, l'equite climatique et l'acces aux financements necessaires a la transition ecologique, soulignant d'ailleurs lors d'une visite effectuee au pavillon marocain lors de la COP31 le 11 novembre que « le Maroc participe a ce sommet non pas en simple invite ou en tant que pays beneficiaire, mais avec un engagement fort, une experience solide et des reponses nationales concretes ». Le gouvernement marocain a fixe des politiques visant la reduction des emissions des gaz a effet de serre de 53 % a l'horizon 2035, et ce, grâce au developpement des energies renouvelables, la transformation des secteurs economiques, la decarbonation des transports et la promotion d'une economie a faible empreinte carbone. Pour 2030, le pays vise aussi le taux de 52 % pour la part des energies renouvelables dans ses capacites electriques installees. Pour concretiser ces ambitions, le ministre marocain a souligne la necessite de mettre en place des mecanismes innovants de financements aptes a soutenir les investissements en matiere de resilience climatique.

items.title: Microsoft says ‘improvements’ for Outlook in North America, Europe
items.description: Microsoft said on Friday that it was seeing “improvements” for Outlook email and other services amid an outage that was disrupting public services and businesses around the world. In an update, it noted “broader improvements in North America, sustained improvements across much of Europe, and encouraging recovery signals in Asia-Pacific”. A more than 12-hour outage of Microsoft Outlook and Teams crippled communications for businesses and governments globally, forcing some organisations to revert to fax machines and halting at least one bond repurchase in Europe. Microsoft said server issues were behind the incident that also affected its Copilot AI assistant and that a broader roll-out of software fixes was starting to stabilise the system. It said it was not aware of any malicious activity. Outlook and Teams are two of the most widely used workplace applications with hundreds of millions of users. The outage prevented people from performing essential functions such as sending emails, managing calendars and hosting virtual meetings. It affected government agencies from Australia to Japan and the United States, caused delays at trading firms, hindered some companies from publishing earnings and prompted airlines to warn customers of communication lags, according to public statements. Organisations that host Microsoft services on their own servers, rather than in the cloud, were somewhat spared. In its latest update, Microsoft said efforts to improve serviceability were not progressing as expected. “We’re identifying alternate workstreams that can be applied to increase capacity in the face of sustained traffic management imbalances,” it said. Downdetector, which tracks outages by collating status reports from a number of sources, showed more than 25,000 reports of Outlook problems in the US at 9:30 p.m. ET (0230 GMT). It also showed outages for several Microsoft services in the Asia-Pacific region, including India, Australia and Japan, early Friday local time. At its peak, Downdetector showed more than 130,000 reports of Outlook problems in the US around 1 p.m. ET on Thursday. In a service health notice, Microsoft said features of Microsoft 365 services that depended on Exchange Online and email were affected, while elements that did not rely on Exchange Online remained functional. Exchange Online is the company’s cloud-based messaging platform that delivers email, calendar, contacts, and tasks. Another outage for Microsoft The outage is one of the longest in Microsoft’s history and the second disruption to its services this year. Microsoft said the outage specifically hit features tied to Exchange Online — its cloud-based email and scheduling hub — leaving unconnected applications operational. The incident deepens questions about the global reliance on a handful of Big Tech companies that supply both the essential software and the cloud infrastructure that underpins it. Microsoft shares fell 1.7 per cent before the bell, lagging the broader market. They have gained roughly 8pc so far this year. “The bigger worry is that this is not the first Microsoft 365 outage this year,” said Josh Gilbert, a market analyst at trading platform eToro. “If reliability starts to look like a recurring problem, it hands every IT department a reason to think twice before putting even more of their business in one provider’s hands.” Still, some analysts have questioned whether such incidents can push customers on to rivals due to the steep switching costs of replacing tools embedded so deeply in daily operations. Microsoft faced an outage with its 365 services in January this year and also in October last year. Last month, it reported an outage of its Azure cloud platform that impacted its suite of productivity software, and a range of industries worldwide. Trades had to be confirmed by fax A spokesperson for the UK government said it was working with Microsoft to find a solution for the outage that hit organisations such as the NHS and London’s Metropolitan Police. Lack of access to emails and other services was impacting the Metropolitan Police’s ability to report some crimes online, though its ability to respond to calls was not affected. NHS said its local services were turning to alternate measures such as using IT systems or paper records. For businesses, the fallout was widespread. European exchange operator Euronext reported email disruptions, British insurer Aviva activated backups for its earnings calls and Danish shipping giant Maersk warned customers of delayed updates. American AI giants OpenAI and Anthropic also faced issues with Microsoft connectors, while Indian airlines IndiGo, Akasa Air and Air India said their email support services were impacted. The outage also disrupted fund management at Taiwanese securities firms, life insurers, and investment trust companies. One of the companies went as far as cancelling a bond repurchase transaction, a source familiar with the situation told Reuters . Another Taiwanese financial company resorted to using fax to confirm trades, a second source said. In the US, electric truck maker Workhorse Group rescheduled its results on Thursday to November 16, while Switzerland’s Richemont briefly delayed its first-half results announcement on Friday. In Australia, where the spy agency and federal police were among organisations caught in the outage, Cyber Security Minister Tony Burke said Microsoft does not suspect a cyber attack. “The impact that they are dealing with … is very much on email systems,” the minister added. Impact on email systems Burke said that Microsoft believed it was not dealing with a cyberattack. “They believe they are dealing in some ways similar to what we saw with respect to CrowdStrike where there is an update that has gone awry,” Burke said at a press conference. “The impact that they are dealing with … is very much on email systems,” the minister added. Australia’s spy agency and federal police were among organisations caught up in the outage on Friday. The CrowdStrike malfunction of 2024 was one of the largest internet disruptions, hobbling technology systems in hospitals, banks, and airports, highlighting the vulnerability of the world’s interconnected technologies. The US House of Representatives said the outage impacted its users and its engineers were working with Microsoft. The company had earlier in the day pointed to a number of servers being unexpectedly unavailable and said it was not driven by an increase in traffic. Microsoft had then said the restored servers remained stable so far and that it was shifting traffic to alternate routes wherever possible while streamlining the process to bring the remaining impacted servers back online. “As capacity is restored, users may experience a gradual recovery as their clients reconnect,” Microsoft said in a previous statement. At 6 p.m. ET (2300 GMT), Microsoft had said it observed limited recovery as users gradually reconnected. Businesses feel the impact OpenAI said it was investigating an issue with Microsoft connectors in which new connections may be broken and tools are not working as expected. Anthropic said it had identified an issue with an upstream provider affecting its Microsoft 365 connector. Microsoft last month reported an outage of its Azure cloud platform that impacted the tech giant’s suite of productivity software, and a range of industries worldwide. Electric truck maker Workhorse Group, which was expected to report third-quarter results on November 12, rescheduled it to November 16 citing business disruptions caused by the global Microsoft outage.

items.title: Ogou: Le ministre de la santé visite l’ENAM-ENSF d’Atakpamé
items.description: Atakpamé, 13 nov. (ATOP)- Le ministre en charge de la Santé, Jean-Marie Ewonoulé Tessi, a visité le jeudi 12 novembre l’École nationale des sages-femmes et des infirmiers (ENAM-ENSF) d’Atakpamé. Cette visite s’inscrit dans le cadre du suivi de la rentrée académique 2026-2027. L’objectif est de s’assurer du bon démarrage des activités pédagogiques, d’apprécier les conditions de formation des futurs professionnels de la santé, et d’échanger avec la communauté éducative sur l’amélioration continue de la qualité de la formation. Entretien du ministre avec le corps enseignant La rencontre a été marquée par la remise officielle d’équipements destinés à dynamiser l’apprentissage pratique et théorique. Il s’agit notamment d’un bâtiment d’études réhabilité et d’un bus de transport pour les étudiants. L’établissement a aussi reçu du matériel didactique spécialisé composé des spécimens anatomiques, à savoir cerveaux humains, squelettes, mannequins de placenta avec cordon ombilical, modèles de bébés et bassins pelviens, viscères du cou et du thorax. Il a été aussi mis à la disposition de l’établissement, des équipements technologiques et bureautiques composés, entre autres, d’ordinateurs portables, d’imprimantes, de vidéoprojecteurs, d’écrans de projection, de photocopieurs et de scanners. Par ailleurs, l’OMS a pris en charge l’installation d’un réseau Wi-Fi haut débit et d’un système de visioconférence. Le ministre Tessi a exhorté les étudiants à faire preuve d’assiduité, de rigueur et de conscience professionnelle, insistant sur le fait que la qualité des soins de santé de demain repose sur l’excellence de la formation initiale. La cérémonie s’est déroulée en présence de personnalités administratives et militaires, parmi lesquelles le gouverneur de la région des Plateaux, Général de brigade Dadja Maganawé, le préfet de l’Ogou, Ekpé Kodjo, le directeur régional de la Santé des Plateaux, Dr. Nyametso Dzifa, le directeur de l’ENAM-ENSF, Dr Akpalou Kossivi ainsi que les responsables de l’encadrement pédagogique. Pour le compte de cette rentrée scolaire, l’établissement a accueilli 110 nouveaux élèves, à savoir : 67 infirmiers d’État et 43 sages. ATOP/KJ/KKT/MD
