items.title: Panne mondiale de Microsoft: quand les défaillances du géant américain rappellent l’importance des solutions technologiques africaines
items.description: La panne mondiale qui affecte depuis le jeudi 12 novembre 2026 les services Outlook, Teams et Copilot de Microsoft met en lumière la dépendance des organisations aux grandes infrastructures numériques internationales. Alors que le géant américain peine à rétablir normalement ses services, cet incident rappelle l’importance de développer des solutions technologiques endogènes, à l’image de Aïobi, une DeepTech burkinabè qui ambitionne de contribuer à la souveraineté numérique africaine. Le monde numérique est mis à rude épreuve. Depuis le jeudi 12 novembre 2026, une panne d'ampleur mondiale perturbe plusieurs services du géant américain Microsoft, notamment Outlook, Teams et son assistant d'intelligence artificielle Copilot. Malgré les différentes mesures engagées, l'entreprise peine à rétablir la situation et reconnaît que ses premières tentatives de correction n'ont pas produit les résultats escomptés. À l'origine de cette perturbation, une «charge élevée» sur l'infrastructure de Microsoft, qui affecte la connectivité aux services Microsoft 365. Face à des déséquilibres persistants dans la gestion du trafic, le groupe déclare rechercher des solutions alternatives afin d'augmenter les capacités de ses infrastructures et de rétablir progressivement les services. Dans ses communications sur le réseau social X, Microsoft a notamment reconnu l'inefficacité des premières modifications apportées à son système. L'entreprise affirme toutefois avoir observé des signes encourageants concernant la stabilité de ses serveurs après l'application d'un correctif. Elle assure également ne disposer, à ce stade, d'aucun élément indiquant une activité malveillante à l'origine de l'incident. Une panne aux conséquences internationales La perturbation a rapidement dépassé les frontières américaines pour atteindre des utilisateurs dans 74 pays et territoires, selon la plateforme Downdetector. Des signalements ont été enregistrés dans plusieurs régions des Amériques, d'Europe, d'Asie et d'Afrique. Au-delà des désagréments rencontrés par les particuliers et les entreprises, cette panne a également affecté des services publics essentiels. Au Royaume-Uni, les perturbations ont notamment eu de «graves répercussions» sur les services de santé. Selon Rachel Harrison, responsable des services publics au sein du syndicat GMB, les personnels des lignes téléphoniques 111 et 999 rencontrent des difficultés pour transmettre les informations relatives aux patients, entraînant une accumulation importante de dossiers en attente. Les interventions d'urgence semblaient toutefois épargnées. La Nouvelle-Zélande a également signalé des difficultés dans la réception de ses courriels, précisant que ses ambassades, consulats et représentations diplomatiques à travers le monde étaient concernés. Cette situation illustre une réalité incontournable : la dépendance aux grandes plateformes technologiques peut exposer des millions d'utilisateurs, d'entreprises et d'administrations à des perturbations dont les conséquences dépassent largement le cadre informatique. Aïobi, l'alternative africaine qui mérite attention Bowendsom Thibaud Nikiema, CEO de Aïobi Dans ce contexte, la nécessité de soutenir l'innovation technologique africaine prend tout son sens. Le développement de solutions conçues sur le continent, adaptées à ses réalités et reposant sur des infrastructures maîtrisées localement, constitue un enjeu stratégique pour renforcer l'autonomie numérique des États et des entreprises africaines. C'est dans cette dynamique que s'inscrit Aïobi. Fondée en 2025 et adossée au groupe BURVAL Corporate / BBS Holding. Cette entreprise burkinabè se présente comme la première DeepTech d'Afrique de l'Ouest spécialisée dans l'intelligence artificielle appliquée aux entreprises. Officiellement lancée le 20 août 2025 à Ouagadougou, elle est dirigée par Bowendsom Thibaud Nikiema, expert en intelligence artificielle. À travers ses différentes solutions numériques, Aïobi entend apporter des réponses concrètes aux besoins des organisations africaines. Son ambition ne se limite pas au marché burkinabè: ses technologies sont déjà utilisées dans dix pays africains, témoignant de sa volonté de déployer son savoir-faire à l'échelle régionale. L'un des aspects qui retient particulièrement l'attention, réside dans le choix de développer et d'héberger ses solutions sur une infrastructure établie au Burkina Faso, avec un accent particulier sur la sécurité des données des utilisateurs. Une orientation qui rejoint les préoccupations grandissantes autour de la souveraineté numérique, de la protection des informations et de la maîtrise des infrastructures technologiques. L'innovation africaine, un impératif stratégique Si Aïobi ne saurait être présentée comme une solution de remplacement immédiat à l'ensemble des services de Microsoft, son positionnement illustre néanmoins le potentiel des entreprises technologiques africaines à concevoir des outils adaptés aux besoins du continent. L'enjeu est désormais de consolider ces initiatives, de renforcer leur capacité d'innovation et de favoriser leur adoption par les administrations et les entreprises. La panne de Microsoft rappelle ainsi que même les géants mondiaux du numérique ne sont pas à l'abri des défaillances. Pour l'Afrique, le défi ne consiste pas seulement à consommer les technologies venues d'ailleurs, mais aussi à investir dans la conception de ses propres solutions. Dans cette perspective, Aïobi représente une initiative à encourager et à suivre, car la souveraineté numérique du continent se construira aussi grâce à l'audace et au génie créatif de ses propres acteurs. Par Valentin SOMANDE L’article Panne mondiale de Microsoft: quand les défaillances du géant américain rappellent l’importance des solutions technologiques africaines est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: GHS launches second round of MDA against Onchocerciasis
items.description: The Ghana Health Service (GHS) has launched the second round of its 2026 Mass Drug Administration (MDA) campaign against Onchocerciasis (river blindness), urging residents in affected communities to participate in the exercise to help eliminate the disease by 2030. The campaign, scheduled for November 15 to 29, will cover 86 endemic districts across 15 regions, with trained health workers and community drug distributors providing free medication to eligible persons. The Director-General of the GHS, Dr Samuel Kaba Akoriyea, speaking at a press briefing in Accra on Thursday, said river blindness, also known as Onchocerciasis, was caused by a parasite transmitted through the bites of infected blackflies and could damage the skin and eyes, potentially leading to blindness. He said the disease could also deprive people of their ability to work, attend school and support their families, making its elimination important to the health and economic well-being of affected communities. Dr Akoriyea said Ghana had made significant progress since the GHS and its partners began interventions in 1997, reducing the number of districts requiring treatment from 152 to 86. He said the first round of the 2026 campaign, conducted from June 20 to July 10, reached more than 4.8 million people and recorded a national treatment coverage of 86.1 per cent. However, he identified gaps in household registration as a challenge, noting that inadequate registration could result in some eligible persons being missed. He said the Service would strengthen household registration under the Free Primary Healthcare initiative, improve supervision and provide additional support to districts requiring attention. Dr Akoriyea urged residents to welcome campaign teams, seek clarification where necessary and take the medication if eligible, particularly those in remote communities. He expressed appreciation to health workers, community drug distributors, development partners, traditional and religious leaders and the media for their continued support. Dr Manal Taryam, Chief Executive Officer and member of the Board of Trustees of the Noor Dubai Foundation, reaffirmed the Foundation’s commitment to supporting Ghana’s efforts to eliminate river blindness by 2030. She said the Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum Global Initiatives was providing a US$7.7 million grant to fund a three-year programme aimed at eliminating the disease. The programme included twice-yearly mass treatment in affected communities, disease surveillance and training for health workers and community drug distributors. Dr Taryam said the first round of the 2026 campaign treated about 4.7 million people across 86 targeted districts, representing 85.5 per cent of the target, while 20,000 people were trained. She said the programme would target more than five million people annually and was projected to generate over US$410 million in economic benefits over 30 years. She commended the Ghana Health Service, Ministry of Health, community drug distributors and other partners for their contributions. She said the foundation would continue supporting Ghana until river blindness was eliminated. On his part, the Director of Public Health at the Ghana Health Service (GHS), Dr Franklin Asiedu-Bekoe, called on the media to support the 2026 Mass Drug Administration campaign against river blindness by providing accurate information to the public. He said the media’s partnership was essential to increasing public awareness of onchocerciasis, a neglected tropical disease that affects vulnerable communities, particularly those in rural and underserved areas. Dr Asiedu-Bekoe said although the disease was preventable and treatable, it could cause disability, suffering, stigma and financial difficulties for affected individuals and their families. “Collective efforts and continued stakeholder support were necessary to eliminate river blindness in Ghana,” he said. He assured that the GHS remained committed to eliminating the disease and improving the health and quality of life of Ghanaians. The campaign provided safe and effective medication to eligible persons in affected communities and formed part of Ghana’s efforts to eliminate river blindness as a public health problem by 2030.

items.title: Muntaka hosts ALEO, NYPD delegation to discuss collaboration with Ghana Police Service
items.description: A delegation from the African Law Enforcement Organisation (ALEO) and the New York Police Department (NYPD) has called for stronger collaboration with the Ghana Police Service to improve relations between the police and the communities they serve. The delegation, led by Lieutenant Yaw Offin, made the call during a visit to the Minister for the Interior, Muntaka Mohammed-Mubarak, at the Ministry in Accra. The visit forms part of ALEO’s efforts to strengthen cooperation with Ghana’s law enforcement institutions and promote community-oriented policing. ALEO is a non-profit fraternal organisation made up of active and retired law enforcement and security professionals, based in Jamaica, New York. It promotes protection, unity, and community responsibility, extending its work beyond policing and the borders of New York City. Its current mission to Ghana, under the theme “ To Serve and to Protect Beyond Borders ,” is aimed at providing support and hope to underprivileged children and vulnerable communities. Welcoming the delegation, Mr Muntaka assured them of Ghana’s peace and security and outlined the Ministry’s mandate as the institution responsible for internal security. He also briefed them on the agencies under the Ministry and their respective responsibilities. The Minister said engagements of this nature were important because they provided opportunities for both sides to exchange ideas, learn from one another and improve service delivery. He wished the delegation a pleasant stay in Ghana and a safe journey home after their visit.

items.title: Premature babies need more than survival – Deputy Health Minister
items.description: The Deputy Minister of Health, Professor Dr Grace Ayensu-Danquah, has called for increased investment in neonatal healthcare and stronger follow-up services to ensure premature babies receive the care they need beyond the first days of life. She said survival was only the beginning of a longer journey for babies born too soon, who often require specialised medical attention, continuous monitoring and sustained support to achieve healthy growth and development. Speaking at the 3rd Purple for Prematurity Summit, Prof. Ayensu-Danquah highlighted government interventions aimed at reducing newborn deaths. These include the Presidential Initiative on Maternal Health Emergency Response (PRIMER) and the expansion of community-based newborn care services. She stressed the need for stronger collaboration between government and health sector stakeholders to develop a national maternal and child health roadmap that guarantees quality care for every baby born too soon, too small, or sick. Founder of the African Foundation for Premature Babies and Children (AFPNC), Selma Bentoom, also called for the introduction of a National Action Plan on Prematurity. She urged the government to integrate follow-up care for premature babies into the National Health Insurance Scheme (NHIS) benefits package and increase investment in neonatal healthcare. Ms Bentoom said efforts to save the lives of premature babies must be matched with sustained care to give them the best opportunity to grow and thrive.

items.title: GES processes 347 salary arrears cases for 2024 recruited teachers; 119 staff ID applications unverified
items.description: The Ghana Education Service (GES) says it has successfully processed 347 salary arrears cases involving teachers recruited in 2024 and forwarded them to the Controller and Accountant-General’s Department (CAGD) for validation and payment. The development follows a one-month exercise during which the GES received and examined 471 complaints from affected teachers through a Help Desk established at its headquarters on September 8, 2026. In a statement issued on Friday, November 13, the Service said the Help Desk was created to receive individual complaints from teachers recruited in 2024 who had concerns relating to their salaries and to facilitate their prompt resolution. An assessment of the 471 complaints showed that 347 concerned outstanding salary arrears, while the remaining 124 involved teachers who had not been issued Staff IDs. GES said all 347 salary arrears cases had been processed and forwarded to the CAGD for the necessary validation and payment. Regarding the Staff ID complaints, the Service said five of the 124 cases had been successfully processed, with the affected teachers expected to receive their Staff IDs in the coming weeks. However, the remaining 119 cases could not be verified because the individuals had no records in the GES database and their appointment letters could not be authenticated in accordance with due process. The Service disclosed that Regional Directors who had such individuals teaching in their respective regions had already been queried to explain why they were in the classrooms despite the absence of verifiable employment records. GES assured teachers whose cases had been successfully processed that they would receive their appropriate salaries, including any outstanding arrears.

items.description: Conakry, 17 septembre 2026 — Soutra Money annonce l'obtention de la certification PCI DSS de niveau 1, le palier de validation le plus exigeant du référentiel mondial de sécurité des données de paiement. La fintech guinéenne rejoint ainsi le cercle restreint des acteurs africains capables de démontrer, audit à l'appui, un niveau de protection aligné sur les exigences de l'industrie internationale des paiements. Le PCI DSS (Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard) s'applique à toute organisation qui stocke, traite ou transmet des données de paiement. Le niveau 1, réservé aux environnements traitant de très importants volumes de transactions ou présentant des enjeux critiques, impose un audit annuel complet portant sur la sécurisation des systèmes, la protection des données, la gestion des accès, la surveillance continue et les tests réguliers d'intrusion. Cette certification intervient dans un marché guinéen où les paiements digitaux progressent rapidement et où la sécurité devient un critère de choix déterminant pour les particuliers, les commerçants, les entreprises, les banques et les partenaires institutionnels. En élevant son niveau d'exigence, Soutra Money contribue à relever celui du secteur tout entier. Au-delà du marché national, la certification ouvre de nouvelles perspectives de coopération régionale et internationale : elle constitue, pour de nombreux partenaires commerciaux, financiers et technologiques, un préalable à toute intégration de services de paiement à grande échelle. À propos de Soutra Money — Soutra Money est une plateforme guinéenne de services financiers numériques dont la mission est de rendre les paiements plus accessibles, plus sûrs et plus utiles au quotidien. items.title: England’s most capped players in history as Kane sets record [Top 5]
items.description: England captain Harry Kane has become the country’s most-capped men’s footballer of all time after making his 126th international appearance in the Three Lions’ UEFA Nations League clash against Croatia on Thursday. The Bayern Munich striker surpassed former goalkeeper Peter Shilton, who previously held the record with 125 appearances for England between 1970 and 1990. Kane achieved the milestone when he started against Croatia at Wembley Stadium, becoming the first England men’s player to reach 126 senior international caps. The 33-year-old was honoured before kick-off, with Shilton presenting him with a commemorative award, while Prince William handed him a special shirt bearing the number 126. Kane also marked the occasion on the pitch, scoring a penalty in England’s 2-1 victory over Croatia to increase his international goals tally to 92. The striker, who made his England debut against Lithuania in March 2015, already holds the national team’s all-time goalscoring record, having moved past Wayne Rooney’s previous mark of 53 goals in March 2023. The Guardian+2 Here are England’s five most-capped men’s players in history. 1. Harry Kane – 126 appearances Kane sits at the top of England’s all-time appearance chart after overtaking Shilton with his 126th cap against Croatia. Since making his international debut in 2015, the striker has established himself as one of the country’s most influential players, captaining the national team and becoming its leading goalscorer. He won the Golden Boot at the 2018 FIFA World Cup, helping England reach the semi-finals, and subsequently led the Three Lions to the final of Euro 2020 and Euro 2024. His international record includes 92 goals in 126 appearances, making him both England’s most-capped men’s player and its leading goalscorer. 2. Peter Shilton – 125 appearances Former goalkeeper Peter Shilton held England’s appearance record for 36 years before Kane surpassed him. Shilton represented England between 1970 and 1990, accumulating 125 caps during an international career spanning two decades. He featured at three FIFA World Cups, in 1982, 1986 and 1990, as well as the 1984 and 1988 European Championships. The former Nottingham Forest goalkeeper was part of England’s squad that reached the semi-finals of the 1990 World Cup in Italy, where they lost to West Germany on penalties. Shilton also recorded 66 clean sheets for England during his international career. 3. Wayne Rooney – 120 appearances Wayne Rooney occupies third place with 120 appearances for England, having represented the national team between 2003 and 2018. The former Manchester United and Everton forward made his international debut as an 17-year-old against Australia in February 2003. He went on to become one of England’s most important players, scoring 53 goals and holding the national team’s goalscoring record until Kane surpassed him in 2023. Rooney featured in three World Cups and three European Championships during his international career. He also captained England before announcing his retirement from international football in 2017, although he returned for a farewell appearance against the United States in November 2018. 4. David Beckham – 115 appearances Former England captain David Beckham is fourth on the list with 115 international appearances. The former Manchester United and Real Madrid midfielder represented England between 1996 and 2009, scoring 17 goals. Beckham captained the Three Lions 59 times and featured at three World Cups, in 1998, 2002 and 2006, as well as two European Championships. He is particularly remembered for his free-kick against Greece in October 2001, which secured England’s qualification for the 2002 World Cup. Beckham also became the first Englishman to score at three different World Cups, finding the net in the 1998, 2002 and 2006 tournaments. 5. Steven Gerrard – 114 appearances Former Liverpool captain Steven Gerrard completes the top five with 114 appearances for England. Gerrard made his international debut against Ukraine in May 2000 and went on to become one of the country’s leading midfielders. He scored 21 goals for England and represented the national team at six major tournaments, including three World Cups and three European Championships. The former Liverpool midfielder captained England at the 2010 World Cup in South Africa and the 2012 and 2014 European and World Cup tournaments. He announced his retirement from international football following England’s disappointing group-stage exit at the 2014 World Cup in Brazil. Vanguard News The post England’s most capped players in history as Kane sets record [Top 5] appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Minority demands BoG Governor’s appearance over new cedi notes and Theodosia Okoh portrait controversy
items.description: The Minority in Parliament is demanding that the Bank of Ghana Governor appear before Parliament to answer questions over alleged misrepresentations of identities on the newly introduced Heritage Series cedi notes, insisting that the central bank must account for the designs and the process leading to their approval. The caucus has also questioned the absence of parliamentary consultation ahead of the introduction of the new banknotes, saying lawmakers must be given access to the due diligence report detailing how the designs were assessed and approved. Chairman of the NPP Policy Committee and Ranking Member of Parliament’s Economy and Development Committee, Kojo Oppong Nkrumah, made the demand at a press conference on Friday, November 13. He said the Minority had received information that the Bank of Ghana’s board intended to hold an emergency meeting that evening to consider the concerns surrounding the currency designs. “We are hearing, for example, that the bank board wants to meet tonight on an emergency basis to try and respond to those questions”he said. Mr Oppong Nkrumah maintained that the controversy, particularly the questions surrounding the portrait of Ghana’s national flag designer, Theodosia Salome Okoh, required the central bank to provide clear explanations to Parliament. He warned that the Governor and relevant officials would have to appear before the House to respond to the issues raised. “We want to serve notice, and notice is hereby served. They will have to show up before Parliament and answer all of these questions,” he declared. Minority questions identities on new banknotes The Committee Ranking Member questioned how the Bank of Ghana intended to address what the Minority considers misrepresentations of identities on some of the new banknotes. He also raised concerns about the financial implications of correcting the designs, particularly if the affected notes had to be reprinted. “How do they respond to the misrepresentations of identities on the face of some of the notes that they have presented? What will it cost us to reprint those notes on which identities have been misrepresented?” he asked. The concerns come amid public debate over the portrait of Mrs Theodosia Salome Okoh on the new GH¢50 Heritage Series banknote. The Minority wants the central bank to explain the decisions behind the selection and presentation of the personalities featured on the currency, as well as the checks undertaken before the designs were finalised. Parliament to demand due diligence report Beyond the questions surrounding the portraits, Mr Oppong Nkrumah said Parliament would seek a copy of the due diligence report on the new banknote designs. He said lawmakers wanted to establish the individuals responsible for reviewing the designs and those who gave final approval. “Parliament will also be looking for a copy of the due diligence report on the designs and who signed that report,” he stated. Mr Oppong Nkrumah stressed that the caucus was aware of developments surrounding the new currency and would take up the matter in Parliament, although its immediate focus at the press conference was the 2027 Budget. He said the Minority would return to the issue and pursue the explanations it was demanding from the central bank.

items.title: Interior Minister calls for stronger Ghana-Côte d’Ivoire cooperation on border security
items.description: The Minister for Interior, Muntaka Mohammed-Mubarak, has called for stronger security cooperation between Ghana and Côte d’Ivoire to improve border management and address emerging security threats along their shared borders. He made the call during a visit to the Ivorian Sector Commander for Customs, Excise and Special Taxation (CEPS), Adou Tah Felix, at Elubo, as part of his working visit to the Western Region. Mr Muntaka said the two countries shared a long history and strong bonds, making it important for their security agencies to maintain close and cordial relations. He described Ghana and Côte d’Ivoire as essentially one people and stressed the need for sustained cooperation among security personnel operating along their common borders. The Minister said his visit to Elubo was intended to give him first-hand insight into the operations and challenges confronting security personnel, as well as the importance of cross-border collaboration in maintaining peace and security. He commended the Ivorian security authorities for their cooperation, intelligence sharing and willingness to work closely with their Ghanaian counterparts. Mr Muntaka assured the Ivorian Commander of Ghana’s commitment to strengthening the existing partnership and called for closer collaboration to address shared security concerns. For his part, Mr Adou Tah Felix welcomed the Minister and his delegation, describing the visit as an important demonstration of both countries’ commitment to improving cooperation on border security. He reaffirmed his commitment to maintaining cordial relations with Ghanaian security agencies, stressing the need for continued collaboration, information sharing and mutual support to tackle security challenges along the shared border. The Minister wished the Commander and his personnel well and expressed optimism that relations between the two countries would continue to grow stronger.

items.title: Jospong champions solar-powered fleet electrification and subnational climate action in Antalya, Türkiye
items.description: The Jospong Group of Companies (JGC) continues to demonstrate its commitment to Africa’s green transition at the ongoing COP31 in Antalya, Türkiye, highlighting practical solutions for accelerating solar energy deployment, sustainable waste management and carbon neutrality. On Day 4 of the global climate conference, the General Manager of the Jospong Green Transition Office, Dr Ing. Glenn Kwabena Gyimah, participated as a panellist in a high-level session dubbed “The Next Terawatt – Scaling Solar Through Subnational Action”, held at the International Solar Alliance Pavilion (The Solar Hub). The discussion, aligned with COP31’s focus on Clean Energy Transition and Electrification and the Climate Implementation Bridge, explored how partnerships with subnational governments, private sector investment and innovative financing can accelerate solar energy adoption. Sharing Jospong’s experience, Dr Gyimah highlighted the Group’s growing investments in green technologies and its transition towards solar-powered waste management operations. With over 75 companies operating across more than 25 African markets, Jospong operates 36 waste treatment plants and approximately 1,000 waste trucks in Ghana alone. The Group is advancing efforts to transition its diesel-powered fleet to electric vehicles, supported by solar mini-grids, charging stations and energy storage systems. He explained that municipal waste collection fleets provide predictable energy demand, creating opportunities for local governments and private operators to attract investment in solar infrastructure without depending entirely on national electricity grid expansion. Dr Gyimah also highlighted Jospong’s achievements in climate finance, including the Swiss Government’s authorisation secured at COP28 for internationally transferred mitigation outcomes from its composting facilities, with an estimated value of US$20 million by 2030. He emphasised the importance of reinvesting carbon revenues into clean energy infrastructure and community development initiatives, including access to clean water, reforestation and green job creation. The session reinforced Jospong’s position that Africa’s clean energy transition requires more than commitments. It demands bankable projects, credible private sector partnerships, innovative climate financing and practical technologies that deliver measurable environmental and economic benefits. Through its investments in fleet electrification, solar infrastructure, resource recovery, and carbon financing, Jospong is positioning itself as a key private sector partner in advancing Africa’s transition towards a low-carbon, circular economy.

items.title: Mahama opens 6th National Muslim Conference in Accra
items.description: President John Mahama has opened the 6th Annual Conference of the National Muslim Conference of Ghana, calling for continued collaboration among Muslim leaders to promote good governance and national development. The President, who was represented by the Minister for the Interior, Muntaka Mohammed-Mubarak, formally opened the conference at the National Mosque in Kanda, Accra. The conference is being held on the theme, “Towards Promoting Good Governance in Ghana – The Role of the Muslim Community.” President Mahama described the theme as timely, saying governance affects all spheres of life and commended the organisers for creating a platform to examine the Muslim community’s contribution to good governance. He also pledged to seek observer status for Ghana at the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) and pursue membership of the Islamic Development Bank. He said he would seek advice from the Attorney-General and the Minister for Foreign Affairs on granting executive recognition to the National Muslim Conference of Ghana to enable it to obtain at least observer status at the OIC’s annual conferences. According to him, Ghana does not need to be an Islamic country to qualify for membership of the organisation. He said the move would open up economic opportunities for Ghana and improve access to facilities for Muslims undertaking Hajj. The President commended Ghanaian Muslims for their unity, noting that Ahlul Sunnah, Shia, Ahmadiyya and Tijaniyya groups sit together to deliberate on issues of common interest. He described this as a milestone achieved under the leadership of the National Chief Imam and said Muslim leaders across Africa and the world had lessons to learn from Ghana’s experience. President Mahama assured the Muslim community that the government would continue to support the National Chief Imam, leaders of the four main Muslim sects and the Muslim Caucus of Parliament in their efforts to sustain the unity and peaceful coexistence.

Des œuvres de sculpture sur bois, sur os et sur corne, ainsi que des articles de transformation et de confection, témoignent également de la créativité nigérienne. Appréciant cette édition 2026, Sahabi Yagi s’est réjoui de l’engouement des exposants et de l’affluence des visiteurs. Il a invité le public à découvrir les productions artisanales et à soutenir les acteurs du secteur par des achats. Du côté du Mali, la mobilisation est également remarquable avec près de 150 exposants. Sahabi Yagi, président de la Chambre des métiers et de l’artisanat du Niger, a salué l’affluence des visiteurs à la biennale de l’artisanat africain Pour le directeur national de l’artisanat, Daya Niass, cette participation est une occasion de répondre à l’invitation du Burkina Faso, pays frère, et de présenter le savoir-faire malien. Au-delà des ventes, le responsable malien insiste sur les retombées commerciales du SIAO. Il estime que les contacts avec les acheteurs professionnels et la conclusion de partenariats constituent des opportunités essentielles pour accéder aux marchés internationaux. Pour les deux responsables, le SIAO demeure un cadre privilégié de promotion de l’artisanat, de création d’emplois et de lutte contre la pauvreté Hubert BADO

items.title: Surprise! You’re in Congress Now
items.description: Z ack Mullock spent the past nine months campaigning for a U.S. House seat, but never actually pictured himself in Washington as a newly elected member of Congress. Yes, the mayor of Cape May, on the southern tip of New Jersey, believed in his long-shot congressional campaign. But the Democrat never really stopped to think about what would happen if he won. And why would he have? As of late October, political prognosticators still rated the seat he was running for, New Jersey’s Second Congressional District, as safely Republican. After Mullock eked out a shock victory against Representative Jeff Van Drew on November 3, there was a lot to do. For one thing, he had to Google how much members of Congress make ($174,000 a year—more than 10 times what he was paid to serve as mayor). Mullock, a 41-year-old father of three, also had to scramble his travel plans. He had scheduled a vacation for immediately after the election to mark the end of an exhausting stretch for his family. Then someone informed him that he needed to show up at freshman orientation instead. “The first thing I had to tell my kids was, ‘We’re not going to Florida, guys. I’m sorry,’” Mullock told us. Forty-eight hours later, he was on the road to D.C. When we ran into Mullock this past Tuesday outside the Capitol, he had just come from a last-minute shopping trip to Uniqlo, a few blocks away at Union Station. He’d bought a bunch of button-down shirts and crammed them into his messenger bag before running back to pose for a photo with the Blue Dogs, a group of moderate Democrats. He arrived just in time to stand on the outer edge of the crowd, which was clustered around a white 1997 Toyota Land Cruiser that belongs to Marie Gluesenkamp Perez , one of the caucus’s co-chairs. Orientation for incoming members of Congress is a little like the first day of school. Cliques form quickly, helped along by geographical allegiances and ideological affinities. New members—young firebrands and 60-somethings making a major career pivot—jockey over where to sit. Looking the part—which could mean a crisp suit or a trucker hat and cowboy boots, depending on where you’re from—can’t hurt. “It really hadn’t sunk in until I first walked onto the House floor,” J. D. Ford, an Indiana state senator who ousted a Republican who’d won by nearly 19 points two years ago, told us. Every new member we spoke with was adamant that they had thought they could win, even if few other people within the Democratic Party establishment had agreed. Many, though, had not allowed themselves the luxury of picturing what a victory would bring, because most of them had organized their life around a single date: November 3, Election Day. But so far 15 Democrats have flipped House seats in districts that President Trump carried by double digits just two years earlier. Suddenly it was November 4, and their victories had been confirmed, against all odds. Their first task was to figure out how to get to D.C. for orientation—a few days of glitzy receptions, serious meetings, and mundane onboarding tasks. (Even members of Congress need to figure out their health plan.) “I knew that we could win. I didn’t know that we would win,” said Paul Barringer, who flipped a North Carolina district that President Trump had won in 2024 by nearly 17 points. Barringer, who lives on a tree farm in Sanford, told us he was exercising in the dark on Election Night when he heard whooping coming from near his house. He thought it was coyotes. In reality, it was his family and friends running out to tell him he’d won. About 150 miles to the northwest, Chuck Hubbard was walking back to his car close to 1 a.m. when the doors of the watch party he’d left burst open and his supporters streamed out, shouting that he was ahead of longtime Republican Representative Virginia Foxx by just 99 votes. The race for a seat that had once been thought to be firmly in Foxx’s hands is not yet called, but Hubbard now leads by 335 votes. He showed up in Washington just in case he wins. “Isn’t it strange for someone who’s 64 years old to be going to freshman orientation?” Hubbard asked us. There were other surprise winners from North Carolina, where aggressive Republican gerrymandering backfired and became a textbook “dummymander”—when districts drawn to favor the GOP unexpectedly fall into Democratic hands. Cyril Jefferson bested Representative Addison McDowell in a district that was so heavily gerrymandered to favor Republicans in 2023 that a Democrat didn’t even bother running the following year. The Cook Political Report rated the race “Solid Republican”—meaning it was not considered competitive—and Jefferson was outraised 6 to 1. He won by a solid two-point margin. The 34-year-old mayor of High Point said he got into the race not because he thought he could win, but because he felt it was what his district needed. “You see a district like that, you never want to assume, Oh, we can win this ,” Jefferson told us. He said he’d repeatedly contacted national Democrats while campaigning but didn’t garner much support. “After I won, they all reached out and said, Hey, we were wrong .” Others won with virtually no money. LaKesha Womack brought in just $59,000 through mid-October, while her Republican opponent raised more than $2 million. She spent most of her time out in her district, which includes part of Charlotte. Womack faces a wrinkle in acclimating to the new job: Before taking office in January, she will be in court, making her first appearance next month on a felony charge that she allegedly failed to return a rented Toyota Corolla in 2019. (Womack told us she could not comment on the pending case, but suggested the timing was suspicious. She was served a criminal summons at an October campaign rally, seven years after the alleged incident; Womack has previously said she did not know a charge had been filed against her, because she was homeless at the time.) [ Read: The unlikeliest Democratic win of all ] L ike first-year college students , freshmen members of Congress have to set up a whole new life for themselves. One of the first tasks is navigating D.C.’s rental market. “Everyone from across the aisle had told me it’s not a good idea to live in your office, something I didn’t even know people did,” said Katy Padilla Stout, who won a seat in Texas’s Twenty-Third Congressional District, which Trump won in 2024 by 15 points. Angela Gonzales-Torres, a California Democrat, has tasked her partner with the apartment hunt because she has too much to do, a list that includes hiring more than a dozen staffers, attending IT trainings (those exist in Congress too), and going to caucus meetings. “I don’t know if I’m excited to have two different landlords or apartments to keep up,” the 31-year-old Gonzales-Torres told us in a phone call as she waited for the bus to orientation. She placed second in California’s nonpartisan primary for a Los Angeles–area House seat in June, so her victory—against a member of her own party, who has a history of fending off challenges from his left—was unexpected. After chatting with a group of Democrats who are at the end of their first term and who share an apartment, she is now considering living with roommates in D.C. For the more than 75 new Democrats who will be sworn in on the floor of the U.S. House in January, this moment—the rush to staff offices, the chaos of learning to get around Washington, and the idealism and excitement of thinking about how to govern before the messy reality of partisan politics kicks in—is a high point after a year of campaigning. But for Fred Wellman, it might not be the most important thing he does this year. Wellman, who won a Missouri district that hasn’t been represented by a Democrat in more than 30 years, is getting married during the week of Christmas. When he got engaged to Heather Schaefer in 2024, Wellman, who is 61, wasn’t even thinking about running for Congress. That decision came more than a year later. The wedding would have to wait until after the election. “I just thought, Let’s just go through the rough-and-tumble of the campaign and let her have her privacy. And then once it’s over, we’ll figure it out ,” Wellman told us in a congressional office building on Tuesday. He had stepped out of the committee room where the new Democrats were getting to know one another, and Representative Emanuel Cleaver, an 11-term lawmaker from Kansas City, had just introduced Wellman to the Democratic Caucus. “Well, it’s over, and we won. So now we’re gonna go ahead and seal the deal,” Wellman said. The new members—both those who expected to be here and those who are still pinching themselves—said they’re eager to get to work. Wellman wants to see Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth investigated . Hubbard, the North Carolina Democrat leading by 335 votes, said Democrats are ready to “start correcting some things.” But first, they all need to find a place to sleep. And buy some new clothes. *Illustration sources: Aaron Schwartz / Getty; Allison Robbert / AP; Andrew Harnik / Getty; Annabelle Gordon / Reuters; Daniel Heuer / Bloomberg / Getty.

items.title: Ghana-Canada strengthens economic partnership as bilateral trade rises 56% to $752m in 2025
items.description: Ghana and Canada are seeking to deepen their economic partnership and expand investment opportunities following a 56 per cent increase in bilateral trade, which reached US$752 million in 2025. Deputy Minister for Trade, Agribusiness and Industry Sampson Ahi disclosed the trade figures at a meeting in Accra on Thursday, November 12, 2026, involving Canada’s Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs, Arun Tjangaraj, and the Canadian High Commissioner to Ghana, Myriam Montrat. He said bilateral trade had risen from US$483 million in 2024 to US$752 million in 2025, describing the growth as a reflection of increasing confidence, economic complementarity and expanding commercial opportunities between the two countries. Mr Ahi described Canada as a longstanding and trusted partner, noting that Ghana and Canada would celebrate 70 years of diplomatic relations in 2027. He identified agribusiness and agro-processing, pharmaceuticals, textiles and garments, renewable energy, clean technology, critical minerals, railway infrastructure, digital technology and artificial intelligence as priority areas offering significant opportunities for Canadian investment. Canada’s Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs, Arun Tjangaraj, reiterated his country’s commitment to building a genuine economic partnership with Ghana. He highlighted the considerable opportunities available to strengthen bilateral relations and support Ghana’s economic transformation. The meeting reaffirmed both countries’ commitment to deepening cooperation in trade, investment, industrial development and private-sector collaboration. The Chief Executive Officer of the Ghana Investment Promotion Authority (GIPA), Simon Madjie, also spoke about doing business in Ghana, government reforms and initiatives to attract investment.

items.title: Malawi endorses Jospong waste management investment at COP31
items.description: Malawi has approved a proposal allowing Ghana’s Jospong Group of Companies (JGC) to undertake a feasibility study for the establishment of integrated waste management facilities in the country, marking a major step towards a potential partnership between the two parties. Dr Misheard Yagontha Munthali, Principal Secretary at Malawi’s Ministry of Natural Resources, disclosed this during an interaction with the media on the sidelines of COP31 in Antalya, Türkiye. He said the approval by the Public-Private Partnership Commission Board had cleared the way for the next stage of discussions. Speaking on behalf of the Minister of Natural Resources, Patricia Wiskes, he explained that the proposed collaboration followed visits by a Malawian delegation to Ghana, where it engaged Jospong and signed a memorandum of understanding outlining areas of cooperation. Dr Munthali said the feasibility study would help determine the scope and requirements for establishing the facilities. “I am glad to report that last week the Board was able to meet and has fully approved that Jospong can now come and do a full feasibility study of their operations in Malawi,” he said. He added that Jospong was expected to arrange a date with the Ministry for the formal issuance of a letter authorising the study. The initial proposal is to explore opportunities in four city councils: Lilongwe, Blantyre, Zomba and Mzuzu, before considering possible expansion to 28 district councils. Dr Munthali said the feasibility study would guide both parties on suitable locations, investment requirements and the next steps towards establishing the integrated waste management facilities. He described the approval as a breakthrough, adding that Malawi was eager to move quickly towards the proposed partnership. Waste as an economic opportunity The Principal Secretary said the visit to Jospong’s operations in Ghana had changed the delegation’s perception of waste management, shifting its focus from viewing waste as an environmental nuisance to recognising its potential as an economic resource. “For a long time, we used to look at waste as something bad or a nuisance or a problem. But when we visited Jospong, we realised that actually waste is a big economic opportunity,” he stated. He noted that waste processing could generate useful products and resources while improving sanitation and creating employment opportunities. According to him, the proposed partnership could support cleaner cities, create jobs for young people and open up economic opportunities for women and other groups. Dr Munthali said Malawi was particularly interested in learning how waste could be converted into products such as fuel, gas and other materials. Local businesses to remain involved. Responding to concerns about how foreign investment could crowd out local stakeholders, Minister of Natural Resources Patricia Wiskes stressed that the proposed arrangement was not intended to displace local waste management operators and small-scale businesses. Patricia Wiskes, MP and Minister of Natural Resources, Malawi. She said the government and Jospong had discussed a model under which existing local operators would continue collecting waste from communities and transporting it to designated facilities for further processing and management. “Our agreement with Jospong is that we are actually not going to push these small-scale business people out of business, but we’ll find a way to coordinate with them,” she said. Under the proposed arrangement, Jospong would concentrate largely on managing waste at designated sites, while local businesses and existing operators would retain responsibility for waste collection within the cities. Ms Wiskes said effective coordination would be necessary to ensure a steady supply of waste to the facilities and protect the interests of all parties. She added that the feasibility study would identify operational gaps and help determine how local businesses could be involved in discussions on the partnership. Skills transfer and carbon credits Tawonga Mbale-Luka, Director of Environmental Affairs, said Malawi expected foreign investors to work with local partners to strengthen domestic capacity. She noted that such collaboration would promote the transfer of knowledge and technical skills, ensuring that local businesses and the country benefited from the investment. Ms Wiskes also said Malawi was interested in exploring opportunities to generate carbon credits from waste management, drawing on Jospong’s experience in developing carbon projects. She further highlighted the Group’s experience in rehabilitating landfill sites for alternative community uses, including converting overused landfill areas into community parks. “We also want to learn how we can create the same with some landfills that are overused. Maybe we can also remodel them to become a community park,” she said. The proposed feasibility study is expected to provide the basis for a roadmap outlining the investment, operational arrangements and potential expansion of integrated waste management facilities in Malawi.

items.title: DGE : Mohamed Ali Condé prend fonction et promet de relever le défi sans improvisation
items.description: Nommé le 9 novembre dernier par décret présidentiel, Mohamed Ali Condé a officiellement pris fonction ce vendredi 13 novembre 2026 en qualité de directeur général des élections (DGE). La cérémonie d'installation s'est déroulée dans les locaux de l'institution, en présence de plusieurs cadres de l'administration publique, de représentants d'institutions républicaines et d'acteurs du processus électoral. Elle a été présidée par la ministre de l'Administration du territoire et de la Décentralisation, Djénabou Touré, qui a elle-même dirigé la DGE avant son entrée au gouvernement. À cette occasion, elle a prodigué plusieurs conseils à son successeur, tout en le mettant en garde contre les nombreuses pressions auxquelles il sera confronté dans l'exercice de ses fonctions. « C'est un travail sous pression », a-t-elle prévenu, évoquant les sollicitations internes, les attentes des candidats, les exigences des autorités, les réactions de la population ainsi que la vigilance des médias. Elle a particulièrement insisté sur la nécessité de maintenir un dialogue permanent avec la presse et les organisations de la société civile. « Vous devez travailler avec toutes ces parties prenantes, surtout la presse, travailler main dans la main avec elle, avec la société civile et les plateformes », a conseillé la ministre au nouveau patron de la DGE. Djénabou Touré a également exhorté Mohamed Ali Condé à faire preuve d'impartialité, à préserver la cohésion au sein de son équipe et à privilégier le mérite dans la gestion de ses collaborateurs. « Ne constituez pas de clan au sein de votre direction. Travaillez avec tout le monde et, par le mérite, essayez d'encourager tous ceux qui peuvent apporter leur contribution », a-t-elle recommandé. Abordant le calendrier électoral, la ministre a rappelé les prochaines échéances, notamment les élections régionales du 29 novembre et les sénatoriales du 20 décembre 2026. Elle a également annoncé d'autres scrutins complémentaires attendus l'année prochaine, en lien avec le nouveau découpage administratif et la création de nouvelles communes et préfectures. Prenant à son tour la parole, Mohamed Ali Condé a exprimé sa gratitude au président de la République, Mamadi Doumbouya, pour la confiance placée en lui. Il a toutefois tenu à souligner que cette nomination représente avant tout une responsabilité au service de la nation. « Cette nomination n'est pas simplement une promotion personnelle. Elle constitue avant tout un appel à servir davantage la nation, à répondre aux attentes des citoyens et à contribuer, avec loyauté et détermination, à la consolidation des institutions de notre pays », a-t-il déclaré. Mesurant l'ampleur de la mission qui lui est confiée, le nouveau directeur général a réaffirmé son engagement à œuvrer pour l'organisation d'élections « crédibles, transparentes, inclusives, apaisées et conformes aux textes en vigueur ». Face aux échéances qui se profilent, il entend miser sur l'anticipation, la planification, la coordination et le contrôle rigoureux de chaque étape du processus électoral. « Nous n'avons pas le droit à l'improvisation », a-t-il martelé, résumant ainsi les exigences qu'il entend imposer à la conduite de sa mission. Dans un souci de continuité, Mohamed Ali Condé a également tendu la main aux cadres et agents de l'institution, les invitant à poursuivre les efforts déjà engagés dans un esprit de cohésion et de collaboration. Il a notamment écarté toute volonté de remettre en cause les acquis de la DGE. « Je ne viens pas bouleverser le travail accompli, encore moins remettre en cause les compétences existantes. Je viens m'inscrire dans une dynamique de continuité, de consolidation et de performance », a-t-il assuré. Il s'est par ailleurs engagé à rester ouvert aux initiatives et aux propositions constructives de ses collaborateurs, tout en attendant d'eux « de la loyauté institutionnelle, de la discipline, de la rigueur, de l'intégrité, du professionnalisme et surtout des résultats ». En prenant les commandes de la Direction générale des élections, Mohamed Ali Condé hérite d'une institution stratégique, appelée à jouer un rôle déterminant dans la mise en œuvre du calendrier électoral de 2026. Son premier grand défi sera de conduire les élections régionales et sénatoriales dans les délais annoncés et dans un climat apaisé.

items.title: A Taƙaice: Makamashi, Ilimi, Noma… Muhimman labaran mako
items.description: Litinin 9 ga Nuwamba, 2026 Kiwon Dabbobi: Gangamin Wayar da Kai Kan Abincin Dabbobi da Ba a Bincika Ingancinsa Ba Fiye da makonni biyu kenan da wata tawaga daga ma'aikatar Kiwon Dabbobi ke zagayen sassa daban-daban na Nijar, domin wayar da kan jama'a kan haɗarin amfani da abincin dabbobi da ba a bincika ingancinsa ba. A ziyarar da tawagar ta kai yankin Agadez, Dokta Fati Soumana, shugabar sashen kula da ingancin kayayyaki a hukumar kula da ayyukan likitancin dabbobi, ta yi ƙarin bayani kan wannan gangami. SIAO 2026: Nijar Ta Lashe Babbar Kyautar Rumfar Baje Koli Mafi Kyau An kammala bikin baje kolin sana'o'in hannu na ƙasa da ƙasa na Ouagadougou, SIAO 2026, karo na 18, a ranar Asabar 7 ga Nuwamba. Nijar ta lashe babbar kyautar shugaban ƙasar Burkina Faso, wadda ake bai wa ƙasar da ta fi tsara rumfar baje kolinta. Mali ta zo ta biyu, yayin da Burkina Faso ta zo ta uku. Dokta Ousmane Bougouma, shugaban majalisar dokokin jama'a, wanda ya jagoranci bikin rufe taron, ya bayyana ra'ayinsa kan wannan biki a cikin bayanan da Radiodiffusion Television du Burkina, RTB, ta tattara. Talata 10 ga Nuwamba, 2026 2026 Tillaberi: An Tsayar da 15 ga Disamba a Matsayin Ranar 'Yantar da Gonaki A yankin Tillaberi, an tsayar da ranar 15 ga Disamba 2026 a matsayin ranar 'yantar da gonaki. Gwamnan yankin ne ya ɗauki wannan mataki a ranar 9 ga Nuwamba, bayan wani taron shawarwari. A cewar bayanan da aka bayar, matakin na da nufin hana rikice-rikice tsakanin manoma da makiyaya, kare amfanin gona da kuma sauƙaƙa wa makiyaya samun wuraren kiwo. Hukumomin yankin sun yi kira da a yaɗa wannan sanarwa ga dukkan jama'ar da abin ya shafa. Niamey: Ana Ci Gaba da Makon Masu Aikin Notaire Karo na Shida Ana gudanar da makon masu aikin notaire karo na shida daga ranar 9 zuwa 12 ga Nuwamba a Niamey. Ƙungiyar Chambre nationale des notaires du Niger ce ta shirya wannan taro, domin ƙara wayar da kan jama'a game da rawar da masu aikin notaire ke takawa da kuma ayyukan da suke yi wa al'umma. Maître Kane Dan Baou Mamane Siraji, mai aikin notaire a Niamey, ya yi ƙarin bayani kan wannan taro. Laraba 11 ga Nuwamba, 2026 Nijar: An Gano Kusan Sabbin Masu Cutar Kuturta 200 Tun Farkon Shekara A Nijar, an gano kusan sabbin masu cutar kuturta 200 tun daga watan Janairun 2026, a cewar shirin TLM na yaƙi da cutar. An gabatar da wannan rahoto ne a taron shekara-shekara na tantance ayyukan shirin, wanda aka gudanar a ranakun 10 da 11 ga Nuwamba a Maradi. Dokta Raïssa Lompo, mai kula da shirin lafiya da sa ido da tantance ayyuka, ta yi ƙarin bayani kan wannan batu. Rijiyar Mai ta Goumeri W-8: Gwamnati Ta Sanar da Tsayawar Fitar Mai Gwamnatin Nijar ta sanar a ranar 10 ga Nuwamba cewa fitar mai ba tare da kulawa ba daga rijiyar Goumeri W-8, wadda ta fara tun ranar 25 ga Satumba, ta tsaya. A cewar sanarwar haɗin gwiwa ta ma'aikatun Man Fetur da Muhalli, fitar man ta tsaya ne ranar 20 ga Oktoba, da misalin ƙarfe bakwai na safe, kuma har zuwa lokacin sanarwar ba a sake samun fitar man ba. Sai dai ana ci gaba da ayyukan tabbatar da tsaron wurin. A ɓangaren muhalli kuma, wata tawagar ƙwararrun Nijar ta kammala tattara samfuran da za a bincika, inda ake jiran bayyana sakamakon gwaje-gwajen ga jama'a. A halin yanzu, gwamnati ta buƙaci makiyaya su nisantar da dabbobinsu daga yankin da abin ya shafa, tare da sanar da hukumomin yankin duk wani abin da suka lura da shi. Alhamis 12 ga Nuwamba, 2026 AES: Ministocin Ilimi Na Neman Daidaita Tsarin Makarantu na Ƙasashe Uku Ministocin da ke kula da ilimi na ƙasashen Burkina Faso, Mali da Nijar sun gudanar da taro a ranakun 10 da 11 ga Nuwamba a Niamey. Bayan kammala taron, ministocin sun gabatar da wasu muhimman shawarwari da ke da nufin kusantar da tsarin makarantu na ƙasashe ukun da ke cikin ƙungiyar ƙasashen Sahel, AES. Ismail Hassane zai kawo ƙarin bayani kan wannan taro. Sana'o'in Hannu: Wani Bincike Ya Nuna Gudunmawar Kashi 18 Cikin Ɗari ga Tattalin Arzikin Nijar An gabatar da sakamakon wani bincike na ƙasa kan sana'o'in hannu a ranar Talata 10 ga Nuwamba, a wani biki da ministar Yawon Buɗe Ido da Sana'o'in Hannu ta jagoranta. A cewar sakamakon binciken, ɓangaren sana'o'in hannu na bayar da gudunmawar kashi 18 cikin ɗari ga jimillar arzikin da ƙasar ke samarwa, wato PIB, da darajar fiye da biliyan 3,774 na CFA. Haka kuma, an ƙididdige kusan masu sana'o'in hannu miliyan uku. A cewar ministar, wannan bincike wani mataki ne a cikin ƙoƙarin inganta tsarin gudanarwa da kuma ƙara darajar sana'o'in hannu a Nijar. Juma'a 13 ga Nuwamba, 2026 Zinder: 'Yan Sanda Sun Sanar da Kama Wasu Mutane da Ake Zargin Suna Cikin Ƙungiyoyin Aikata Laifuka Biyu A Zinder, hukumar 'yan sandan binciken manyan laifuka ta yankin ta sanar da kama wasu mutane da ake zargin suna cikin ƙungiyoyin aikata laifuka guda biyu. A cewar bayanan da 'yan sanda suka bayar, ana zargin ƙungiya ta farko da mallaka da kuma yaɗa takardun kuɗi na jabu, yayin da ake zargin ƙungiya ta biyu da aikata zamba ta hanyar intanet. Maman Djamilou Warssou, jami'in 'yan sandan binciken laifuka a Zinder, ya yi ƙarin bayani kan wannan batu. Mayahi: An Shirya Gangamin Wayar da Kai a Cikin Bikin FEGALMA A Mayahi, cikin yankin Maradi, an shirya wani gangamin wayar da kan jama'a a gidan matasa na Dan Anko, a cikin ayyukan bikin al'adu na FEGALMA. Jafarou Malan Kossaou, wanda ya ƙaddamar da wannan bikin al'adu, ya yi ƙarin bayani kan manufofin gangamin.

items.title: Macenta : un garçon de 8 ans retrouvé mort, sa mère et plusieurs autres personnes interpellées (procureur)
items.description: Un drame secoue le district de Sédimaï, dans la commune rurale d’Orémaï, préfecture de Macenta. Jacques Pamavogui, un garçon de 8 ans, élève en deuxième année du primaire, a été retrouvé mort dans des circonstances troublantes le vendredi 6 novembre 2026. Sa mère biologique et plusieurs autres personnes ont été interpellées dans le cadre de l’enquête, selon une déclaration du procureur de la République près le tribunal de première instance de Macenta, dont Mediaguinee détient copie. D’après cette déclaration, l’enfant a été découvert ligoté dans une bassine déposée devant une concession. À la suite de la découverte du corps, une enquête de flagrance a été ouverte et confiée à la police judiciaire de la gendarmerie territoriale de Macenta. Plusieurs personnes, dont la mère biologique de la victime, ont été interpellées et placées en garde à vue. Le procureur précise également que des examens médico-légaux sont en cours afin de déterminer les causes exactes et les circonstances du décès. Dans sa déclaration, le magistrat réaffirme la détermination de la justice à faire toute la lumière sur cette affaire. Il appelle les populations au calme et invite les médias ainsi que les citoyens à éviter les rumeurs et les spéculations, dans le strict respect du principe de la présomption d’innocence. Amara Souza Soumaoro, correspondant à N’Zérékoré. L’article Macenta : un garçon de 8 ans retrouvé mort, sa mère et plusieurs autres personnes interpellées (procureur) est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: Kloto : le ministre Tessi s’assure de l’effectivité de la rentrée académique à l’ENAM et l’ENSF de Kpalimé
items.description: Kpalimé, 13 nov. (ATOP) – Le ministre en charge de la Santé, Jean-Marie Tessi, a effectué, le jeudi 12 novembre, une visite à l’Ecole nationale des auxiliaires médicaux (ENAM) et à l’Ecole nationale des sages-femmes (ENSF) de Kpalimé pour de la rentrée académique 2026-2027. Par cette visite, le ministre entend s’enquérir des conditions d’apprentissage, apprécier les équipements pédagogiques et d’évaluer les efforts consentis par les équipes administratives et pédagogiques. Il s’est agi également d’échanger avec les apprenants et de leur rappeler les exigences de leurs futures professions, notamment la compétence, la discipline, le dévouement, l’éthique et le sens des responsabilités. Le ministre leur a transmis les orientations du Président du Conseil relatives à l’amélioration de la qualité des soins et au renforcement de l’accueil des patients dans les formations sanitaires. Il les a invités à faire de ces valeurs des principes fondamentaux de leur future pratique professionnelle. A l’occasion, des équipements destinés à soutenir les deux établissements dans leurs missions pédagogiques ont été remis. Il s’agit notamment d’un bus et du matériel didactique et informatique comprenant des ordinateurs, des photocopieurs, des imprimantes et divers équipements de santé. Cette dotation, contribuera à améliorer les conditions de formation et d’apprentissage, faciliter les déplacements des apprenants dans le cadre des stages pratiques et des travaux de terrain. L’ENAM et l’ENSF de Kpalimé ont été créées en octobre 2018. Elles forment des infirmiers diplômés d’Etat et des sages-femmes. ATOP/KAT/BA/BV

items.title: Pakistan aiming to become competitive destination for long-term investment, CDF Munir tells minerals moot
items.description: Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir said on Friday that Pakistan was aiming to become a competitive destination for long-term mineral investment. He made the remarks while addressing the participants of the Pakistan Minerals Investment Forum 2026 in Islamabad, according to state-run Radio Pakistan . Delegations, exhibitors and attendees have arrived from across the world to attend the event. As the two-day event opened on Thursday, Pakistan showcased its vast mineral resources, ranging from coal and salt to gold and critical minerals, to attract international investment, promising predictable, investor-friendly policies, institutional support and security. On Friday, CDF Munir said all possible measures were being taken to ensure the security of the entire mining ecosystem. He said mines and miners, investments, industries, projects and all associated people would be provided adequate protection, the Radio Pakistan report said. He added that harnessing Pakistan’s mineral wealth was a collective national objective. He also emphasised that the country’s goal was not merely to export raw materials but to develop the entire value chain, including refining and manufacturing, it added. CDF Munir also said that Pakistan sought to foster long-term partnerships that created sustainable economic value for the country and its partners. “He stressed that mineral development must benefit local communities, adding that people living in mineral-rich areas should witness tangible improvements in their lives,” the report said. He also emphasised that Pakistan must move from potential to productivity, from promises to action and from raw exports to value-added growth. PM expresses hope for Pakistan’s economy Addressing the same event, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif expressed the hope that Pakistan could become the world’s sixth-largest economy “earlier than 2050”. In his remarks, he recalled a Goldman Sachs assessment , which had projected Pakistan to become the sixth-largest economy in the world by 2075 and said: “I would like to make a small amendment here — instead of 2075, it will be earlier than 2050.” He commended the hard work of the petroleum minister in organising the forum and specially acknowledged CDF Munir and his team, saying that his invaluable support and untiring efforts had “placed Pakistan’s mines and minerals agenda at the heart of our economic vision”. The premier highlighted that the production of copper and gold at Reko Diq on the Tethyan copper belt was expected to commence in 2028 after having stalled for about two decades. He renewed a commitment he made at last year’s forum to end the practice of shipping Pakistan’s minerals out of the country in raw form, saying, “That day is not far away when this will come to a grinding halt.” Instead of simply extracting and exporting raw minerals, he expressed his desire for Reko Diq and every project along the Tethyan belt to establish “refineries, smelters, cable and conductor factories — the industries that will connect Pakistan with the rest of the world”. He called on the investors present to “mine in Pakistan, process in Pakistan, manufacture in Pakistan, and then export to the rest of the world”, terming it a “win-win partnership” for everyone. Regarding Pakistan’s efforts to meet investor expectations, PM Shehbaz highlighted that the country was simplifying procedures, “eliminating red tape, cutting inordinate delays and ensuring complete transparency in awarding licences and contracts”. He added that through digitisation of records and the National Minerals Data Centre, investors would be able to know what was beneath the ground before committing “a single dime or yuan” to projects. The prime minister stressed that the federal and provincial governments would work in a unified fashion to provide “all necessary support” to investors to promote their business in the country. He acknowledged that the safety and protection of manpower, assets and supply routes was “the paramount responsibility” of the government and expressed his commitment to fulfilling it. “Your safety is our safety and your protection is our protection.” PM Shehbaz underscored the need for the cooperation of local communities as well as the availability of reliable infrastructure, power, water, roads, rail and communications to help investments thrive. He also declared, “If any file gets stuck due to bureaucratic delays or cumbersome procedures, bring it straight to me. I will personally ensure that it moves at lightning speed.” The premier highlighted the country’s youth population as its “real wealth”. He urged investors to build skilled training centres and vocational institutes so that these young people could become skilled professionals, innovators and entrepreneurs. “Every investment in mining must translate into local jobs, local businesses, local contractors; into schools, clinics, clean drinking water, and above all for a better life for the communities where these investments are being undertaken,” he stressed. He added that his government and the provinces would work alongside the investors to ensure that those living nearest to these sites would be the main beneficiaries of these economic activities. The premier also underscored the need for responsible mining in line with international standards, saying that “development and environmental protection must go hand in hand”. He said the mining projects would be carried out with “state-of-the-art” technology while protecting Pakistan’s water, land and the health and safety of workers. In this regard, he said, he had directed “every relevant ministry and department” to provide a responsible point of contact to investors with the authority to resolve their issues without any delay, enabling speedy implementation of their plans. He reiterated that the government and all institutions “will stand with you like a rock at every step”, inviting investors to visit Pakistan and promising that “we will roll out the red carpet for you”. “Together, we will turn Pakistan’s mineral wealth into mutually beneficial economic cooperation, industrial growth and shared prosperity,” he said. ‘Mineral exploration increasingly focused on strategic resources’ Earlier in the day, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik addressed the forum and stated that Pakistan’s exploration efforts were increasingly focused on minerals that were of strategic importance to global investors. In continuation of the pitch, Malik told the investors that Pakistan’s exploration efforts were being complemented with “modern geochemical and geophysical surveys, exploratory drilling, and upgrading of our geoscience advanced research laboratories with sophisticated analytical technologies”. Here, he particularly mentioned the exploration of copper and gold in Chagai and western Balochistan to lithium, tin and tungsten in Gilgit-Baltistan and antimony and base metals in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. He said Pakistan had been exporting raw ore and importing the finished products to meet its requirements for a long time. “We are now advancing copper smelting to capture more of the value chain from the mine to the finished metal,” he added. The minister said Pakistan was also strengthening the scientific foundation of its mineral sector through the Geological Survey of Pakistan. “The government’s accelerated geological mapping programme, including detailed surveys at a scale of 1:50,000, is helping identify mineral prospects across the country.” The minister further said that through international technical cooperation, including the UK Pakistan Geoscience Capacity Building Programme, “we are strengthening expertise in digital mapping, airborne surveys and mineral assessment”. “We are also digitising decades of geological information to give investors greater access to reliable data, reduce exploration uncertainty, and enable informed investment decisions,” he continued. The petroleum minister highlighted that discovering a mineral deposit was only the initial stage and a commercially viable mine required electricity, water, roads, railways and access to international markets. “That is why infrastructure development is aligned with our mineral ambitions,” he explained. In this context, he described the planned upgrade of the Rohri-Nokundi railway corridor, connectivity to Port Qasim and the development of supporting infrastructure around Reko Diq as “important steps” towards connecting Pakistan’s mineral-rich regions with the global markets. He said, “Our objective is very clear: to build not just individual mines, but an integrated, competitive and sustainable mineral industry. “Where it is commercially and technically viable, we want investment to support processing, refining, downstream industry, technology transfer and integration into the global value chains. “We want this industry to build Pakistani capability as it grows through technical skills, vocational training, engineering services, a stronger base for Pakistani suppliers and real career opportunities for young people, including women entering the sector for the first time.” But, he contended, none of this would hold together without the communities in our producing regions. “Projects that earn the trust of the communities around them are, in our experience, the projects that actually get built and sustained.”

items.title: Tensión entre Martín Caparrós y una portavoz de Vox en un acto sobre la ELA en el Congreso: “No sabía que venían xenófobos, no habría venido”
items.description: Se ha vivido un momento de tensión inesperada este viernes al mediodía en el Congreso de los Diputados, en un evento para celebrar dos años de la Ley ELA. Tras la presentación del último informe de la asociación ConELA, varios representantes de los partidos han debatido sobre el estado de la norma. Entre ellos ha intervenido María Ruiz, de Vox, miembro del Comité Ejecutivo Nacional del partido, que ha puesto sobre la mesa la cuestión de la prioridad nacional: “Lo verdaderamente justo y solidario entre los españoles es que son quienes deben tener preferencia en su propia tierra”. La reacción de Martín Caparrós, reconocido escritor argentino y columnista de EL PAÍS, también paciente de ELA , ha sido inmediata: alzar la voz desde su silla, aunque no participaba en esa mesa. “¿De verdad está diciendo eso? No sabía que venían xenófobos aquí, si no, no habría venido”. Ruiz ha defendido su postura asegurando que en su partido “no odian al extranjero, aman a los españoles”. Caparrós ha respondido con ironía y dureza: “Los aman tanto que los quieren matar a todos”. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Las seis horas de Jordi Wild con Sánchez, Feijóo, Colau (y el Fary) en su casa: “Esto es una vez en la vida”
items.description: Y al fin llegó el día. La primera charla, con la candidata del Frente Amplio, se ha publicado en su canal de YouTube a las 8.00. La segunda, con el líder del PP, a las 10.00. Y la del presidente del Gobierno, a las 12.00.
